sections.heading: Topic 1: SC seeks clarity on FSSAI front-of-pack warning labels
sections.content:
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260911-01`  
> **GS Paper:** **GS-II** (judiciary, public health regulation) + **GS-III** (food safety, packaged food)

sections.heading: 1. What is in the news
sections.content:
The **Supreme Court** on **Thursday (10 September 2026)** questioned the **Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)** on how it would decide that a packaged food is **“high”** in **sugar, salt or fat** for its proposed **front-of-pack warning labels (FoPL)**. Food safety, the Bench said, is a cause of **“national interest.”**

**Bench:** Justices **J.B. Pardiwala** and **K. Vinod Chandran**.

**Matter:** public-interest litigation by non-profits (**3S** and **Our Health Society**; advocate **Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi** in the same day’s Hindu) seeking **mandatory** front-of-pack warnings on packaged foods high in sugar, salt and saturated fats.

**Appearing for Centre + FSSAI:** **Additional Solicitor-General (ASG) Brijender Chahar**.

sections.heading: 2. What FSSAI proposed (affidavit)
sections.content:
| Lock | Class / clip line |
|:---|:---|
| Shape / colour | **Red hexagonal** warning on the **front** of the pack |
| Words | **“HIGH FAT” / “HIGH SUGAR” / “HIGH SALT”** (and, in the proposal, **“HIGHLY SWEETENED BEVERAGE”** where it applies) |
| Trigger (first design) | Product **high in two or more** nutrients of concern — **fat, sugar or salt** |
| Thresholds | **Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024**, issued by the **Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) – National Institute of Nutrition (NIN)** |
| Last month | FSSAI proposed **prominent red** warning labels — the paper calls this a **regulatory U-turn** |

The Court asked the obvious Prelims trap: if you say **high in salt / high in sugar / high in sodium**, **have you laid down guidelines** for the cut-off? It also asked whether FSSAI was adhering to the **ICMR–NIN** guidelines.

Justice Pardiwala (clip): **“We are concerned with the health of people, particularly growing children.”** Take the Court’s orders **seriously**. Homework and study have been done; **cooperation** is expected in a **national-interest** cause.

sections.heading: 3. Same day’s written order (same reporter — do not skip)
sections.content:
After the hearing the Bench’s order (Thursday night) put a **two-phase** FoPL rollout under the scanner.

- **Phase 1 (FSSAI design):** warning if **two or more** nutrients of concern are high.  
- **Phase 2:** extend to products high in **even one**.  
- FSSAI’s reason: time for consumers to adapt and for industry to **reformulate**.  
- **SC:** consumer acceptability / industry time **cannot** leave Phase 2 **indefinitely postponed**. Need a **reasonable, scientifically justified, clearly defined** timeline between the two phases.

**Also in the order (Hindu):**

- Consider an alternative: start with products at the **highest** levels of nutrients of concern, then **progressively lower** thresholds.  
- Why wait for **two** nutrients when **one** excess nutrient can harm?  
- **Nutritional literacy in schools** — children are **vulnerable** to impulse / uninformed diet choices; teach how to read labels.  
- **Insufficient information** on hexagon **size and placement**. Word-only labels assume literacy; ideally **words + pictorial** nutrients so the label works across languages and ages.  
- Reducing salt/sugar/fat must not push makers into more **artificial preservatives / emulsifiers** — keep that danger in mind.  
- **ASG Chahar** told the Court the government was **open** to warnings even when **one** nutrient is high (the U-turn vs two-or-more).  
- FSSAI to file an **affidavit in 10 days**. Next hearing **28 September 2026**.

sections.heading: 4. One-liner
sections.content: **FoPL = red hexagon on the pack.** First design = **two or more** of fat/sugar/salt, cut-offs from **ICMR–NIN Dietary Guidelines 2024**. SC (Pardiwala–Vinod Chandran): **what is “high”?** Phase 2 needs a **real timeline**. Affidavit **10 days**; list **28 Sep**. **Prelims trap:** This is **not** the Radura / food-irradiation FSSAI line. Thresholds are **ICMR–NIN 2024**, not a number the clip invents. **Two-or-more** was FSSAI’s first trigger; ASG said they may move to **even one**.

sections.content: `CSE-2018-Q23` **missed** (`MST-078`). **1 only.** The **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006** replaced the **Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954**. FSSAI is a **statutory authority under the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, **not** “under the charge of the Director General of Health Services (DGHS).” He picked **both**. Tonight’s FoPL hearing does not change that institutional lock.

sections.heading: Update — 12 September 2026 (evening paper)

sections.heading: Topic 1: Rapid Himalayan erosion can be a hidden CO₂ *source*
sections.content:
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260913-01`  
> **GS Paper:** **GS-I** (Himalaya, Indus, weathering) + **GS-III** (carbon cycle, climate)

sections.heading: 1. What is in the news
sections.content: **Vasudevan Mukunth.** A team from the **Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Pune**, the **Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology**, and the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Roorkee** — paper in ***Chemical Geology***. Textbook story: Himalayan **silicate weathering** *eats* carbon dioxide (CO₂) and has helped **cool** the Earth for about **50 million years**. This paper: another mineral path can **more than offset** that cooling in the **upper Indus**.

sections.heading: 2. The two paths (clip)
sections.content:
**Sink (the usual story).** The **Indian plate** keeps pushing into the **Eurasian plate**. Mountains erode → fresh **silicate** minerals meet atmospheric CO₂ → rivers carry the carbon to the **oceans** → it locks into **seafloor sediments**.

**Source (the paper).** Himalayan rock also holds **pyrite** (“fool’s gold”). Rapid slope erosion (glaciers are good at **crushing** rock) exposes **sulphides** to air and water for the first time in **millions of years**. Sulphides **oxidise to sulphuric acid**. That acid attacks **carbonate rocks** (common in the **Indus** basin) → **CO₂ is released to the air**.

How they told gypsum apart from pyrite: **sulphur and oxygen isotope** ratios of **sulphates** in the Indus water.

sections.heading: 3. Numbers and map (clip only)
sections.content:
| Lock | Clip |
|:---|:---|
| Where | **Headwaters / upper Indus** |
| Rate | **CO₂ release** from this oxidation path about **three times** the **CO₂ uptake** by silicate weathering |
| Steep mountains | **Net CO₂ sources** |
| Flatter **floodplains** downstream | **CO₂ sinks** — water moves **more slowly**, so silicate weathering can dominate |
| Timescale the authors claim | Glacier-fed catchments as geological CO₂ sources over **million-year** climate, not a next-monsoon inventory |

**Double-edged erosion:** the same grinding that supplies silicates to *remove* CO₂ also feeds the **more aggressive sulphide** reactions.

sections.heading: 4. One-liner
sections.content: Upper **Indus**: pyrite → sulphuric acid → carbonate weathering **outgasses** CO₂ at about **3×** the silicate sink; **mountains source / floodplains sink**. IISER Pune + **Wadia** + IIT Roorkee, *Chemical Geology*. **Prelims trap:** Himalayan weathering is **not only** a CO₂ sink. **Pyrite oxidation ≠ gypsum** (isotopes). **3×** is **upper Indus**, not a global Himalaya average. Flood hook ≠ a new GLOF topic. ```mermaid flowchart LR PY["Pyrite sulphides"] --> SA["Sulphuric acid"] SA --> CAR["Indus carbonates"] CAR --> SRC["CO2 to air · mountains"] SIL["Silicates + CO2"] --> OCN["Ocean sediments · sink"] SRC -.->|"~3× in upper Indus"| SIL ``` ---

sections.heading: Topic 1: PRAHAAR — National Counter-Terrorism Policy and Strategy
sections.content:
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260914-01`  
> **GS Paper:** **GS-III** (internal security, terrorism) + **GS-II** (India and neighbours)

sections.heading: 1. What is in the news
sections.content:
**Rajeev Agarwal** (retired colonel). After **9/11 (11 September 2001)**, terrorism shifted from large groups under named leaders (**Osama bin Laden**, **Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi**) toward **smaller, more autonomous** units, **lone-wolf** attacks, **drones**, **cyber**, and **artificial intelligence** — used by groups **and** by states.

**India lock:** strategy moved from **passive** (warn Pakistan, **do not punish**) to **bold and active**: any act of terrorism **backed by support from across the border** = **“act of war”**. Margin: **defensive restraint → proactive counter-terrorism**.

sections.heading: 2. Firsts on the clip (do not invent extras)
sections.content:

Other named blasts (no extra numbers): **Akshardham 2002**; **Varanasi 2006**; **German Bakery, Pune, 2010**; **Red Fort, 22 December 2000 (LeT)**; Delhi serial bombs **October 2005** (**over 60**); Delhi **September 2008** (including **Sarojini Nagar**, **Paharganj**); **Delhi High Court, 7 September 2011** — **Harkat-ul-Jihad Islami (HUJI)**, al-Qaeda-affiliated, based in Pakistan.

**May 2014:** change of government → clip’s turning point toward **not leaving terror unpunished**.

sections.heading: 3. After Sindoor — three intentions (clip)
sections.content:
1. Era of **restraint and patience** is over; Pakistan pays a **direct and heavy price**.  
2. Future **cross-border terrorism emanating from Pakistan** = **“act of war”**.  
3. **Pakistani nuclear blackmail** will **no longer** be a restraining factor.

sections.heading: 4. PRAHAAR (23 February 2026)
sections.content:
India unveiled **PRAHAAR**, its first comprehensive **National Counter-Terrorism Policy and Strategy**, **23 February 2026**. National framework to **prevent and respond** to terrorist activity and radicalisation through **whole-of-government** and **whole-of-society**. (Clip does not expand the letters — do not invent a full form.)

**Four-fold strategy (clip):**

1. Hunt down and eliminate **remnants** of the terror network **in the country**, especially **Kashmir**.  
2. **Pre-emptive military action** against terror **building across the Line of Control (LoC)**, including **launch pads**.  
3. Exhaustive **de-radicalisation** — make joining / supporting terror **unattractive and prohibitively costly**.  
4. Cut **terror financing**, in coordination with **friendly countries**.

Clip: terror-related incidents in Kashmir have **declined drastically**; the live risk is a **few terrorists infiltrating** across the LoC.

sections.heading: 5. One-liner
sections.content: **PRAHAAR (23 Feb 2026)** = first national counter-terror **policy + strategy**; **whole-of-government / whole-of-society**. Cross-border terror from Pakistan now framed as **act of war**. **Uri** = first surgical strikes; **Balakot** = first IAF strike in Pakistani airspace. **Prelims trap:** **PRAHAAR** is **23 February 2026**, not Sindoor week. **Sindoor 6–7 May** ≠ class **28–29 minutes** (both can be on the clip/class; do not swap). **Correct the Map** is **not** this file. **9/11** here is the **global** turn, not India’s first attack (**Rajiv Gandhi / LTTE 1991** on this clip).

sections.heading: Lok Sabha passes Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026
sections.content:
*   **Context:** The Lok Sabha passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026 amid protests by the Opposition.
*   **Key Provisions of the Bill:**
    *   It seeks to make the delayed registration of births and deaths more stringent.
    *   It requires an order from a judicial magistrate (first class) for registrations done after two years.
*   **Related Constitutional Articles:** Article 246 (Seventh Schedule - Concurrent List Entry 30: Vital statistics including registration of births and deaths).
*   **Other Developments in Parliament:**
    *   **Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025:** A deadline extension was granted to the Joint Parliamentary Committee examining this bill for the submission of its report. The bill proposes the automatic removal of Ministers, Chief Minister, or Prime Minister if they are arrested and held in custody for 30 days on serious criminal charges carrying a jail term of five years or more.
    *   **Related Constitutional Articles:** Article 74, 75 (Council of Ministers for Union); Article 163, 164 (Council of Ministers for States); Article 102, 191 (Disqualifications for membership).

sections.heading: Need for Humane Education System Reform (Editorial)
sections.content:
*   **Context:** Recent student protests have highlighted the need for a complete overhaul of the Indian education system, particularly the competitive examination and admission culture.
*   **Related Constitutional Articles:** Article 21A (Right to Education); Article 45 (Early childhood care and education); Article 46 (Educational interests of weaker sections); Article 246 (Seventh Schedule - Concurrent List Entry 25: Education).
*   **Critique of Current System:**
    *   The single-shot, marks-based competitive exams create a dangerous emotional environment and high stress.
    *   A centralized agency like the National Testing Agency (NTA) assumes a "one-size-fits-all" model which is flawed for a diverse country like India.
    *   A single national test creates logistical overload and demographic unfairness (language, geography, school background, digital access).
    *   The coaching ecosystem displaces formal schooling and exploits student vulnerabilities.
*   **Proposed Reforms:**
    *   **Multi-dimensional Assessment:** Shift from purely memory/speed-based tests to assessing reasoning, persistence, communication, judgment, and ethical orientation. Assessments should include school performance, aptitude, analytical writing, structured interviews, verifiable portfolios, and internships.
    *   **Decentralized System:** Allow universities or clusters of institutions to design and conduct their own assessments within broad University Grants Commission (UGC) norms, moving away from a single centralized exam.
    *   **Safeguards for Exams:** Implement encrypted digital paper transmission, multi-layered question banks with algorithmic randomization, biometric candidate verification, time-staggered papers, and post-examination forensic review to prevent leaks and ensure the sanctity of exams.
    *   **Shift in Focus:** Move from rank-based filtration to capacity-based recognition, emphasizing holistic development over rote learning.

sections.heading: Conservation of Western Ghats (Editorial)
sections.content:
*   **Context:** The debate over the declaration of the Western Ghats as an Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA) is ongoing, with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) extending the tenure of an expert panel by another year after the expiry of the last draft notification in July 2026.
*   **Related Constitutional Articles:** Article 48A (Protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wild life); Article 51A(g) (Fundamental duty to protect and improve the natural environment).
*   **Background:**
    *   **Western Ghats:** Spans six coastal states in India, internationally recognized for its rich biodiversity, and declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012.
    *   **WGEEP (Madhav Gadgil Committee, 2010):** The Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel recommended declaring the entire Western Ghats as an ESA and subdividing it into three Ecologically Sensitive Zones (ESZ) to regulate human activities under the Environment Protection Act, 1986.
    *   **Kasturirangan Committee (2012):** Constituted due to strong local and political opposition to the WGEEP report. It limited restrictions to ecologically sensitive natural landscapes, reducing the ESA coverage to only 37% of the Western Ghats.
*   **Current Status & Challenges:**
    *   Between 2015 and 2026, multiple draft notifications have been issued, but consensus between the Centre and States (especially Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa) remains elusive.
    *   **Case of Karnataka:** The state has consistently opposed the ESA declaration, which covers ~20,668 sq km across 10 of its districts. The state cites potential negative impacts on agriculture, plantations (shade-grown coffee, rubber, coconut), mining, and infrastructure development.
    *   **Local Concerns:** Villagers and stakeholders express fear of possible eviction, restrictions on agricultural practices, and challenges to forest rights (e.g., minor forest produce collection).
*   **Way Forward:**
    *   Conservation efforts cannot be indefinitely delayed as it can result in states losing control over ecological systems to administrative boundaries.
    *   The ESA declaration should proactively include and protect indigenous communities living within forests. They naturally follow conservation principles and their presence serves as a vital bridge in preserving biocultural diversity.

sections.heading: 1. CAPF vs IPS: Dispute Over Leadership Positions
sections.content:
**Context:** Over 3,000 serving Group A officers from Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) have approached the Supreme Court against the recently notified **Central Armed Police Force (General Administration) Act, 2026**.

**The Core Issue:**
*   **The CAPF Act 2026:** Reserves the majority of top leadership positions for Indian Police Service (IPS) officers on deputation. Specifically:
    *   **50%** of Inspector General (IG) posts.
    *   At least **67%** of Additional Director General (ADG) posts.
    *   **100%** of Special Director General (SDG) and Director General (DG) posts.
*   **Negation of SC Ruling:** The new Act effectively negates a landmark May 2025 Supreme Court judgment (*Sanjay Prakash v. Union of India*), which had directed:
    *   Recognizing Group A Executive Cadre officers of CAPFs as **Organised Group A Services (OGAS)**.
    *   Progressively *reducing* IPS deputation in CAPFs up to the IG level over two years.
    *   The SC had previously dismissed the Ministry of Home Affairs' (MHA) review petition against this ruling, prompting the MHA to introduce the Bill in Parliament to bypass the judgment.

**Legal & Constitutional Grounds of Challenge:**
*   The petitioners argue that the law hinders the career progression of CAPF cadre officers, depriving them of leadership roles despite years of service.
*   The petition seeks to declare **Sections 3 and 4** of the CAPF Act as *ultra vires* (beyond the powers) of the Constitution.
    *   *Section 3:* Pertains to regulation of recruitment and conditions of service.
    *   *Section 4:* Gives the Union government power to amend the First and Second Schedules of the Act through mere notification.

**About CAPFs:**
*   They function under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)**.
*   Includes: Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Border Security Force (BSF), Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), and Central Industrial Security Force (CISF).

**Related Constitutional Articles:**
*   **[Article 13](../../Articles/Article_13.md):** Basis for judicial review; laws inconsistent with fundamental rights can be declared *ultra vires*.
*   **[Article 33](../../Articles/Article_33.md):** Power of Parliament to restrict/modify fundamental rights in their application to armed forces and police forces to ensure proper discharge of duties and discipline.
*   **[Article 312](../../Articles/Article_312.md):** Deals with All-India Services, under which the IPS is constituted, whose officers go on deputation to CAPFs.

---

sections.heading: 2. Drug Testing in Educational Institutions
sections.content:
**Context:** Under directions from the Union government, higher educational institutions across India, starting with IITs and IIMs this year, will begin suggesting voluntary drug testing as part of the admission process. Results will remain confidential.

**Key Initiative:**
*   This is part of a broader government push against substance abuse among the youth.
*   The Prime Minister is scheduled to launch the **'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat'** initiative.
*   It follows an expansive survey of substance users across India, with results expected in the coming years.

**Related Constitutional Articles:**
*   **[Article 47](../../Articles/Article_47.md) (DPSP):** It is the primary duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and standard of living and improve public health. Specifically, the State shall endeavour to bring about the **prohibition of the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs** which are injurious to health (except for medicinal purposes).

---

sections.heading: 3. Bhitarkanika National Park Reopens with Plastic Ban
sections.content:
**Context:** The Bhitarkanika National Park in Kendrapara district, Odisha, has reopened to tourists after a three-month closure.

**Key Details:**
*   **Reason for Closure:** Closed from May 1 to July 31 annually for the **nesting and breeding season of estuarine (saltwater) crocodiles**.
*   **New Measure:** Authorities have enforced a **complete ban on plastics** within the park.
*   **Features:** It is a vital mangrove ecosystem and wildlife habitat.

**Related Constitutional Articles:**
*   **[Article 48A](../../Articles/Article_48A.md) (DPSP):** The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wild life of the country.
*   **[Article 51A(g)](../../Articles/Article_51A_g.md) (Fundamental Duties):** It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life, and to have compassion for living creatures.

sections.heading: 1. Andhra Pradesh & Australia Sign 4 MoUs on Education & Clean Energy
sections.content:
**Context:** Andhra Pradesh and Australia signed four Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) covering clean energy, advanced manufacturing, inclusive education, student mental health, and skill development.

**Key Details:**
*   Agreements signed in the presence of **AP HRD Minister Nara Lokesh** and **Australia's Assistant Minister Julian Hill**.

*   The four MoU domains:
    1. Clean Energy (Solar Manufacturing)
    2. Advanced Manufacturing
    3. Inclusive Education
    4. Student Mental Health & Skill Development

**UPSC Significance:**
*   **GS-II (International Relations):** India-Australia bilateral relations expanding beyond security (QUAD) into education and clean energy technology transfer.
*   **GS-III (Science & Technology / Energy):** Solar manufacturing is a key pillar of India's **National Solar Mission** (target: 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030) and **PLI Scheme for Solar PV Modules**.
*   India-Australia relations have deepened post-**ECTA (Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement, 2022)** — the first FTA between the two nations.

**Related Constitutional Provisions:**

sections.heading: 2. Strong Health Systems for All with Better Public Spending (Editorial)
sections.content:
**Context:** An editorial by **Nahil Golafi** and **Vasa Thiru** (former WHO officials) argues for building robust public health systems through increased and better-directed public financing, especially in Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs).

**Key Arguments & Data Points:**

sections.heading: Health Aid Under Pressure
sections.content:
*   Global development assistance for health reached a peak during the **COVID-19 pandemic** but has since **plateaued and declined**.
*   The trend of donor aid is **heterogeneous** — some countries contributed more, while others reduced aid.
*   Between **LMICs and high-income countries (HICs)**, the health spending gap remains enormous — per capita spending on health can be **100× lower** in LMICs.

sections.heading: Developing Countries' Debt Crisis
sections.content:
*   In 2024, the **public debt of developing countries** has risen to approximately **$29 trillion** — **twice** as fast as that of advanced countries, according to **UNCTAD (United Nations Conference on Trade and Development)**.
*   Developing countries paid **$823 billion** in net interest payments in 2024.
*   This debt burden is **crowding out** essential public health and social sector spending.

sections.heading: The Right Health Investments
sections.content:
*   The editorial argues that there is **chronic underspending** in public health care globally.
*   Key recommendation: Increase **public financing of health** to enhance service delivery, governance, and accountability.
*   Countries that invest in **primary healthcare systems** show better health outcomes and greater resilience to pandemics.

**UPSC Significance:**
*   **GS-II (Health / Governance):** India's **National Health Policy 2017** targets raising public health expenditure to **2.5% of GDP** (currently ~2.1% as of 2024-25).
*   **GS-III (Economy):** Debt distress in developing countries and its impact on social sector allocation — links to India's fiscal policy and **FRBM Act** considerations.
*   Key organizations: **WHO**, **UNCTAD**, **World Bank**.

**Related Constitutional Provisions:**
*   **[Article 21](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_21.md)** — Right to Life (includes Right to Health as interpreted by the Supreme Court in *Paschim Banga Khet Mazdoor Samity v. State of West Bengal*, 1996).
*   **[Article 47](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_47.md)** — DPSP: Duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health.

---

sections.heading: 3. Drugs-Free Youth Crucial for Developed India: PM Modi
sections.content:
**Context:** Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched a nationwide campaign — **"Nasha Mukt Yun for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan"** (Drug-Free Youth for Developed India Pledge Campaign) — calling for physically and mentally fit young Indians as the foundation of 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India by 2047).

**Key Details:**
*   **Over 1 crore participants** joined the pledge against substance abuse.
*   Supported by **125+ spiritual and public organisations**, educational institutions, and industrial associations.
*   Conducted at **28,000+ locations** across the country, with participation from several Chief Ministers and Governors.
*   The pledge will continue over the **next 100 weeks**, with weekly activities related to art, culture, sports, meditation, spirituality, and service.

**PM's Key Statements:**
*   *"Over the next 20 to 25 years, you will shape your own lives, and by 2047, it is you who will lead India to the goal of becoming a developed country."*
*   *"When a young person falls into drug addiction, it is not only that individual who loses. A dream dies before it can be fulfilled. An entire family suffers and often falls apart."*
*   *"Hostile countries also conspire to lure our youth into drug addiction. Profit from drug trafficking while weakening our country is part of their malicious agenda."*
*   Urged people not to hide cases of addiction and to seek professional help. Rehabilitation centres have been established to aid recovery.
*   Government taking **stringent action against drug traffickers** — arrests have increased significantly compared to previous years.

**UPSC Significance:**
*   **GS-II (Social Issues / Governance):** Drug abuse as a social challenge; government's multi-pronged approach (awareness, rehabilitation, enforcement).
*   **GS-IV (Ethics):** Societal responsibility toward addiction — *"Someone who defeats addiction is a true warrior. Society should respect them and give them a second chance."*
*   Relevant Schemes: **NMBA (Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan)** launched in 2020 across 272 most-affected districts.
*   **NDPS Act, 1985 (Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act)** — India's primary anti-drug legislation.

**Related Constitutional Provisions:**
*   **[Article 47](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_47.md)** — DPSP: The State shall endeavour to bring about prohibition of the consumption of intoxicating drinks and of drugs which are injurious to health (except for medicinal purposes).
*   **[Article 21](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_21.md)** — Right to Life includes the right to live with dignity, free from substance-induced degradation.

---

sections.heading: 4. Lepidoptera Hotspot: India Is Home to 8.25% of the World's Butterflies & Moths
sections.content:
**Context:** A landmark scientific publication — **"Catalogue of Lepidoptera of India"** — published in the peer-reviewed journal **Zootaxa**, documents India's extraordinary lepidopteran (butterfly and moth) diversity.

**Key Data Points:**
*   India hosts **13,703 species** of Lepidoptera:
    *   **12,286 are moths**
    *   **1,417 are butterflies**
*   This represents **8.25% of the world's total** lepidopteran species.
*   Classified into **240 subfamilies, 102 families, 2,048 genera**.
*   The catalogue was compiled by scientists **Navneet Singh** and **Rahul Joshi** over **12 years** of research.
*   India has **31 superfamilies** of butterflies and moths.

**Ecological Significance:**
*   Butterflies and moths serve as **ecological indicators** — their populations reflect ecosystem health.
*   They play a **crucial role as pollinators** and serve as a vital part of the food chain.
*   They are also important as **natural assets for biodiversity science** — helping researchers track environmental degradation.
*   These insects are among the most **ancient fauna** — predating even trees, serving as essential herbivores.

**UPSC Significance:**
*   **GS-III (Environment & Biodiversity):** India as a **mega-biodiversity hotspot** — links to Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF, 2022).
*   India has **4 of the world's 36 biodiversity hotspots**: Western Ghats, Eastern Himalayas, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland.
*   **National Mission on Biodiversity and Human Well-Being** — proposed under the Prime Minister's Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council (PM-STIAC).
*   Butterflies as **bio-indicators** — frequently asked in Prelims context (e.g., indicator species, keystone species, flagship species).

**Related Constitutional Provisions:**
*   **[Article 48A](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_48A.md)** — DPSP: The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country.
*   **[Article 51A(g)](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_51A_g.md)** — Fundamental Duty: To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.

sections.heading: Lok Sabha Passes Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026
sections.content:
*   **Context:** The Lok Sabha passed a bill to **increase the strength of judges in the Supreme Court from 34 to 38** (including the Chief Justice of India). The bill was passed **without any discussion** as the House was adjourned repeatedly due to Opposition protests.
*   **Background:**
    *   The Supreme Court's sanctioned strength was last increased in 2019 from 31 to 34.
    *   Rising pendency of cases (over 80,000 cases pending in SC) necessitates additional judges.
    *   The bill amends the **Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956**.
*   **Other Bills Passed:**
    *   **Indian Statistical Institute Bill** — restructuring and modernizing the Indian Statistical Institute.
    *   **Bankers' Books Evidence (Amendment) Bill** — updating evidence rules for digital banking records.
*   **UPSC Relevance:**

    *   Repeated adjournments without debate raise concerns about **Parliamentary productivity** and the role of the Opposition.

**Related Constitutional Provisions:**
*   **[Article 124](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_124.md)** — Establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court; appointment of judges by the President after consultation with CJI and other judges.
*   **[Article 142](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_142.md)** — SC's power to do complete justice.

sections.heading: Rajya Sabha Passes MSME Bill Amid Opposition Protests
sections.content:
*   **Context:** The Rajya Sabha passed a bill aimed at addressing **liquidity concerns and delayed payments** to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).
*   **Key Provisions:**

sections.heading: The Dilemma Over PM SHRI Schools in Kerala (Editorial — The Hindu)
sections.content:
*   **Context:** The newly elected Congress-led **United Democratic Front (UDF)** government in Kerala is caught in a dilemma over the **PM SHRI (PM Schools for Rising India)** scheme — balancing the need for central funds against maintaining educational autonomy and opposing the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**.
*   **What is PM SHRI Scheme?**
    *   Launched in 2022 to upgrade and develop existing government schools as **model schools** showcasing the implementation of NEP 2020.
    *   Requires states to sign an **MoU with the Union government** committing to implement the NEP framework.
    *   Over 14,500 schools selected across India; central funding of ₹1,58,813 crore earmarked.
*   **Kerala's Dilemma:**
    *   The previous **LDF (Left) government** had opted out of PM SHRI in 2022, arguing it would impose NEP's curriculum framework on the state.
    *   The new UDF government initially signalled willingness to implement PM SHRI, but faces internal resistance from coalition partners and Muslim organizations (IUML) who oppose NEP.
    *   **Wavering Stance:** Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan argued Kerala was forced to comply since the previous LDF government had already entered into an agreement; the Opposition vehemently denies this.
    *   Union Minister of State for Education Jayant Chaudhary said: *"States that do not sign the MoU or withdraw from the scheme stand to miss out on the benefits of PM SHRI scheme."*
*   **Pros & Cons:**
    *   **Pro:** Access to substantial central education funding; school infrastructure upgradation.
    *   **Con:** Loss of curricular autonomy; NEP's National Curriculum Framework may be imposed.
    *   **Punjab precedent:** Opted out in 2022, later reversed after Union government froze education funds.
    *   **Tamil Nadu route:** Wrote to Union government seeking freedom to decide its own curriculum within the scheme.
*   **Key Issue — Fiscal Federalism:**
    *   States that don't implement PM SHRI risk losing crucial **central education funding** — creating a *"damned if they do, damned if they don't"* situation.
    *   Raises questions about **conditional central funding** as a tool for policy imposition on states.
*   **UPSC Relevance:**
    *   **GS-II (Education + Centre-State Relations):** NEP 2020 implementation challenges; Education is on the **Concurrent List** (Entry 25, Seventh Schedule) — both Centre and States can legislate.
    *   **GS-II (Fiscal Federalism):** Conditional vs. unconditional central transfers; states' autonomy in education policy.

**Related Constitutional Provisions:**
*   **[Article 21A](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_21A.md)** — Right to Education (6–14 years) as a Fundamental Right.
*   **[Article 246](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_246.md)** — Seventh Schedule, Concurrent List Entry 25 (Education).
*   **[Article 45](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_45.md)** — DPSP: Early childhood care and education.

sections.heading: Critical Minerals — The Foundation of Strategic Power (Op-Ed — The Hindu)
sections.content:
*   **Context:** An op-ed by Vinayak Vipul (EY-Parthenon India) highlighting why **critical minerals** are the new geopolitical battleground and India's urgent need to secure supply chains.
*   **What are Critical Minerals?**
    *   Minerals essential for **clean energy transition, EVs, semiconductors, defence, and advanced manufacturing**.
    *   Key minerals: **Lithium, Cobalt, Nickel, Graphite, Copper, Rare Earth Elements (REEs), Gallium, Germanium**.
*   **Why Critical Now?**
    *   Global shift to clean energy (solar, wind, EVs, battery storage) is **mineral-intensive** — an EV requires 6x more minerals than a conventional car.
    *   **Demand projection:** IEA estimates demand for critical minerals could increase **4–6x by 2040**.
*   **Geopolitical Risk — China's Dominance:**
    *   China controls ~**60% of global mining** and ~**90% of processing** for rare earth elements.
    *   China is the leading refiner in 19 out of 20 strategic minerals.
    *   Average market share: ~86% for rare earths, ~70% for cobalt processing, ~65% for lithium processing.
    *   The EU, US, and Australia are building **parallel supply chains** through partnerships (e.g., Minerals Security Partnership).
*   **India's Position:**
    *   India depends on **imports for over 90%** of its critical mineral needs.
    *   **KABIL (Khanij Bidesh India Limited)** — Joint venture (NALCO + HCL + MECL) for overseas mineral acquisition.
    *   India's **Critical Mineral Strategy** identifies 30 critical minerals (updated 2023 list).
    *   Domestic potential: India has significant reserves of **rare earths** (beach sands of Kerala, Odisha) and **lithium** (Jammu & Kashmir — Reasi discovery, 2023).
*   **Structural Constraints:**
    *   India's mineral processing capacity is limited — mostly exports raw ore.
    *   No domestic graphite processing; nearly **75% of critical mineral imports** come from China.
    *   Recycling and urban mining are underdeveloped.
*   **Mission to Execution:**
    *   Phased approach: Explore → Mine → Process → Manufacture.
    *   Need: Scale up domestic exploration, build processing infrastructure, diversify sources through bilateral deals (Australia, Chile, Argentina, Africa), promote recycling.
*   **UPSC Relevance:**
    *   **GS-III (Economy — Minerals & Mining):** Critical Mineral Strategy, KABIL, Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act amendments.
    *   **GS-II (IR):** Supply chain diversification, Minerals Security Partnership, India's engagement with resource-rich nations.
    *   **GS-III (Security):** Defence applications — rare earths in fighter jets, submarines, missile systems.

---

*End of Current Affairs — 4 August 2026*

sections.heading: EC Revises SIR Deadline for Delhi Electoral Rolls — Second Extension in a Month
sections.content:
*   **Context:** The Election Commission of India (EC) on Tuesday **revised the schedule for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR)** of Delhi's electoral rolls for the **second time in a month**, extending the ongoing door-to-door verification by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) **till August 17** and postponing the publication of the final electoral roll to **October 27**.
*   **Background:**
    *   The distribution and collection of enumeration forms was initially scheduled to conclude within a month of the exercise beginning on **June 30**.
    *   It was first rescheduled to conclude on **August 8** after the first extension announced by the EC on **July 15**.
    *   This is the **second extension** in a month after Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) **Ashok Kumar** sought additional time, citing **"slow progress in the enumeration process"**.
*   **Key Data (as of Tuesday):**
    *   **63.23%** of the **1.45 crore** enumeration forms had been digitised.
    *   **99.199%** forms were distributed, with just **four days remaining** for the first extension deadline.
*   **'Slow Progress' — CEO's Office Report:**
    *   Reports of slow progress in distribution and collection of enumeration forms.
    *   The proposal for an extension was prepared and sent to the EC.
    *   The remaining time was **not sufficient** for BLOs to complete the exercise without errors and verify all details of the electors.
*   **BLOs' Role During Ongoing Enumeration:**
    *   Visiting households to distribute and collect filled enumeration forms containing details of electors.
    *   Where available, mapping them with the last SIR roll.
    *   Responsible for identifying absent, dead, shifted, and duplicate voters.
    *   Reported challenges in verifying voters who shifted out, and helping electors map their details or those of their relatives with entries in previous rolls.
*   **'Unbearable Burden' on Government School Teachers:**
    *   The extension was in line with a recent **Delhi High Court** direction to ensure that election-related work **does not place an unbearable burden on government school teachers** deployed for the exercise.
    *   *"Some teachers are doing the SIR work after their regular school duties. By the time they come to the field, they are already exhausted."*
*   **Revised Timeline:**
    *   Door-to-door verification by BLOs: Extended till **August 17**.
    *   Draft roll publication: **August 24**.
    *   Claims and objections filing: **24 September — 23 October**.
    *   Followed by a **month-long** notice period and disposal of claims.
    *   **Final electoral roll publication: October 27**.

**Related Constitutional Provisions:**
*   **[Article 324](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_324.md)** — Superintendence, direction, and control of elections vested in the Election Commission of India. The EC has plenary powers over electoral roll preparation.
*   **[Article 326](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_326.md)** — Elections to the House of the People and Legislative Assemblies shall be on the basis of **adult suffrage** — every citizen above 18 years is entitled to be registered as a voter.

*   **UPSC Relevance:**
    *   **GS-II (Polity — Election Commission):** Powers and functions of EC under Article 324; electoral roll revision process; role of BLOs and CEOs; challenges of universal adult suffrage under Article 326.
    *   **GS-II (Governance):** Administrative burden on school teachers for election duties; Delhi HC intervention to protect fundamental duties of teachers.

sections.heading: Supreme Court Directs RBI to Frame SOPs to Curb 'Digital Arrest' Scams
sections.content:
*   **Context:** The Supreme Court directed the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to prepare and circulate within **four weeks** a **Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)** for banks for placing **temporary debit holds on mule accounts** linked to money laundering activity and cyber-enabled fraud.
*   **Key Directives by the SC:**
    *   A copy of the SOP shall be furnished to the **Registrars-General of all High Courts**.
    *   States and Union Territories directed to **frame modules for grievance redressal and money restoration** as per the Ministry of Home Affairs' SOP concerning the **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal** and **Cyber RMS**.
    *   States asked to **notify Cyber Crime Coordination Centres and e-Zero FIRs within four weeks**.
*   **Fourth Status Report — Key Data:**
    *   A **data-sharing MoU** between the **Reserve Bank Innovation Hub** and **I4C (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre)** was executed on **May 11, 2026**.
    *   The **grievance redressal mechanism portal** now covers **1,23,590 branches of 69 banks**.
    *   **Money Restoration Mechanism Portal:** 57 participating banks, covers all **36 States and UTs**; restoration completed in **36,290 cases** involving aggregate amount of **₹18.05 crore**.
    *   **e-Zero FIR mechanism** functional in **19 States**; only **14 States** had notified their State Cyber Crime Coordination Centres.
*   **Telecommunications Regulations Status:**
    *   **Telecommunications (Radio Equipment Possession Authorisation) Rules, 2025** — notified.
    *   **Telecommunications (User Identification) Rules, 2025** — at final stage of notification.
*   **CBI Investigation Findings:**
    *   Presently registered **10 digital arrest cases** and several connected cases.
    *   Identified **238 victims**, **67 first-layer bank accounts**.
    *   Transactions of approximately **₹80 crore**.
    *   Conducted searches at **93 locations across 16 States**.

**Related Constitutional Provisions:**
*   **[Article 21](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_21.md)** — Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Digital arrest scams violate citizens' right to live with dignity, free from fraud and coercion. SC's intervention protects this fundamental right.
*   **[Article 142](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_142.md)** — SC's power to pass any order necessary for doing "complete justice"; basis for directing RBI and States to frame SOPs.

*   **UPSC Relevance:**
    *   **GS-II (Judiciary):** SC's suo motu intervention; judicial activism in directing executive agencies (RBI, MHA) to act.
    *   **GS-III (Internal Security):** Cyber security infrastructure — I4C, National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, e-Zero FIRs; digital fraud typology (mule accounts, digital arrest scams).
    *   **GS-III (Economy):** RBI's role in banking regulation; SOP for temporary debit holds; grievance redressal mechanisms.

sections.heading: NATO Enters a New Strategic Era of Transformation
sections.content:
*   **Context:** An analysis of NATO's evolving strategic posture, its adaptation to the changing global security landscape, and implications for India.
*   **NATO's Evolution Over Time:**
    *   **Founded:** April 4, 1949 (North Atlantic Treaty / Washington Treaty).
    *   **Original Purpose:** Collective defence against the Soviet Union during the Cold War (Article 5 — an attack on one is an attack on all).
    *   **Post-Cold War:** Expanded role — peacekeeping (Balkans), counter-terrorism (Afghanistan post-9/11), humanitarian interventions.
    *   **2010 Strategic Concept:** Adopted at Lisbon Summit — identified three core tasks: collective defence, crisis management, and cooperative security.
    *   **2022 Madrid Summit:** New Strategic Concept — identified **Russia as the most significant and direct threat**; first time acknowledged challenges posed by **China**.
*   **Current Transformation:**
    *   **Defence spending:** NATO members committed to spending **2% of GDP** on defence; many now pushing towards **2.5–3%**.
    *   **Military readiness:** 75,000-strong rapid-deployment force; NATO Response Force (NRF) enhanced.
    *   **Technology focus:** AI, cyber defence, space domain awareness.
    *   NATO's defence spending by 2029 target: **$400 billion** (up from $130 billion in 2006).
    *   **Sustaining support for Ukraine** in its conflict with Russia — NATO certified military assistance.
*   **America's Skin — US Role:**
    *   US remains NATO's **principal financier** and military guarantor.
    *   Questions about long-term US commitment amid domestic political shifts.
    *   US accounts for roughly **70%** of total NATO defence spending.
*   **New Delhi and the Rebalance — India-NATO Dynamics:**
    *   India is not a NATO member and maintains **strategic autonomy**.
    *   However, India has engaged with NATO through **partnership mechanisms** and dialogue on shared concerns (counter-terrorism, maritime security).
    *   India's concerns about NATO's **Indo-Pacific tilt** — potential to complicate India-China and India-Russia equations.
    *   Model for India: Can cooperate with NATO's **newer strategic agenda** (cyber, tech, counter-terrorism) without formal membership, using bilateral partnerships with individual NATO members (US, France, UK).
*   **NATO's Shift:**
    *   From a purely **Euro-Atlantic** defence alliance to one with **Indo-Pacific consciousness**.
    *   Invited **Australia, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand** (AP4 partners) to recent summits.

*   **UPSC Relevance:**
    *   **GS-II (International Relations):** NATO's evolution; India's strategic autonomy doctrine; Indo-Pacific geopolitics; India-US-Europe trilateral dynamics.
    *   **GS-II (Bilateral Relations):** India's engagement with NATO members bilaterally vs. alliance-level engagement.
    *   **GS-III (Security):** Collective security mechanisms; defence spending benchmarks; cyber and space as new domains of conflict.

sections.heading: Topic 1: Fiscal Federalism — Efficiency vs. Equity Concerns in FC-16
sections.content:
> **Headlines:** *"Fiscal federalism, efficiency versus equity concerns"* (by K.J. Joseph & Sujit Kumar)  
> **GS Paper:** GS-II (Polity & Governance — Federal Structure) & GS-III (Fiscal Policy)  
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260806-01`

sections.heading: 1. Constitutional Foundation of Grants-in-Aid
sections.content: * **[Article 275](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_275.md) (Grants-in-Aid):** Designed as a routine institutional mechanism for horizontal fiscal equalization. Recognizes that formula-based tax devolution under **[Article 280](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_280.md)** cannot fully address state-specific structural disadvantages (e.g. Kerala's old-age demographic, hill terrain costs in HP & NE states, severe debt stress).

sections.heading: 2. Key Controversies in 16th Finance Commission (FC-16)
sections.content:
* **Reduction in Revenue Deficit Grants (RDG):** FC-16 recommends post-devolution RDGs of ₹1.33 lakh crore to 14 states (down sharply from ₹2.94 lakh crore to 17 states under FC-15).
* **The "Grand Bargain" & Cesses/Surcharges:** The Centre has increased non-shareable cesses and surcharges (which do not enter the divisible pool), while offering to gradually merge them in exchange for a lower vertical devolution share to States.
* **Conditional Sector-Specific Grants:** Tying grants to strict performance targets in water, sanitation, and accounting reforms limits the fiscal autonomy of State governments.
* **Efficiency vs. Equity Trade-off:** FC-16 shifts weightage towards performance incentives (market efficiency), which disproportionately penalizes states with high structural costs or historical fiscal deficits.

sections.heading: 3. Mains Answer Key Takeaway
sections.content:
> *"True fiscal federalism requires balancing market efficiency with redistributive equity. Over-reliance on conditional grants or restricting Article 275 RDGs weakens the equalizing core of India's fiscal architecture."*

sections.heading: Topic 2: Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) Bill, 2026 & Governance Controversy
sections.content:
> **Headlines:** *"Why is the Indian Statistical Institute Bill controversial?"* (Text & Context)  
> **GS Paper:** GS-II (Statutory, Regulatory & Quasi-Judicial Bodies; Governance)  
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260806-02`

sections.heading: 1. Historical Context of ISI
sections.content:
* **Founder:** Prof. P.C. Mahalanobis (father of Indian statistics) founded the Statistical Laboratory at Presidency College, Kolkata on **17 December 1931** (registered 28 April 1932 under Societies Registration Act 1860).
* **Statutory Status:** Declared an **Institution of National Importance (INI)** under the *Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959*.

sections.heading: 2. Key Changes Proposed in ISI Bill, 2026
sections.content:
* Replaces the 67-year-old ISI Act of 1959.
* **Governance Model Shift:** Shifts ISI from a **"learned non-profit society model"** (where the General Body of members holds ultimate legislative/administrative control) to a **corporate-style Board of Governors / Academic Council** structure (on par with IITs and IIMs).

sections.heading: 3. Core Points of Contention
sections.content:
* **Usurpation of Autonomy:** Faculty, academics, and MPs argue that creating a central Board of Governors weakens the democratic, peer-reviewed learned society model of Mahalanobis.
* **Executive Overreach:** Gives the Central Government direct power over executive appointments (Director, Board Chairman) and policy regulations without requiring General Body ratification.

sections.heading: Topic 3: Conservation Architecture of the Asiatic Lion
sections.content:
> **Headlines:** *"The road ahead for the Asiatic lion"* (by Meena Venkataraman)  
> **GS Paper:** GS-III (Environment & Biodiversity Conservation)  
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260806-03`

sections.heading: 1. Species Profile & Population Dynamics
sections.content:
* **Species:** Asiatic Lion (*Panthera leo persica*).
* **Habitat Range:** Sole free-ranging population in the world resides in the Gir landscape (Gujarat).
* **Population Recovery:** Grown from 400–450 to **over 1,000 lions** today.
* **Key Vulnerability:** **Nearly 50% of Asiatic lions now live OUTSIDE protected areas** (Gir National Park & Sanctuary) across 9 Saurashtra districts (Bhavnagar coast, Mitiyala, Savarkundla-Liliya, Babarkot).

sections.heading: 2. Major Threats & Conservation Challenges
sections.content:
* **Single-Landscape Vulnerability:** Concentration in a single geography creates extreme risk of catastrophic disease outbreaks (e.g. **Canine Distemper Virus - CDV** in 2018; **Babesiosis** outbreak in May 2026).
* **Habitat Fragmentation & Linear Barriers:** Proposal to divert ~75 hectares of reserved forest for limestone mining in the Babarkot corridor threatens dispersal routes.
* **Human-Wildlife Coexistence:** Increasing reliance on shared agricultural and human-dominated landscapes outside Gir.

sections.heading: 3. Conservation Roadmap & Satellite Refuges
sections.content:
* **Barda Wildlife Sanctuary:** Designated as a crucial secondary home / satellite sanctuary in Gujarat to accommodate spillover lion populations and mitigate epidemic risks.
* **IUCN Status:** **Endangered** (Listed under Schedule I of Wildlife Protection Act, 1972; CITES Appendix I).

sections.heading: Topic 1: Union Govt Opposes Income-Based "Creamy Layer" in SC/ST Quotas
sections.content:
> **Headlines:** *"Govt. opposes income-based creamy layer in SC/ST quotas"* (by Abhinay Lakshman)  
> **GS Paper:** GS-II (Polity & Governance — Constitutional Rights, Reservations & Social Justice)  
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260807-01`

sections.heading: 1. Context & Union Government's Stand in Supreme Court
sections.content:
* The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court opposing a batch of petitions seeking the exclusion of the **"creamy layer"** from Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) on the lines of Other Backward Classes (OBCs).
* The Centre asserted that any modification of reservation policy—particularly introducing income-based preferences within SC/ST categories—must be preceded by a **holistic review and empirical study**, including socio-economic data of reserved category beneficiaries, rather than ad-hoc judicial mandates.

sections.heading: 2. Constitutional Architecture & Judicial Precedents
sections.content:
| Landmark Case / Provision | Core Ruling / Context | Application to SC/ST Creamy Layer |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **[Article 15(4)](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_15.md) & [Article 16(4)](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_16.md)** | Enable Special Provisions & Reservations for Socially & Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs), SCs, and STs. | Forms the constitutional bedrock for affirmative action in education and public employment. |
| ***Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)*** | 9-judge bench established that the "creamy layer" test applies to **OBCs** to filter out economically/socially advanced individuals. | SC explicitly held that the creamy layer concept is **NOT applicable to SCs and STs**. |
| ***M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006)*** | Applied criteria of backwardness, inadequacy of representation, and overall efficiency (Art. 335) for SC/ST promotions. | Observations on creamy layer in SC/ST promotion were treated by Centre as *obiter dicta* (general observations), not binding ratio. |
| ***State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024)*** | 7-judge bench upheld state governments' power to **sub-categorize** SC/STs to give preference to more backward sub-groups. | Justice B.R. Gavai's concurring opinion suggested identifying creamy layer in SC/STs, but Centre clarified that sub-categorization sanction does not equate to mandating an income-based creamy layer at the national level. |

sections.heading: 3. Key Substantive Arguments of the Centre
sections.content:
* **Social Stigma vs. Income Poverty:** SC/ST reservations were instituted to address centuries of structural social discrimination, untouchability, and historical exclusion—**not merely economic backwardness**. Income elevation does not automatically erase social stigma or untouchability.
* **Pre-existing "Means Test" in Welfare Schemes:** The Centre highlighted that a "means test" (income threshold) is already actively enforced across most government welfare, scholarship, and development schemes for SC/STs to ensure targeted benefit delivery to the poorest. However, constitutional reservation under Part III aims at **representation and social empowerment**.
* **Lack of Empirical Basis:** Introducing income criteria without a nationwide socio-economic survey risks denying constitutional guarantees of equal opportunity ([Article 16](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_16.md)).

sections.heading: Update — 10 September 2026 (Social Issues L2)
sections.content: Class lock on *Indra Sawhney* (cluster `SOC-02`, no extra Day-1): creamy layer is **families** inside an OBC caste, **social and educational** status first (income is a proxy); **OBC only**, not SC/ST. Sub-classification allowed for OBCs so benefits reach the last mile; Centre has **not** subclassified the central list (**Rohini Commission 2017**, report **2022**: about **15** OBC castes take **~90%** of the benefit). Full lecture: `GS_Society_VR_Notes/02_Caste_Power_and_Reservation.md`.

sections.heading: Update — 12 September 2026 (Social Issues L3 — no extra Day-1)
sections.content:
Same clip, class extras on `SOC-03` (do **not** spawn a new cluster): **2004** Court barred SC/ST sub-classification because they were **homogeneous**. ***Davinder Singh v. State of Punjab* (2024)** allows it — **no longer homogeneous**; more backward SCs **within** SCs (Punjab **Valmiki / Mazhabi**; TN **Pallar / Arunthathiyar**). Creamy layer **inside SC** is now a **class reform ask** so have-nots get seats — **not** a claim that the Union affidavit has flipped. Centre’s **oppose income-based creamy layer** line above still stands.

sections.heading: Topic 2: SC Clarification on Ramsar Wetland Sites & Mining Buffer Zones
sections.content:
> **Headlines:** *"How will the Supreme Court order impact mining around Ramsar wetland sites?"* (by Jacob P Koshy)  
> **GS Paper:** GS-III (Environment & Ecology — Wetlands, Environmental Clearance & SC Judgments)  
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260807-02`

sections.heading: 1. Supreme Court Clarification (August 2026)
sections.content:
* **Background:** In February 2024, the SC directed that mining proposals within a **10-km radius** of the **Asan Wetland Conservation Reserve** (Uttarakhand) require prior approval from the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL).
* **Clarification:** Hearing an application from Himachal Pradesh, the SC clarified that the 10-km mining restriction in the Feb 2024 order was **specific to the Asan Reserve** (due to its distinct conservation reserve status & NBWL mandate) and **does NOT automatically apply as a universal 10-km statutory buffer zone to all Ramsar sites across India**.

sections.heading: 2. Legal & Environmental Framework Comparison
sections.content:
| Regime | Governing Law / Treaty | Buffer Zone & Mining Rules |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Ramsar Convention Sites** | International Treaty (Ramsar, 1971; India joined 1982). India has **101 Ramsar sites** *(101st: Glaw Lake, Arunachal Pradesh — Aug 3, 2026)*. | Ramsar status is an international commitment for "wise use". It **does NOT automatically create a statutory buffer zone** under domestic law unless designated under WPA 1972 or ESZ rules. |
| **Wetlands Conservation Rules, 2017** | Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. | Prohibits solid waste dumping, untreated effluent discharge, and permanent construction inside wetlands. Does **not** mandate a default 10-km buffer zone outside wetland boundaries. |
| **National Parks & Wildlife Sanctuaries** | Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. | Mining is strictly **prohibited within 1 km** of notified boundaries or designated Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs). |
| **Forest Clearances** | Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 & EIA 2006. | Mining in forest land requires prior Forest Clearance (Stage I & II) and Environmental Clearance (EC) subject to site-specific appraisal. |

sections.heading: 3. Key Takeaway for UPSC
sections.content:
* International treaty designations (like Ramsar) provide high conservation priority but require specific domestic statutory notifications (ESZs or PA declarations) to enforce mandatory territorial buffer zones like mining bans.

---

sections.heading: 1. Historical Context of National Handloom Day

sections.heading: 2. Socio-Economic Profile of Handloom Sector
sections.content:
* **Largest Cottage Industry:** Employs **over 35 lakh weavers and allied workers**.
* **Women Empowerment:** **Nearly 72%** of handloom weavers and workers in India are **women**.
* **Iconic Traditions:** Bengal Muslin, Banarasi Silk, Kanchipuram Weaves, Pochampally Ikat, Assam's Maina Loom & Sivasagar Chitranjan Handloom, Ambar Charkha.

sections.heading: 3. Key Government Initiatives & "Handloom 4.0"
sections.content: * **Handloom 4.0 Initiative:** Incorporates Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital monitoring tools (e.g. *VisioNXT* trend forecasting platform) across 100 pilot looms to assist weavers with design trends, quality monitoring, and global market linkages. * **National Handloom and Handicraft Programme:** Aims to strengthen 1,800 clusters across >500 districts, directly benefiting 65 lakh artisans. * **Institutional Network:** Supported by 29 Weavers' Service Centres and 11 Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology (IIHT). ---

sections.heading: Topic 4: Police Reforms — Kerala's "My Police Station" Democratic Policing Initiative
sections.content:
> **Headlines:** *"Kerala set to launch project to improve police-citizen ties"* (The Hindu Bureau)  
> **GS Paper:** GS-II (Polity & Governance — Police Reforms, Custodial Violence & Accountability)  
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260807-04`

sections.heading: 1. Core Features of "My Police Station" Project
sections.content:
* **Launch:** August 15, 2026 by Kerala Police.
* **Structural Reform:** Entrusts the position of **Station House Officer (SHO)** to **Sub-Inspectors (SIs)** in 419 out of 484 law-and-order stations (including female SIs as SHOs in 63 police stations). Reverses the earlier practice of assigning Circle Inspectors (CIs) as SHOs.
* **Strategic Exception:** 64 high-importance stations (e.g. Mullaperiyar dam station) will retain higher-ranking officers (DySP / CIs).

sections.heading: 2. Objectives & Governance Relevance
sections.content:
* **Elimination of Custodial Crimes:** Primary mission to eliminate custodial deaths, custodial torture, and arbitrary violence.
* **Empowering Young Leadership:** Direct-recruit SIs handle ground-level station leadership, fostering agility and fresh administrative accountability.
* **Alignment with Police Reforms Commissions:** Aligns with recommendations of the **National Police Commission (1977-81)**, **Padmanabhaiah Committee (2000)**, and SC's ***Prakash Singh Judgment (2006)*** regarding SHO operational clarity, human-rights-centric policing, and community accountability.

sections.heading: Topic 5: Future of Multi-Sport Events — Commonwealth Games (CWG) Governance & India's 2036 Bid
sections.content:
> **Headlines:** *"Should the Commonwealth Games be scrapped?"* (Parley — Debate between Anju Bobby George & Heena Sidhu)

sections.heading: 1. Key Challenges Facing CWG
sections.content:

* **Exclusion of Core Sports:** Scaled-down formats omit key disciplines (Shooting, Badminton, Wrestling, Hockey, Cricket), eroding audience engagement and damaging elite athlete preparation pipelines.

sections.heading: 2. Strategic Perspectives & Recommendations
sections.content:
* **Decentralized Hosting Model:** Experts advocate shifting from single-city host models to **multi-city or regional co-hosting** (similar to the FIFA World Cup format) to utilize existing infrastructure and prevent "white elephant" stadiums.
* **Stepping Stone for India's 2036 Olympic Bid:** Participation and targeted hosting of multi-sport events serve as critical benchmarks for building sports infrastructure, event-management capability, and high-performance training systems for India's **2036 Olympic Hosting Bid**.

sections.heading: Topic 1: DPDP Act 2023 vs RTI Act 2005 — Supreme Court Hearing on Section 44(3)
sections.content:
> **Headlines:** *"Is data protection law crippling RTI, asks SC"*  
> **GS Paper:** GS-II (Polity & Governance — Fundamental Rights, Right to Information vs Right to Privacy, Administrative Transparency)  
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260808-01`

sections.heading: 1. Context & Core Judicial Controversy
sections.content:
* The Supreme Court of India is hearing a batch of petitions challenging provisions of the **Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023**, specifically **Section 44(3)**.
* **Section 44(3) of DPDP Act** amended **Section 8(1)(j)** of the **Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005**, creating a profound legal conflict between public transparency and personal data privacy.

sections.heading: 2. Legal Architecture: Pre-Amendment vs. Post-Amendment Comparison
sections.content:
| Parameter | Original Section 8(1)(j) of RTI Act, 2005 | Amended Section 8(1)(j) via Sec 44(3) DPDP Act |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Scope of Exemption** | Personal information exempted **ONLY IF** it had no relationship to any public activity/interest OR would cause unwarranted invasion of privacy. | **Blanket Exemption:** Blankly exempts all "personal information" from RTI disclosure without qualification. |
| **Public Interest Test** | **Mandatory Balancing Test:** Public Information Officer (PIO) or First Appellate Authority (FAA) had to disclose information if larger public interest justified it. | **Public Interest Exception Abolished:** Discretion of PIO/FAA to weigh public interest against privacy was completely removed. |
| **Impact on Citizen Scrutiny** | Facilitated investigative journalism, anti-corruption inquiries, asset disclosures of public servants, and audit of social welfare lists. | High potential to shield public functionaries and government actions behind the veil of "personal information". |

sections.heading: 3. Key Arguments Presented in Supreme Court
sections.content:
* **Inversion of Fundamental Right to Privacy (*Puttaswamy* Judgment, 2017):**
  * Petitioners submitted that Section 44(3) turns the Right to Privacy on its head.
  * Right to Privacy under [Article 21](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_21.md) was recognized to protect ordinary citizens against State overreach/incursion.
  * The amended RTI provision extends privacy protections to shield the **State and public functionaries** from citizen scrutiny and RTI disclosures.
* **Impact on Investigative Journalism & Public Interest:**
  * Counsel argued that journalists reporting on corruption or administrative malpractices must now seek explicit consent from the "data principal" (the individual concerned).
  * Data principals have the right to request erasure of their data, paralyzing investigative journalism.
* **Supreme Court's Observation on Journalism:**
  * SC explicitly noted that **journalists cannot be treated as a "special category"** with unreserved or unregulated access to personal data, emphasizing the need for legal balance between privacy rights under [Article 21](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_21.md) and press freedom under [Article 19(1)(a)](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_19.md).

---

sections.heading: Topic 2: Strategic Shift in India-U.S. Relations — "Flexible Realism" & Geopolitical Dynamics
sections.content:
> **Headlines:** *"The changing logic of the India-U.S. partnership"* (by Prof. G. Venkat Raman, IIM Indore)  
> **GS Paper:** GS-II (International Relations — Bilateral Relations, Geopolitics, Strategic Autonomy & Quad)  
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260808-02`

sections.heading: 1. Shift from Post-Cold War Liberalism to "Flexible Realism"
sections.content:
* **Foreign Policy Shift:** U.S. foreign policy has evolved away from post-Cold War liberal internationalism toward **"flexible realism"** / transactional realism.
* **Key Characteristics:** Focuses on national interest, tariff negotiations, technology trade restrictions, demands for greater burden-sharing, and bilateral transactional bargains rather than moralistic alliance commitments.
* **Impact on Partners:** U.S. assesses alliances and strategic partnerships less by shared historical/democratic values and more by **tangible economic, technological, and strategic value delivered**.

sections.heading: 2. The China Factor as Strategic Anchor
sections.content:
* **Core Foundation:** The India-U.S. strategic logic over the past decade has been anchored by **China's strategic emergence**.
* **Key Collaboration Pillars:** Defense cooperation, supply-chain resilience, critical and emerging technologies (iCET), and the **Quad (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue)**.
* **Evolution of Logic:** While democratic values provided a favorable backdrop, the convergence of strategic interests driven by China's rise gave the partnership its real momentum.

sections.heading: 3. The Next Phase of Partnership & Strategic Autonomy
sections.content:
* **Redefining Partnership:** India can no longer assume that U.S.-China strategic competition alone will sustain U.S. commitment without India actively strengthening its own defense manufacturing, critical tech capabilities, and reciprocal strategic contributions.
* **Re-conceptualizing Strategic Autonomy:**
  * Strategic autonomy is **NOT about maintaining equal physical/political distance** from competing global powers.
  * It is about **preserving the national capacity to make independent choices** based on India's own long-term interests.
* **Multi-Alignment Framework:** Requires India to actively manage strategic partnership with the U.S. while simultaneously deepening economic, technological, and strategic partnerships with the European Union, Japan, and the Global South, alongside managing relations with China.

sections.heading: 1. Context of the Trilateral Mecca Defence Pact
sections.content:
* **Signing Event:** Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkiye signed a landmark trilateral defence agreement at the **Mecca Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence** in Mecca.
* **Signatories:** Saudi Crown Prince & Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
* **Triad Configuration:** Brings together a **South Asian nuclear power (Pakistan)**, an **oil-rich Persian Gulf power (Saudi Arabia)**, and a **NATO member state (Turkiye)**.

sections.heading: 2. Core Operational Provisions & West Asian Crisis Context
sections.content:
* **"Collective Defence & Deterrence" Clause:** Formally commits all three member nations to **collective defence and deterrence**, declaring that an **armed attack against any one member state will be treated as an attack against all three** (resembling NATO's Article 5 mechanism).
* **Regional Crisis Backdrop:** Signed amidst escalating West Asian security volatility:
  * Unresolved U.S.-Israel military conflict with Iran.
  * Repeated drone/missile attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and Red Sea shipping blockades by Iran-aligned Houthi forces (Ansar Allah).

| Member (Trilateral Mecca Defence Pact) | Strategic Identity | Contribution to the Pact |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Pakistan** | Nuclear power | Troop deployment, nuclear deterrence, military advisory role |
| **Saudi Arabia** | Gulf energy power | Financial capital, energy resources, diplomatic hub |
| **Turkiye** | NATO member state | Defence manufacturing, military hardware/drones, NATO technology |

sections.heading: 3. Questions Over Practical Scope & Strategic Implications
sections.content:
| Dimension | Key Features & Strategic Dynamics | |:---|:---| | **Precedent & Enforcement Gaps** | In Sept 2025, Saudi Arabia & Pakistan signed a Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement. However, neither intervened militarily during Pakistan-Taliban clashes or Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities, raising doubts on operational readiness. | | **Regional Reactions** | **Iran:** Iranian Parliament's National Security Commission criticized the deal, stating it would fail to bring genuine security to Saudi Arabia. | | **Turkiye & Pakistan Ambitions** | Turkiye seeks a dominant security role across West Asia; Pakistan leverages its military & nuclear stature for regional security leverage and Gulf economic support. | | **Implications for India** | • Aligns a hostile neighbor (Pakistan) with major Middle Eastern powers (Saudi Arabia & Turkiye).
• Challenges India's strategic balancing in West Asia (where India maintains strong economic, energy, and diaspora ties with Saudi Arabia/UAE).
• Potential defense-technology transfers between Turkiye and Pakistan. | ---

sections.heading: Topic 1: PMLA Prosecution Post-Predicate Conviction & Double Jeopardy — Karnataka HC Ruling
sections.content:
> **Headlines:** *"PMLA case after conviction for predicate offence doesn't amount to second trial: HC"*  
> **GS Paper:** GS-II (Polity & Governance — Fundamental Rights: Article 20(2), Prevention of Money Laundering Act 2002, Criminal Procedure Code Sec 300)  
> **Micro-Topic ID:** `CA-260811-01`

sections.heading: 1. Context & Judicial Ruling
sections.content:
* The **Karnataka High Court** (single bench of **Justice M. Nagaprasanna**) held that prosecuting an individual under the **Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002** after conviction for a predicate/scheduled offence under the Indian Penal Code (IPC) or other penal laws does **NOT** amount to a second trial for the same offence.
* The ruling dismissed petitions filed by 11 individuals convicted in 2024 for a 2016 demonetisation note-exchange cheating scam (looting people under the guise of exchanging demonetised notes).

sections.heading: 2. Core Legal Principles & Rationale
sections.content:
| Legal Parameter | Constitutional / Statutory Basis | High Court Analysis & Distinction |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Double Jeopardy** | **[Article 20(2)](file:///c:/Users/nitee/OneDrive/Desktop/UPSE_Syllabus/Articles/Article_20.md)** & **Section 300 CrPC** (Section 337 BNSS) | Bars trial and punishment for the **same offence** more than once (*Nemo debet bis vexari*). |
| **PMLA Offence Nature** | **Section 3, PMLA 2002** | Independent statutory offence deriving existence from laundering of **proceeds of crime**, though emanating from the commission of a predicate offence. |
| **Section 300 CrPC Scope** | **Criminal Procedure Code, 1973** | Extends **only** to a second trial for the exact same offence, **not** to prosecution for a distinct statutory offence under a separate enactment. |

sections.heading: 3. Key Takeaways for UPSC
sections.content:
* **Distinct Statutory Offence:** The crime of money laundering (concealment, possession, acquisition, or use of proceeds of crime) is legally distinct from the underlying predicate crime (e.g., forgery, theft, cheating).
* **Constitutional Validity:** PMLA proceedings running concurrently or post-conviction of predicate offences do not violate Article 20(2) or fundamental rights.
