sections.heading: 0. How to study IR (before the board)
sections.content:
IR is the **dynamic** half of GS. After a class on India–Pakistan or West Asia, **tomorrow’s paper can still change the story**. Class cannot teach the future.

| Resource | Role |
|:---|:---|
| **Newspaper** | Primary. Pick **one**: *The Hindu* **or** *Indian Express*. Not both. |
| **Recitals** (monthly current-affairs magazine) | **Revise and memorise** what you already read. It does **not** replace the paper. Year-end compilation also comes. |
| **Class handouts** | These **are** the class notes. No dictation in IR; explanation in class, details on the sheet. |
| **Yellow Book (IR)** | Extra literature if you want more. |

Read the paper as **curiosity** (what is Trump doing; why a Makkah defence pact; why Russia–Ukraine), not as “I must mug every line for the exam.” That expectation is impossible and makes you hate the paper.

**Where IR is tested:** Prelims MCQs (this year’s paper: **Strait of Hormuz** in the US–Iran war; neighbourhood); **GS-II** — **4–5** questions every year; **GS-IV** (morality — Gaza casualties, Hiroshima/Nagasaki); Essay; Personality test.

Two IR faculties: Sandhu Sir (this lecture) and **Dr Sushant Varma**.

---

sections.heading: 1. What IR is
sections.content:
**International Relations (IR) = International Politics = Geopolitics.** Same thing. You cannot read relations between **sovereign** nations without **geography**.

**Examples from class**

| Pair | Geography that decides the politics |
|:---|:---|
| **US–Iran** | **Persian Gulf**; **Strait of Hormuz** (oil/gas trade of the region). |
| **India–Bangladesh** | Bangladesh is not landlocked; it is **India-locked** on three sides, Bay of Bengal on the fourth. Territory is a **bridge** between mainland India and the **Northeast**. Alternative to the **Siliguri Corridor** (**Chicken’s Neck**). |
| **India–Bhutan** | Bhutan is **landlocked**, sandwiched between India and China. Sheet: population about **7 lakh**. If China grabs Bhutanese territory, China gets a run at **Siliguri**. India will not allow that. |

**Definition:** IR is the study of **relations between the states of the world**. Here **state = nation / country**, not Punjab or Karnataka.

**Why study it:** humans have not solved **conflict → war**. Wars destroy life and property (class: Gaza; Russia–Ukraine; US–Iran). Purpose of the subject: **how to resolve conflicts peacefully, prevent war, get interstate peace.**

---

sections.heading: 2. What is a state
sections.content:
A **state** is a political entity with **four necessary features**:

Figure: Sovereignty + territory + population + government. Type of government does not matter for the definition.

**Sovereignty** (Preamble of the Constitution for India): autonomy to make **your own** policies and decisions **without external interference**. **Government in this definition:** any **sovereign** government — democracy (India), dictatorship (North Korea / Kim Jong-un), monarchy (Saudi Arabia / Mohammed bin Salman), military junta (Myanmar), **theocracy** (Iran: a spiritual leader as head of state). Class does **not** care about the type. Only: sovereign government + territory + population. ---

sections.heading: 3. Domestic politics vs international politics
sections.content:
Do **not** use Polity-class rules to read IR. Universities keep **Political Science** and **IR** in different buildings. | | **Domestic politics** | **International politics** | |:---|:---|:---| | Also called | **Intra-state** | **Inter-state** | | Subject | Political Science / your **Polity** lectures | **IR** | | Structure | **Hierarchical authority** (a pyramid) | **Anarchy** = **absence of authority** | | Who is sovereign | The **state**. You as a citizen are **not**. | Every **state** is sovereign. No world government. | | Law | Legislature makes, executive implements, judiciary adjudicates | No world police / PM / court that states must obey | | Basic need | **Rule of law** → security and survival of **persons** | **National security** (*rashtra suraksha*) of the **state** | **Hierarchy in India (class pyramid):** Union Parliament above State Assemblies; President → Vice-President → Council of Ministers / PM → CMs → district → the traffic cop on Pusa Road; CJI / Supreme Court → High Courts → districts. Authority is always a pyramid. The **type** of authority can change (monarchy ↔ democracy ↔ junta); authority **does not disappear** inside a state. **Why obey?** After thousands of years, the lesson: the best way for **human survival and safety** is to live under **rule of law**. That is how you get **rights**. Most basic right: **life**. **Article 21** of the Constitution: protection of life. Supreme Court line used in class: Article 21 is the **heart of Fundamental Rights** — if life is gone, equality, freedom, religion, culture are empty. **Thought experiment:** if every authority vanished overnight — jungle *raj*, survival of the fittest, might is right, **fear**. That nightmare **cannot** happen in domestic politics (a state always has a government). It **is** the **permanent** condition of **international** politics.

Figure: Inside a state, someone can pick up the phone to the police. Between states, nobody comes. Self-help.

---

sections.heading: 4. National security, diplomacy’s limit, hard power
sections.content:
In anarchy, states live in a **self-help** world. They are **afraid / insecure**. The first national interest is **national security** — survival of the **state**.

If China launched a full attack tomorrow, the PM cannot dial a world police. That luxury is **domestic** (Article 21). IR is jungle.

**Two methods class tested**

**1. Diplomacy** — maintain peaceful, friendly relations so the threat shrinks. India **tried** this with China: **Panchsheel** (**Panch** = five, **Sheel** = principles) friendship treaty, **1954**. Slogans of *Hindi-Chini bhai-bhai*. **It did not work.** China attacked in **1962** — betrayal of the treaty. You cannot **force** friendship. Diplomacy **may or may not** work. It is **not fail-safe**.

**2. Power** — fail-safe in a self-help world: **become the fittest**. More power → more security.

**Hard power** = **military power + economic power**.

- Military: army, navy, air force, guns, nuclear weapons, missiles, fighters, tanks, carriers, submarines.  
- Empty pockets cannot buy that → **economic** power is required.

Class: if India had **nuclear weapons in 1962**, would China have dared. If Iran had them, would the US have struck.

So **every sovereign state is power-hungry** — **power maximisation**.

---

sections.heading: 5. Finite resources → struggle for power → war
sections.content: All power resources are **finite** (this is **not** an Environment lecture on carbon; even **solar** needs **panels** made of **critical minerals**). Territory is finite. **More territory → more resources.** China dominates **critical minerals / rare earths** — that **is** power. **IR, alternative definition:** IR **is** the **struggle for power**. Unresolved conflicts → **wars**. | Conflict | Power resource in the fight | |:---|:---| | **India–Pakistan / Kashmir** | Territory; **Indus** and tributaries. India **upstream**, Pakistan **downstream**. Water = drink, irrigation, industry. **Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK)** = Indian territory illegally held. | | **India–China 1962** | Territory — **Aksai Chin** (class: China captured this; more land = more power). | | **US–Iran (2026)** | Oil and gas of the **Persian Gulf**; whoever holds the **Strait of Hormuz** holds the trade. | | **Russia–Ukraine** | Many reasons (including **NATO** eastward expansion). Geography class stressed: Russia’s hunt for **warm-water ports** (north coast frozen) → east Ukraine / **Black Sea**. | | **Pax Silica** (US initiative in the papers) | Counter **China’s** hold on **critical minerals / rare earth** supply chains. | **Viksit Bharat by 2047** in this lecture is also a **power** story: health, education, jobs, highways, ports, manufacturing, exports — all need **finite** energy and minerals. **Prelims trap:** Geopolitics is not a synonym for “maps for fun.” **Siliguri / Chicken’s Neck**, **Hormuz**, **Aksai Chin**, **Indus upstream** are the IR facts. **Pax Silica** is a **minerals** counter to China, not a peace slogan. ---

sections.heading: 6. Two theories: realism and idealism
sections.content:
Full IR theory is **optional (PSIR)**. For GS, lock **two** lenses.

| | **Realism** | **Idealism** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Starting point | Study **reality**: IR **is** power struggle | In an **ideal** world, states **would cooperate** |
| Cooperation | **Rejects** it — power-hungry states cannot share the cake | Peaceful dialogue, diplomacy, **multilateralism** |
| Prescription | **Balance of Power (BOP)** | **Collective security** + international organisations + law |
| Mood | Pessimistic but diagnostic | Hope for peace (class: do not dump this) |

**Zero-sum** (sheet, circled): **my gain = the other’s loss.** Realist reading of finite power.

Nobody **wants** war — war makes you **poorer**. Last option. Conflicts are inevitable under power struggle; **wars** happen when conflicts stay **unresolved**. Avoid war by **resolving conflicts peacefully** = **cooperation** (talk, negotiate, diplomacy). Diplomacy = **art and science of maintaining peaceful / friendly relations**.

---

sections.heading: 7. Multilateralism, organisations, treaties
sections.content:
| Count of partners | Name |
|:---|:---|
| 2 | **Bilateral** |
| 3 | **Trilateral** |
| 4 | **Quadrilateral** |
| Many | **Multilateral** |

**Unilateral** = I am sovereign, I will not factor others (class: Russia into Ukraine; US killing an Iranian leader; Trump leaving the **Paris** climate deal).

**No unilateral fix** for **global** problems (climate, terrorism, Covid). Atmosphere does not take a visa. Himalayan melt → Nepal **and** downstream **India** (floods, rivers, food).

**International organisations** exist to **run multilateralism** and to **mediate**.

| Body | Class use |
|:---|:---|
| **United Nations (UN)** | **193** members. Best example of multilateralism. |
| **World Trade Organization (WTO)** | Trade dispute → don’t start a tariff war; use the org. |
| **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**, **World Bank** | Finance / mediation |

**Treaty** = agreement of **two** states. **Convention** = **many** states.

| Instrument | Point |
|:---|:---|
| **UNFCCC** | United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change — cut carbon. |
| **UNCLOS** | United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea — **maritime** disputes (sea territory). |
| **Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), 1960** | India–Pakistan share of Indus and tributaries. **World Bank mediated** (*madhyasthata*). Class: **65 years** of peace on **water war**. Class wording: India **suspended** it in **2025** after **Pahalgam**. **MEA (Ministry of External Affairs)** wording after the **22 April 2025** Pahalgam attack: treaty placed **“in abeyance.”** Detail in the Pakistan lecture. |

**International law** = treaties and conventions between sovereign states. If they are respected → **rule-based order** in international politics (common rules).

**Two stages**

1. **Signing** — expression of **intent** (PM signing Paris). **Not** yet legally binding.  
2. **Ratification** — take it to **your legislature** (Lok Sabha / Rajya Sabha). Then it is a **legal obligation**. Violating a ratified treaty is violating **your own** Constitution / authority.

States stay sovereign: they can **de-ratify**. Class: **US signed UNCLOS but has not ratified** — no legal obligation. India has signed some treaties it has **not** ratified.

sections.heading: Update — 5 September 2026 (*The Hindu* — Tommy Koh on UNCLOS; not a new topic)
sections.content: Same convention as class (sign ≠ ratify; US unsigned-into-force). Interview: **Tommy Koh** (president, Third UN Conference on the Law of the Sea, **1982**; Ramon Magsaysay award). - **172** parties — “near universal.” Koh: no need for a **“UNCLOS IV.”** Still the **“constitution of oceans.”** - **Ronald Reagan** blocked on **Part XI** (deep seabed = **common heritage of mankind** — against free-enterprise / private-property). A **1994** fix to Part XI exists; the **United States of America (USA) still has not ratified**. It treats UNCLOS as **authoritative customary law**. - **Iran** is not a party. **Transit passage** (class / paper: **Strait of Hormuz**; also **Malacca–Singapore**) is **customary international law** → binds non-parties too. - South China Sea / Indian Ocean **Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)** and seabed disputes: core architecture “holding.” **“Dark fleet”** (unregulated / sanctioned shipping) on the high seas → take it to the **International Maritime Organization (IMO)**. **Prelims trap:** UN is **not** a world government. Creating a world government would mean India is **not** sovereign. Orgs are **tools of sovereign states**. Signing ≠ ratification.

sections.heading: Newspaper update — 1 September 2026 (*The Hindu*; Kallol Bhattacherjee)
sections.content: Same IWT file as class — **do not duplicate** as a new CA topic. * **Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA), The Hague** (Court of Arbitration chaired by **Prof. Sean D. Murphy**, US): treaty remains **“fully in force”**; India must observe obligations on **Western Rivers** hydro-electric design and operation. Terror attacks, in the court’s view, do **not** justify suspension or termination. * **India’s rejection:** MEA calls it a **“so-called award”** of an **illegally constituted** court; World Bank’s constitution of the body is a **“grave violation” / “patent breach”** of the treaty. India **will not appear** and will **not take cognisance** of its pronouncements. Abeyance after **Pahalgam (22 April 2025)** **remains in force** (India’s position). * **Ratle Hydro-Electric Plant (RHEP):** “Award on the Status of the IWT and Order on Interim Measures.” India is prohibited from **concreting the dam wall and power intake** above set levels until **90 days after** a **Neutral Expert’s** final decision (expected **July 2027**). **Prelims trap:** PCA says IWT is **in force**; India says it is **in abeyance**. Class said **suspended**. Neutral Expert on Ratle is **July 2027**, then **+90 days** on the concreting bar — not a 2026 finish. ---

sections.heading: 8. Balance of Power (realism)
sections.content:
Realism: you cannot **abolish** power struggle. You can **manage** it so the world is less bloody. **Balance of Power (BOP):** **rough equilibrium** of power. No one state **dominates**. Less imbalance → less insecurity → fewer conflicts → fewer wars. **Counterbalance** in the newspaper = **trying to achieve BOP** (India vs China). **China ~5× India** (class illustration) → India **must** feel insecure. Hypothetical **equal** power → both less jumpy. **Two methods** (can be **both**):

Figure: Internal = grow stronger at home. External = borrow strength through friends. States often do both.

**Internal balancing → arms race:** competition for more weapons. Class story: weak IAF / “flying coffins” (MiGs) vs Pakistan **F-16s** and Chinese jets → **Tejas** (Hindustan Aeronautics Limited), **Prachand** attack helicopter, **Sukhoi**, **Rafale**, **Apache**. China putting **S-400** on the **Ladakh** side is the same logic. **Make in India** / a bigger economy is also internal balancing (class numbers were illustrative: China as a much larger GDP). **External balancing → alliances.** Bhutan cannot match China internally. Bhutan can call **India**; India has a **self-interest** (Siliguri). Sheet boxes **BRICS** and **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)** as grouping examples. Recent **Makkah defence pact** (Saudi) = BOP, because a sane state will **not** bet **only** on the UN. ---

sections.heading: 9. Collective security (idealism)
sections.content: Idealism’s **rival** to BOP: **collective security**. **Woodrow Wilson**, US President, **Fourteen Points** speech in the **US Congress** after **World War I**. US legislature: **Upper House = Senate**, **Lower House = House of Representatives** (sheet: “common”). **Pledge:** all nations defend each other. **All for one, one for all.** An attack on one is an attack on all → **collective** punishment. **Instrument:** **League of Nations** — a common platform to take that oath. **It failed.** **World War II** still happened. Why (class): 1. **The US did not join.** Wilson wanted to sign; **Congress refused** — depending on an international org would **compromise US sovereignty**; America should secure itself. The country that **invented** the League stayed out → dead on arrival. 2. **Interwar period (1919–1939):** Britain and France had **more faith in BOP** (arms races, alliances) than in collective security. League was **toothless**. **Second attempt:** **United Nations, 1945**, after WWII. Same **collective-security** assumption. **Simultaneous** with BOP in the real world (sheet: “simultaneous implementation”; “more confidence in BOP”). UN has **successes and failures**. Wars still happen. Class: UN often **does nothing** when principles are broken (Russia–Ukraine, US, Israel/Gaza). Experts: **talking shop** — speeches in **New York**, then war at home. States remain **sovereign**. **UN Security Council (UNSC):** organ meant to **run** collective security. **P5** (permanent five) with **veto**: **US, Russia, China, Britain, France**. They **misuse** veto. India wants **permanent membership** and **UNSC reform** — **Dr Sushant Varma** will do the UN lecture. If UN is not reformed it risks the League’s fate: **lose relevance**. **Do not drop idealism.** Realism diagnoses; idealism is the **hope** of cooperation. GS needs **both**. The world runs **BOP and collective security at the same time**. **Prelims trap:** League failed **before** WWII, not because of WWII’s start date alone — **US absence + European BOP habits**. UN (1945) is the **second** try, not the first world government. **P5 veto** is why “UN will save us” is not a security policy. ---

Class drill: **Operation Sindoor** / Pahalgam → Jammu and Kashmir police under the Lieutenant Governor (not the Chief Minister) → internal security / terrorism → communal tension → drones and satellites (Science and Technology) → root in **1947 / two-nation theory** (History).
4. **Dynamic** — “you cannot step in the same river twice.” Supplement class with the newspaper.
5. **Revision** — “survival of the revision.” Before class: revise yesterday; read tomorrow’s **handout** (uploaded a day before).

**Answer writing:** Mains is the Test match; Prelims is the One-Day; interview is T20. Appear for Prelims only when Mains-ready (**minimum four revisions** + answer practice).

sections.heading: 1. Origin of the United Nations (IR-02-01)
sections.content:
**United Nations Organisation (UNO / UN)** = international organisation formed at the **end of the Second World War**.

**Four fundamental objectives** (class order):

| # | Objective | How (class) |
|:---:|:---|:---|
| 1 | Maintain **international peace and security** | **Collective security** = *all for one and one for all*; punish the aggressor. Protect future generations from the “scourge of war.” |
| 2 | Uphold respect for **international law** | — |
| 3 | Protect **human rights (HR)** | Rights available **by virtue of being born as a human** — inalienable; race / sex / tribe do not matter. |
| 4 | Ensure **progress** of humanity | Development, later widened (Human Development Index, Sustainable Development Goals). |

**Blueprint:** **San Francisco Conference, April–June 1945**. **50** founding members → **193** members now.

**Came into existence: 24 October 1945** = **UN Day** (UN’s birthday).

**India** was a **founding member** among the 50 — still a **British colony** in 1945; the British allowed it. India was also a founding member of the **League of Nations**.

**Predecessor:** **League of Nations, 1919**, after the **First World War**. It could not stop the Second World War. Framers of the UN tried to fix those weaknesses.

**Human rights as a 1945 idea:** the world saw the **Holocaust** — systematic killing of **6 million Jews**. Aristotle (class): *without laws and order, humans are the worst of animals.* Homework movie: **Schindler’s List**.

**How class will cover the UN (five themes):**

1. Origin  
2. Structure  
3. Assessment → **criticism** + **achievements**  
4. Reform of the UN  
5. India and the UN  

---

sections.heading: 2. Six principal organs (IR-02-02)
sections.content:
A modern state has legislature–executive–judiciary. The UN has **six principal organs** plus specialised agencies, funds and programmes. **Five** are headquartered in **New York**. Only the **International Court of Justice (ICJ)** sits at **The Hague**, Netherlands.

Figure: United Nations Security Council binds; General Assembly recommends. International Court of Justice is the only principal organ not in New York.

sections.heading: 2.1 United Nations Security Council (UNSC)
sections.content: **Executive.** Primary organ for **international peace and security**. Decisions are **legally binding** on all members.

sections.heading: 2.2 United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)
sections.content:
**Not** the legislature (it does not make binding law). **Deliberative** body — discussion of issues of international importance; passes **resolutions** that are **recommendations**. Sometimes called the **World Parliament**.

**Most democratic organ:** **one country, one vote, one value** — United States and Nepal weigh the same. All **193** members sit here.

sections.heading: Update — 14 September 2026 (UPSC CSE Prelims 2022)
sections.content: `CSE-2022-Q78` **missed** (`MST-092`). Official key = **all three**. The UN General Assembly can grant **observer status** to **non-member States**. **Inter-governmental organisations** can seek observer status. **Permanent Observers** can **maintain missions** at UN headquarters. Class lock still: UNGA is **deliberative**, not binding law. He picked **2 and 3 only** (dropped statement 1).

sections.heading: 2.3 International Court of Justice (ICJ)
sections.content: **Judicial** wing. Detail in §5.

sections.heading: 2.4 Secretariat
sections.content:
UN **bureaucracy** — services the principal organs. Headed by the **Secretary-General (SG)** = **public face** of the UN.

- Appointed by the **General Assembly** on the **recommendation of the Security Council**.
- Term: **5 years**; can serve **more than one** 5-year term.
- Current: **António Guterres** (Portugal). **January 2027** — a new SG; class: most probably from **Latin America**.
- **14 Sep *Hindu* extra (maps, not a new UN lecture):** Guterres — **“There is no such thing as a ‘UN map with borders’.”** Website sheet = **NGO / indicative**. Full lock: `Current_Affairs/September_2026/2026-09-08_Current_Affairs.md` (**CA-260908-02**). No extra Day-1.
- **Shashi Tharoor** contested; candidature **not supported by the United States**.

sections.heading: 2.5 Trusteeship Council
sections.content:
Set up to manage **11 trust territories** (many ex-colonies of Germany). By **1994** they had become independent or merged. **No work since 1994.**

**Reform suggestion:** give it **global commons** — a resource that belongs to all humanity. Class examples: **outer space**, **international waters / seas**.

sections.heading: 2.6 Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)
sections.content:
Manages the UN’s **economic and social** work. **54 members**, elected by the General Assembly. **Supervises specialised agencies**.

---

sections.heading: 3. Specialised agencies, funds and programmes (IR-02-03)
sections.content:
Work in a **particular domain**. Class named four.

| Body | Full form / role (class) | Prelims hooks |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **UNESCO** | United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization | **World Heritage sites**; **Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** |
| **WHO** | World Health Organization | **Pandemic Pact**; health **standards** (e.g. Oral Rehydration Solution formula) |
| **ILO** | International Labour Organization | Was part of the **League of Nations**; joined the UN family when the League died; HQ **Geneva**; labour standards |
| **UNDP** | United Nations Development Programme | Annual **Human Development Index (HDI)** ranking |

**United States under Donald Trump pulled out of UNESCO and WHO** — hits their **funding**.

sections.heading: 3.1 UNESCO — India hooks
sections.content:
**World Heritage sites in India: 45.** Latest entry (class): **Sarnath** — where the Buddha gave his **first sermon** after enlightenment.

Know **your state’s** sites for interview. Class named: Delhi (Red Fort, Qutub Minar); Karnataka (Hampi); Tamil Nadu (Mahabalipuram, Brihadisvara / Thanjavur); Assam (**Ahom burial sites**, last year); Maharashtra (**12 Maratha forts**, Ajanta–Ellora).

**Intangible heritage** = cultural **practices**. Latest from India on the sheet: **Deepawali**. Before that: **Durga Puja**. Also on the list: **Garba** (Gujarat), **Kumbh**. Government talking to others for **Chhath Puja** (eastern India / Uttar Pradesh — worships **rising and setting** sun). India–China (as **BRICS** partners) talking a **joint nomination** of **Xuanzang’s** work. A Kerala Sanskrit drama performed for **a thousand years** — homework: read India’s UNESCO intangible list.

sections.heading: 3.2 WHO
sections.content: **Pandemic Pact** (last year) — future pandemics, including **vaccine sharing**. Watches public-health emergencies: **Ebola** in the **Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)** (high fatality). Sets **health standards**.

sections.heading: 3.3 ILO and child labour
sections.content: India’s child-labour laws are in tune with the ILO convention; India is a **signatory**. Constitution: **Article 23** (class correction — not Article 22).

sections.heading: 3.4 UNDP and Human Development Index
sections.content:
UN **broadened development** beyond **per capita income** → **human development**.

**Three HDI criteria (class):** quality of life, **health**, **education**.

Top slot: **Scandinavia** (Norway, Denmark, Sweden) — not the United States. In South Asia: **Sri Lanka** and **Bangladesh** beat **India**. Inside India: **Kerala** highest (class: comparable to Western standards). **Last year two states hit 100% literacy: Himachal Pradesh and Mizoram** — class: their HDI will beat **Rajasthan** and **Bihar**.

---

sections.heading: 4. Security Council: membership, voting, actions (IR-02-04, IR-02-05)
sections.content: Three things to learn: **membership**, **voting**, **actions**.

sections.heading: 4.1 Membership
sections.content:
**15** members = **Permanent Five (P5)** + **10 non-permanent**.

**P5 (always there):** **United States, United Kingdom, Russia, China, France** — victorious powers of the Second World War. They designed an **exalted** status for themselves.

**Non-permanent:** elected by the **General Assembly** for a **2-year term**, on a **regional** basis. A sitting non-permanent member is **not eligible for immediate re-election**.

**India:** non-permanent member **8 times**; now wants a **permanent** seat.

**Current Asia seat:** **Pakistan** is a non-permanent member; tenure ends **31 December 2026** — so Pakistan **cannot** seek immediate re-election. India is competing for the next Asia non-permanent seat; **Tajikistan** is also in the race (class: Prime Minister’s Central Asia visit).

sections.heading: 4.2 Voting on **substantive** matters
sections.content:
Substantive = important = **maintenance of international peace and security**. Rules sit in the **UN Charter** (constitution of the UN).

Two conditions:

1. **9 out of 15** must say yes.
2. **No negative vote by a P5** = **veto**.

The word **veto is not in the Charter**. The Charter says the Council cannot decide without the **concurrence of the P5**.

**Three options** for any member (permanent or not): **yes / no / abstain**.

**Abstention by a P5 is not a veto.**

| Class example | What happened |
|:---|:---|
| Ukraine ceasefire, **14–1**, the “no” is **Russia** | Condition 1 met (14 ≥ 9); condition 2 fails → **veto → end of the matter** |
| **Trump Gaza Peace Plan**, November 2025 | Passed; **Russia and China abstained** (P5 abstention ≠ veto). Binding on all members |
| History of **US** vetoes | Class: **about half** used to protect **Israel** |
| **Soviet Union, 1971** | Veto to protect **India’s interest on Jammu and Kashmir** |

sections.heading: 4.3 Actions — Chapter VI, “6½”, Chapter VII
sections.content:
Figure: Chapter VI talks; Chapter VII hits; “Chapter 6½” is a UN invention sitting in between.

**Chapter VI — peaceful resolution of disputes:** negotiation, **arbitration**, mediation. **India–Pakistan / Jammu and Kashmir:** India took the matter to the Security Council. Council invoked Chapter VI and appointed **United Nations Commission for India and Pakistan (UNCIP)** to mediate. **Ceasefire 1 January 1949**; under UN military observers the **ceasefire line** was drawn — later the **Line of Control (LoC)**. **Chapter VII — coercive:** authorise **use of force**, **economic sanctions**, **arms ban**. **North Korea:** first use of **collective security**, **1950**. North Korean troops had taken **Seoul**. An international force under the **UN flag**, **led by the United States**, pushed them back. **North and South Korea are still technically at war** (no peace treaty). Boundary: **38th parallel** — one of the most heavily militarised lines. Later: sanctions and arms bans over the **nuclear** programme. Leader: **Kim Jong-un**. **“Chapter 6½” — United Nations Peacekeeping Missions (UNPKM):** a Secretary-General’s phrase. **Midway** between VI and VII. **The word “peacekeeping” is not in the Charter** — an **innovation**. Troops (**blue helmets**, mixed nationalities) go **with the parties’ consent** to hold a ceasefire. They may use force **only in self-defence**. Class: **Colonel Sofiya Qureshi** (army brief after Operation Sindoor) has served on a UN peacekeeping mission from India. ---

sections.heading: 5. Three courts in The Hague (IR-02-06)
sections.content:
Newspaper will throw three names. **All three sit in The Hague.** Decisions of all three are **legally binding** on the parties they bind — **none has its own enforcement police**. Weight = **international legitimacy**. For the ICJ, enforcement sits with the **Security Council** (and can be **vetoed**).

| | **ICJ** | **PCA** | **ICC** |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Full name | International Court of Justice | Permanent Court of Arbitration | International Criminal Court |
| UN body? | **Yes** | **No** | **No** |
| Age | Principal organ, 1945 | **Oldest** international court — **Hague Conventions 1899 and 1907** | **Newest** — **Rome Statute 1998**, court from **2002** |
| Who can approach | **Only governments** | **Governments and private parties** | Prosecutes **individuals** |
| Job | Settle **disputes** + **advisory** opinions to UN organs | Arbitration (class: **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)** cases) | Four crimes (below) |
| Binding? | Dispute judgment **legally binding**; **advice non-binding** | Binding on parties | Binding on members / situations it covers |
| Enforcement | **No.** Power is with the **Security Council** | No own enforcement | No own army |

sections.heading: 5.1 ICJ jurisdiction — two doors
sections.content:
Country A can drag B only if:

1. **Voluntary jurisdiction** — the other party **also agrees** (A vs B).  
   **1984 United States vs Nicaragua** (Central America). Both went; ICJ found **against the US**; US **refused** to comply; ICJ **cannot punish**; Nicaragua went to the Security Council; the **US vetoed**.

2. **Compulsory jurisdiction** — a **treaty** both signed says ICJ will settle disputes under that treaty.  
   **December 2023: South Africa vs Israel** on the **1948 Genocide Convention** (in force **1951**; motto *never again* after the Holocaust). Both are parties → Israel **had to appear**. Class figure used by South Africa: **72,000+** killed in Gaza as genocide. Judgment, when it comes, is binding; enforcement still needs the Council.

Homework: **Kulbhushan Jadhav** — India invoked **compulsory** ICJ jurisdiction after Pakistan’s military court death sentence.

sections.heading: 5.2 PCA — India–Bangladesh 2014
sections.content:
**2014 India–Bangladesh maritime** (not land) boundary — **UNCLOS**. PCA decision **binding**. India **lost some maritime space**, could have appealed, **chose not to** (good ties; **Sheikh Hasina** then). Land boundary is the **100th Constitutional Amendment**, not this case.

Class also: a **PCA** verdict on the **Indus Waters Treaty** a few days before this lecture — **India rejected** it (India did not participate). Comes back in the Pakistan lecture.

South China Sea / UNCLOS promised in **Lecture 3**.

sections.heading: 5.3 ICC — four crimes, who is out
sections.content:
Prosecutes an **individual** if his own government will not, for:

1. **War crimes**  
2. **Genocide**  
3. **Crimes against humanity**  
4. **Crime of aggression**

**124** countries have signed. **Not members:** **United States, Russia, China, India, Israel**.

**Arrest warrants** (class, last year) against **Vladimir Putin** and the **Israeli Prime Minister** — they are not members, but the alleged crimes were on the territory of **members** (**Ukraine**, **Palestine**). If the ICC asks India to arrest Putin: India says **the decision does not apply — India is not a member**.

**Rodrigo Duterte** (former Philippines President) on trial at The Hague for **crimes against humanity** (anti-drug campaign; many civilians died).

---

sections.heading: 6. Assessment — first three weak, fourth strong (IR-02-07)
sections.content: Judge the UN on the **four founding objectives**. Class verdict after ~80 years: **poor on peace, law, and human rights**; **impressive on progress**.

sections.heading: 6.1 Peace and security
sections.content:
**Supporters:** no **Third World War**. The League failed that test.

**Critics:** that is **not** the UN’s achievement. Cold War stayed cold because of the **balance of terror** / **Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD)** — **nuclear deterrence**. **1962 Cuban Missile Crisis** — President **John F. Kennedy** chose diplomacy over a first strike (class: no winners in a nuclear war; Hiroshima–Nagasaki). **Full Sandhu chain (9 Sep):** bipolar / NAM / MAD / proxy / NPT → `03_World_Order_After_WW2.md` (**IR-03**).

**Veto paralysis — Cold War:** **1960s Vietnam** (aggressor: US); **1979 Afghanistan** (aggressor: Soviet Union). UN did not rescue either.

**Veto paralysis — after the Cold War:** **Gaza (2023–)** and **Ukraine (2022–)**. UN has not punished **Israel** or **Russia** (US / Russian veto).

sections.heading: 6.2 International law
sections.content:
**2003 Iraq:** US sought Council authorisation to invade on **weapons of mass destruction (WMD)** charges against **Saddam Hussein**. **Russia, France, China** were not convinced. US invaded **unilaterally** — **Kofi Annan**: violation of international law (only the Council can authorise force, as in **Korea 1950**). **No WMD found.** Class: real aim was **oil**. **Matsyanyaya** — big fish eats the small fish (US / Iraq); UN as bystander.

Class current illustrations of the same “might is right”: **Venezuela**; **Strait of Hormuz** / **UNCLOS** freedom of navigation.

sections.heading: Update — 5 September 2026 (*The Hindu* — Tommy Koh; not a new topic)
sections.content: Same UNCLOS / Hormuz file as Lecture 1–2. **Tommy Koh**: transit passage is **customary law** (binds **Iran**, a non-party). **172** parties; USA still unratified over **Part XI / common heritage**. Full clip on `01_Basics_of_International_Relations.md`.

sections.heading: 6.3 Human rights — two glaring misses
sections.content:
| Case | What class said |
|:---|:---|
| **Rwanda, 1994** | Ethnic cleansing: **Hutus vs Tutsis**. **8 lakh** killed. Memorial of skulls in **Kigali**. **Emmanuel Macron** later asked forgiveness — France could have stopped it and did not. France is **P5**. |
| **East Pakistan, 1971** | Pakistani army **Operation Searchlight** against Bengali-speakers. **1 crore** refugees into India. **Indira Gandhi** met **Richard Nixon** — he made her wait, threatened her, used racist language. Pakistan was a **Cold War ally** of the US. Class: rape used as a weapon; **1 million** Bangladeshi women. UN did not protect them. |

sections.heading: 6.4 Housekeeping criticism
sections.content: **Financial crunch** (US pull-out from UNESCO / WHO shrinks operations), **corruption**, **complex procedures**.

sections.heading: 6.5 Achievements — why the UN is still relevant
sections.content:
1. **It survived.** The League died; the UN is still the table.
2. **Broadened development** — **HDI** and **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** (**17** goals, target year **2030**). Sustainable = environment-friendly **and** needs of **future generations**.
3. **Platform** for **193** countries on **global challenges**:

| Challenge | UN hook (class) |
|:---|:---|
| **Climate change** | **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**; **Conference of the Parties 30 (COP-30)** in **Brazil**. Hold warming below **1.5 °C**. **Global South** faces the brunt; Nepal spoke of **compensation**. |
| **Terrorism** | Security Council **1267 Sanctions Committee** — designates individuals / groups as global terrorists; all states must act. Class: **Hafiz Saeed** (**Lashkar-e-Taiba**), **Masood Azhar** (**Jaish-e-Mohammed**). Pakistan was forced to move. |
| **Pandemic** | **WHO** (COVID and the next one), despite weaknesses. |

**Necessity is the mother of invention:** if the UN did not exist, the world would have to invent something like it.

---

sections.heading: 7. Reform of the UN (IR-02-08)
sections.content:
Many reforms need an **amendment of the Charter**.

**Two steps (class):**

1. Approved by **two-thirds of the General Assembly** — **128 of 193**.
2. Approved by the **parliaments of two-thirds of members, including all P5**.

**No amendment against the wish of any P5.** That is a **virtual veto** on the Charter itself.

**Three privileges that make P5 a VIP club:** always present; **veto** on Council decisions; **veto** on Charter amendment. The Council is **not** “one member, one vote, one value.”

**Four pillars of reform (sheet):**

1. **UNSC** — fix the **democratic deficit** (membership + veto). Suggestions: **abolish the veto** (no P5 will agree) or, more practical, **majority among P5** (class: **3–2** instead of unanimity).
2. **UNGA** — **binding recommendations** on some matters (give it teeth).
3. **Financial reform** — more money so operations do not shrink.
4. **Quick / good deployment ability** — send troops **fast**; every second of conflict costs lives.

**External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar (class):** P5 membership is **frozen in the world of 1945**. Britain and France are declining; the **sun has set** on the empire. Missing: class’s **3rd / 4th / 6th** largest economies (**Germany, Japan, India**). P5 is a **predominantly white club** (only **China** is not). **Europe** (smallest continent) has **three** permanent seats (Russia, France, UK). **Asia** has **one**. **Africa** and **Latin America** have **zero**.

sections.heading: 7.1 G4 vs Coffee Club / Uniting for Consensus (UFC)
sections.content:
| | **G4** | **Coffee Club / UFC** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Who | **Japan, India, Brazil, Germany** — four **aspirants** for a permanent seat | Regional **rivals**: **Italy** (vs Germany), **Argentina** (vs Brazil), **Pakistan** (vs India), **South Korea** (vs Japan). Sheet also: **Spain**. Official name **Uniting for Consensus**. Nickname from the **Italian** ambassador calling rivals for **coffee** (also **Cappuccino Club**) |
| Size | **15 → 24 or 26** | **15 → 25** (10 new) |
| New seats | **6 new permanent** + **4 or 5 non-permanent** | **Only non-permanent or semi-permanent** — **no new permanent**, **no veto** |
| How the 6 P split (G4) | **2 Asia** (India, Japan); **2 Africa** (three claimants: **South Africa, Nigeria, Egypt**); **1 Latin America** (Brazil); **1 Europe** (Germany) | — |
| Veto | Undemocratic — **abolish**; **but if veto stays, G4 wants it too** | Forget veto |

**Semi-permanent (Coffee Club):** a member that can be **re-elected for consecutive terms** — today’s rule **blocks** immediate re-election.

**Kite-string point:** members **hold the string**. Weaknesses are **designed** — nobody gives an organisation more power than they will accept (accountability / privacy analogy: Article 21).

---

sections.heading: 8. India and the UN (IR-02-08)
sections.content:
Line from class: **either you are on the table or you are on the menu.** India learned that in **1948** on **Jammu and Kashmir** — others decided. India wants to **hold the string**.

Two grounds for a **permanent seat**:

sections.heading: 8.1 Credentials
sections.content:
- World’s **largest democracy** and **largest population** — a permanent seat = **one-sixth of humanity** at the table; cuts the democratic deficit.
- **6th largest economy.**
- **Responsible nuclear-weapon state** — class: unlike Pakistan, India has **not sold** nuclear technology; non-proliferation record is **impeccable**.
- **Rich civilisational legacy** — **Buddha, Ashoka, Gandhi**; shelter to the persecuted (**Parsis** from Iran; **Maharaja of Nawanagar** took in Polish children in the Second World War — streets in Poland named after him). **21 June** International Yoga Day.

sections.heading: 8.2 Rich contribution
sections.content:
- **Founding member** (and of the League).
- Always pushed **multilateralism** over unilateralism; strengthen the UN.
- One of the **largest contributors** to **United Nations Peacekeeping Forces (UNPKF)** — **blue helmets**; **first country to send an all-women contingent**; lives lost in the line of duty. This year: **Major Abhilasha Barak**, UN Mission in **Lebanon**, **UN Gender Advocate Award**. **Colonel Sofiya Qureshi** also a peacekeeper.
- **Voice of the Global South** (ex-colonies / developing countries): **decolonisation**; **neo-colonialism** (class: Venezuela, rename games, Greenland); **apartheid** (**Nelson Mandela** — Bharat Ratna); **nuclear disarmament** (even as a nuclear-weapon state); **climate finance** (rich countries polluted first; they fund adaptation / mitigation in the South).

sections.heading: 8.3 Challenges to India’s bid
sections.content:
1. **China** — the one P5 that has **not** supported India. Other **four P5 have**. **Shyam Saran** (ex-Foreign Secretary): China sees India as an **inferior power** and will not allow **power parity**. Class line: aspirations have hit the **Great Wall**. China’s Coffee Club friend: **Pakistan**.
2. **Coffee Club** — can block the **two-thirds** in the General Assembly.
3. **Status-quo bias among P5** — even supporters know **nothing moves without China**; cheap to “support” India on paper.

**East vs West** inside the Council: **China + Russia** vs **United States**. They do not want a **pro-Western** new permanent (they **rejected Japan** — **G7**). Gaza / Ukraine votes split the same way.

**BRICS** (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa — **18th** summit **New Delhi, 12–13 September 2026**, India chair): demand **reform of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Bank** (UN specialised-family money bodies). **West dominates:** World Bank President is **always appointed by the US President**; IMF cannot move without the **US** (largest shareholder). India and China want voice matching weight.

sections.heading: Update — 13 September 2026 (*Hindu* New Delhi Declaration — no extra Day-1)
sections.content:
Declaration **adopted 12 Sep**. Clip: **comprehensive UN reform**; **greater role for Brazil and India** in the **UNSC**. Full text / West Asia language / MSME: `Current_Affairs/September_2026/2026-09-06_Current_Affairs.md` (`CA-260906-02`). Class G4 vs Coffee Club lock **stays** — the declaration names **Brazil and India**, not the full G4.

**If the UN does not reform**, legitimacy may shift to **G20 / BRICS**. Reform so the UN reflects **2026 power**, not **1945**.

**What India should do (class close):** stay invested; keep **diplomatic** work to build opinion. Next class: **India–China**. Sources enough for GS: **class + handouts + Yellow Book + current affairs**.

sections.heading: Lecture 3 — 9 September 2026
sections.content:
> **Date of Lecture:** 9 September 2026 (Sandhu Sir, after Lecture 1 on 1 September). **Dr Sushant Varma** UN class (4 September) stays `02_United_Nations_Organisation.md`.  
> **Date Added:** 2026-09-09  
> **Teacher:** **Iqbal Singh Sandhu** (GS International Relations)  
> **Source:** Vajiram & Ravi class + audio transcript + 6 handwritten notebook pages (dated **9/9/26**, circled **2–6**; page 1 is the WW2 / NATO–Warsaw opener)  
> **Already elsewhere:** **Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD)** as a UN-assessment critic is in IR-02. **Naxalbari / Naxalism** (1967, “too early” to call Naxal-free) is in Internal Security L1. This file is the **world-order** chain.  
> **Parked — next class:** evolution of **Indian foreign policy** (Nehru non-alignment → Modi multi-alignment) + India as soft power. Bring **IR handout number 2**.  
> **How to read class shortcuts:** full form on first use. Glossary at the end.

**World order** = nature of international politics in a **period**. It is **not static**. No permanent friends or enemies (class: US–Japan after Hiroshima; India–US; India–Israel only after the 1990s). **History of IR century-by-century is not GS** — optional (Political Science and International Relations) does that. GS needs **after the Second World War**.

---

sections.heading: 1. Superpowers, military blocs, capitalism vs communism (IR-03-01)
sections.content:
After WW2, two **superpowers**: **United States of America (USA)** and **Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) / Soviet Union**.

**Superpower** = extraordinarily powerful: the rest of the planet **cannot** achieve **Balance of Power (BOP)** against it. Only **another superpower** can counterbalance. Same ambition (dominate the world) → rivalry in **two** dimensions.

sections.heading: Military
sections.content:
**Arms race** (nuclear tests: India **twice** — **1974** and **1998**; the two superpowers did **hundreds**). Two alliances:

| | **North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)** | **Warsaw Pact** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Led by | USA | USSR |
| Geography of the name | Friends in **North America** + **West Europe** = rim of the **North Atlantic** | Signed in the city of **Warsaw**; mostly **East Europe** |
| Guarantee | US security against USSR | Soviet security against US / NATO |

sections.heading: Ideological
sections.content:
USA / NATO = **capitalism**. USSR / Warsaw = **communism**. They **cannot coexist**: communism **blames capitalism** for society’s problems.

| Capitalism | Communism (Karl Marx → **Marxism**) |
|:---|:---|
| **Free market** — no inspector / licence raj; **demand and supply** | Root problem = **class struggle** (economic inequality) |
| Example policies: **Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation (LPG)** | **Abolish** the right to own **private property**; only **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** |
| Rich / **capitalist** class = **ownership of property** (land, bank balance, factories — Tata / Ambani / Adani as class examples) | Poor / **working class** = one asset, **labour** |
| | Goal: **egalitarian / classless** society |

Capitalists will not give up property → a **revolution** is required. Two schools:

1. **Peaceful** — **Communist Party of India (CPI)** contests elections (Lok Sabha / Rajya Sabha; governments in **Kerala**, earlier **West Bengal**, **Tripura**; **United Progressive Alliance (UPA)** partners under Manmohan Singh). Legal.  
2. **Violent** — **Mao Zedong**, Chinese revolution **1949**: *power flows from the barrel of the gun.* Followers = **Maoists**. **Communist Party of India (Maoist)** is **banned**. Movement started at **Naxalbari** → **Naxalite**. **Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)** fights it. Sandhu: “on the verge of eradicating.” **IS-01 lock stays: too early to call Naxal-free.** Sheet “CPI(M) banned” = **Maoist**, not CPI(Marxist).

**Bipolar** = two poles (US and USSR). Whole world split: Western bloc vs Eastern bloc.

---

sections.heading: 2. Three worlds, NAM, Cold War, MAD, proxy (IR-03-02)
sections.content:
| World | Who | Ideology / policy |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **First** | Rich / developed; friends of USA | Capitalism |
| **Second** | Friends of USSR | Communism |
| **Third** | **Post-colonial** poor / developing states | **Non-alignment** — join **neither NATO nor Warsaw**; spend scarce resources on **growth**, not the superpower fight |

Not **tripolar**: the third “pole” was **powerless**.

**Non-Aligned Movement (NAM):** post-colonial states’ movement. **Jawaharlal Nehru** = one of the **founding fathers**. India encouraged other newly free states to stay out of the two camps.

**Cold War (1945–1991):** they hated each other, ran alliances and an arms race, but **never a direct (hot) war**. Reason: **nuclear deterrence** (*deter* = frighten). Supported by **realism**: two methods of **national security** = **BOP** (Lecture 1) + **nuclear deterrence**.

**Nuclear Weapon State (NWS) = 9:** USA, United Kingdom (UK), France, Russia, China (**Permanent Five (P-5)**) **+ India, Pakistan, Israel, North Korea**. Everyone else = **Non-Nuclear Weapon State (NNWS)**.

**Nuclear war** = **NWS vs NWS**. **Not** nuclear war: Russia–Ukraine; US–Iran; Hiroshima–Nagasaki (use of a bomb, Japan had **no** bomb). A nuclear war has **never** happened. Outcome = **Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD)** — all lose, **zero** winners. States do **cost–benefit analysis** (rational actors) → they do not fight it. Today’s weapons are **thousands of times** stronger than the **experimental** Hiroshima bombs (class: Oppenheimer). **No defence** except a deep bunker (class: **200–300 feet**, stay **40–50 years**) — not a GS number to invent beyond class.

**Still valid:** US–Russia, US–China, **India–Pakistan**, India–China cannot fight a **direct** war. India–Pakistan wars were **before** both had bombs. Class: if India had bombs in **1962**, China would not have attacked. **Iran** wants a bomb for the same deterrent; US does not want Iran to have it.

**Proxy / indirect war:** an NWS cannot fight another NWS → a friend (usually **NNWS**) fights **on its behalf** (money, weapons, intel). Cold War examples: **Korea** (South = US proxy, North = Soviet); **Vietnam** (North vs South); **Afghanistan 1979**.

**Today:** Pakistan’s proxies against India = **Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT)** and **Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM)**. **Operation Sindoor** = destroy **proxy infrastructure** (terrorist camps), **not** a full-scale war (MAD). Class: camps at **nine** locations; operation in **28–29 minutes**.

sections.heading: Update — 14 September 2026 (*Hindu* counter-terror op-ed — no extra Day-1)
sections.content:
Class lock **stays** (nine camps / 28–29 minutes / proxy ≠ MAD war). **Newspaper extra (Rajeev Agarwal):** Sindoor **6–7 May**, about **96 hours**; **LeT** and **JeM headquarters** destroyed; Pakistani military assets hit. After Sindoor, three stated intentions: (1) era of **restraint and patience** is over — Pakistan pays a **direct, heavy price**; (2) future **cross-border terrorism from Pakistan** = **“act of war”**; (3) **Pakistani nuclear blackmail** will **no longer** be a restraining factor. **Do not** rewrite the class **MAD** sentence — intention (3) is **policy**, not a claim that nuclear war is now thinkable.

**Uri (18 September 2016, JeM)** → first **cross-border surgical strikes (28–29 September)**. **Pulwama (14 February 2019, Central Reserve Police Force convoy)** → **Balakot (26 February 2019)** — first time the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** struck a **JeM** camp **inside Pakistani airspace**. **Pahalgam 22 April 2025** while the PM was in **Saudi Arabia**. Full **PRAHAAR** policy note: `Current_Affairs/September_2026/2026-09-14_Current_Affairs.md` (**CA-260914**).

**Answer drop:** *Cold War stayed cold because of MAD, not because the UN “kept peace.” Superpowers fought through proxies. NAM was the powerless third world opting out.*

---

sections.heading: 3. Why the USSR broke, 1991 (IR-03-03)
sections.content:
**1991:** USSR **disintegrates** into **15** countries. **Russia** = successor (capital **Moscow**; inherits Soviet nuclear weapons). **Warsaw Pact dissolved**. **USA won** the Cold War.

Class names (not a complete 15): Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, Armenia, Belarus, Ukraine, Russia.

| External | Internal |
|:---|:---|
| Power tussle with USA; **expensive arms race**; had to **defend Warsaw** members | **Weak economy** = **failed communism** — no incentive if you **cannot own property**; **over-centralisation of power** (sheet) |

Class equality line: Constitution wants **equal opportunity**, not a mechanical society with **no reward for merit**. After 1991, even the 15 successor states **adopted capitalism**; communist parties became **unpopular**.

---

sections.heading: 4. NPT, NSG, IAEA — India 2008 waiver (IR-03-04)
sections.content:
**Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT):** opened **1968**, in force **1970**. Cut-off **1 January 1967**: bombs **before** that date = recognised **NWS** = **P-5**. Restrictions sit on **NNWS**.

**Five non-parties (class):** **India, Pakistan, Israel, North Korea, South Sudan**. Four of those five have bombs (South Sudan does not). India did **not** sign: NPT is **discriminatory** — nuclear **haves and have-nots**; lets P-5 **dominate**.

**Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG)** = **London Club** — nuclear **technology + fuel** holders; will not share with a country that has not accepted NPT (civilian use only). **International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)** checks no **military misuse**; works **with** NSG. Class: Iran took NSG fuel after accepting NPT; IAEA later reported problems (detail in a later US/Iran class).

**2008:** **USA** helped India get an **NSG and IAEA waiver** — **exception only for India** so NSG members **can** share civilian nuclear technology with India **without** NPT. Full US-lecture later.

sections.heading: Update — 9 September 2026 (UPSC CSE Prelims 2018 / 2020)
sections.content: `CSE-2018-Q07` **missed** (`MST-063`). Consequence of NSG membership: access to **latest nuclear technologies / fuel** (statement 1). It does **not** automatically make the country an **NPT** member (statement 2). Same class lock: **2008** waiver **without** signing NPT.

sections.heading: Update — 10 September 2026 (Ghost Recall)
sections.content:
`MST-063` **held**: NSG ≠ auto NPT; 2008 waiver without NPT; five non-parties named.

`CSE-2020-Q55` **held**. Some Indian reactors sit under **IAEA safeguards** because they use **imported** uranium; reactors on **domestic** fuel are not in that IAEA civilian bucket. Do not pick thorium / foreign operator / private ownership.

sections.heading: Update — 12 September 2026 (UPSC CSE Prelims 2018)
sections.content: `CSE-2018-Q33` **missed** (`MST-084`). Ratifying the IAEA **Additional Protocol** (official stem spelling) means **civilian** nuclear reactors come under **IAEA safeguards**. It does **not** put **military** installations under inspection. It is **not** “privilege to buy uranium from the NSG” and **not** automatic **NSG** membership (`MST-063` cousin). He picked **(c)**. **Held 13 Sep evening** (option a). 15-day **28 Sep**.

sections.heading: Update — 14 September 2026 (UPSC CSE Prelims 2017)
sections.content:
`CSE-2017-Q28` **missed** (`MST-091`). Official key = **neither**. **Nuclear Security Summits (NSS)** are **not** periodically held under the **United Nations**. The **International Panel on Fissile Materials (IPFM)** is **not** an organ of the **IAEA**. Class IAEA checks military misuse of NSG fuel — that is **not** NSS and **not** IPFM. He picked **2 only**. **Held 15 Sep** Ghost Recall (neither). Obama / Princeton extras are **not** on this note — do not bank. 15-day **30 Sep**.

---

sections.heading: 5. Post–Cold War: unipolar LPG, then the dark side (IR-03-05)
sections.content:
**1991 onward = unipolar** = **US hegemony**. Economics: **LPG** → **open economy**. **Globalisation** = **free trade / trade without barriers**. India: **1991** reforms.

**Non-state actors** rise with integration:

- **Multinational Corporations (MNCs)** — **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)**  
- **Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs)** — e.g. **Amnesty** (human rights)  
- **International Monetary Fund (IMF) / World Bank (WB) / World Trade Organization (WTO)** — class: **Washington HQ** (IMF/WB)  
- **Transnational Terrorist Networks (TTNs)** — **Al-Qaeda**; **Osama bin Laden** from **Afghanistan**; **11 September 2001 (9/11)** — sheet **~3,000** Americans died. **JeM / LeT** sit here as Pakistan-based networks.

**Dark side of globalisation:** **illegal arms and drugs smuggling** because economies are **integrated**.

**Economic interdependence** → **multilateral** approach to global problems.

**2008 global financial crisis:** US economy / stock markets crash → **setback** to free trade / globalisation / liberalisation → **protectionism** (**tariff barriers** to **protect domestic industry**). Class: after 2008, more countries (including “manufacturing in India” talk) turn protectionist = **crisis of globalisation**.

---

sections.heading: 6. Trump, BRICS, China, new Cold War, Indo-Pacific (IR-03-06)
sections.content:
**January 2017 — Donald Trump:** US policy **protectionist** (national interest) → **de-globalisation**. Later **Biden**, then Trump again; class treats the **protectionist turn** as lasting. **Make America Great Again (MAGA)** — red cap; class is **sceptical** the tariffs will “bring manufacturing home.” Trump vs India: wants **lower Indian tariffs** so US firms need not manufacture **in India**. Class: threat of **100% tariff** if BRICS even **thinks** de-dollarisation.

**Decline of the West / rise of the rest** → **multipolar**. **Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa (BRICS)** = emerging economies; **beneficiaries** of globalisation (they **support** it). **BRICS Plus** — class: **Indonesia** has joined. US **MNCs** do **offshore manufacturing** in BRICS (India, China, South Africa, Brazil, Indonesia) → US **loses manufacturing** → **loses hegemony**. Angry US workers → Trump.

**US economic hegemony (three legs class):** (1) **highest Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** — class **~$30 trillion**; (2) **US dollar** as trade/oil **anchor** (America cannot have a classic **Balance of Payments (BOP)** crisis the way others can); (3) **IMF / World Bank**.

**BRICS counters:** grow GDP; **de-dollarisation** (yuan, dirham; talk of a BRICS currency); **New Development Bank (NDB)** as alternative to IMF/WB.

sections.heading: Update — 12 September 2026 (*Hindu* NDB / CRA extras — no extra Day-1)
sections.content:
Class lock **stays**: BRICS *talks* de-dollarisation and names NDB against IMF/WB. **Newspaper extra (do not rewrite the class sentence):** NDB **co-finances** World Bank / IMF work — **complementary, not a rival**. **Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA), 2015** ($**100 billion** FX pool) has **never been activated**; drawing **>30%** of a member’s share still requires an **IMF programme**. Rio **July 2025** declaration **omits** the word de-dollarisation; **Putin Nov 2024** said the bloc has **not sought to abandon the dollar**; **India opposes** a common BRICS currency. Kazan/Rio ask for a **bigger say inside** a **quota-based, adequately resourced IMF** (US **16.49%** votes + **85%** supermajority = veto) — **not** to replace it. Full numbers: `Current_Affairs/September_2026/2026-09-06_Current_Affairs.md` (`CA-260906-02`). **18th** summit **12–13 Sep 2026**, New Delhi, **“Humanity First.”**

`CSE-2016-Q67` **held**. NDB was **not** set up by **APEC**. Headquarters = **Shanghai**. Complementary-not-rival extra from today’s clip does **not** change that HQ lock.

sections.heading: Update — 13 September 2026 (*Hindu* New Delhi Declaration — no extra Day-1)
sections.content:
**Adopted 12 Sep** (day 1). **11-member** clip. **Iran + UAE** compromise → **“maximum restraint”** on West Asia; **no** naming of US–Israel or Iran’s Gulf strikes. **Intra-BRICS payments in national currencies** = the **same rails** as `CA-260906-02`, **not** a BRICS currency (India still opposes that). **Unilateral coercive measures** (tariffs / sanctions) condemned. **Pahalgam 2025** named. Class NDB / de-dollarisation sentences **stay**.

**China (last 3–4 decades):** second GDP; **manufacturing / supply-chain** hub (including **critical minerals**); **biggest challenge** to US hegemony. **Revisionist state** = wants to **revise / change** the (unipolar) world order and **displace** the US. **China containment** (US, from **January 2017**).

**Hybrid China (why this Cold War is harder than 1945–91):** **politically communist** (single party, Communist Party of China); **economically capitalist** (LPG, private sector — **learned from Soviet failure**). USSR was a **weak** communist economy; China is not repeating “public sector only.”

**New Cold War = US–China.** Proxies (no direct US–China war — MAD):

| Year | Fight | Backing (class) |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **2022** | Russia attacks Ukraine (ongoing) | Ukraine ← **US / NATO**; Russia ← **China** (oil / money; “limitless friendship”) |
| **2023** | Israel–**Hamas** | Israel ← **USA**; Hamas ← **Iran** ← **China** |
| **2026** | Iran vs **USA / Israel** | Iran ← **China / Russia** (drones, money) |

**Centre of gravity of world politics:** **Atlantic** (old US–USSR) → **Indo-Pacific** (US–China). **Indo-Pacific** = **Indian Ocean + Pacific Ocean + surrounding land**. For the US, **Pacific** now matters more than the old Atlantic fight.

**Answer drop:** *Unipolar US hegemony after 1991 is eroding. BRICS (China first) contest GDP, the dollar and Bretton Woods. A new Cold War is US–China in the Indo-Pacific; wars since 2022 are proxies.*

sections.content:

sections.heading: 1. How this paper is taught (IS-01-01)
sections.content:
| | Class line |
|:---|:---|
| **Importance** | Internal Security (IS) is **99% important** for this faculty’s GS-III slice (~**40–50 marks**). Interlocks with **International Relations (IR)** (example: terrorism asked in GS-II). |
| **References** | **Classes + handouts** (no dictation — handouts follow the class order) + **Yellow Book** (updated to current developments). After the academic block: a **model Q/A** set. |
| **Newspaper** | Beginners: *Indian Express* (digital / app). *The Hindu* is fine if you already correlate names; class prefers IE because *The Hindu* is often **too critical** of government policy. One paper, not both. |
| **Job in class** | **Concept-building** only. One concept → many answer frames. |

**Sample Mains Q (class):** “What are the multidimensional Internal Security threats faced by India. Suggest effective mechanism to counter these threats.” Today = **evolution** of those threats, not the full counter-mechanism chapter.

---

sections.heading: 2. 1947–48: First internal-security opening — J&K (IS-01-02)
sections.content:
**Two-Nation Theory** → **India** and **Pakistan**. **Jammu and Kashmir (J&K)** chose to stay **independent** (not accede to either). Muslim-majority state, Hindu ruler **Maharaja Hari Singh**.

**Trigger (class):** revolt always needs a spark. Here: **Pathans and Scouts** in the **north-western** erstwhile state were unhappy with the Maharaja’s **revenue / taxes**. Pakistan supported the revolt. That **forced** Hari Singh to sign the **Instrument of Accession** — **surrendered sovereignty to India**.

**Supreme Court (class: 2024):** after abrogation of **Article 370** and the **J&K reorganisation (2019)**, once Accession was signed, sovereignty stood surrendered; **J&K is an integral part of India**. Special constitutional arrangement followed — **polity class later** (class said not to dive today).

**Nehru took a bilateral fight to the United Nations (UN)** → **UN Resolution 47** (Kashmir Resolution) → a **ceasefire line (CFL)**.

By the time Accession could be completed, India had already **lost about 1/3** of J&K to Pakistan (**2/3 with India**).

**CFL:** from the **Jammu sector** up to the **southern tip** of the triangular **Siachen** glacier. Not demarcated beyond that: conditions **uninhabitable**; even today deployment at **about −45 °C** is a Herculean task.

---

sections.heading: 3. CFL → Line of Control; Siachen (IS-01-03)
sections.content:
After the **1971** war (**Bangladesh Liberation**; class: third war with Pakistan after **1947–48** and **1965**), the **Shimla Agreement** **rechristened** the same CFL as the **Line of Control (LoC)**. **No cartographic difference** — only the name, before vs after Shimla.

**Operation Rajiv** and **Operation Meghdoot:** Indian Army took **NJ 9842**. Under Meghdoot, control of the stretch / rivers and tributaries from Siachen. That alignment = **Actual Ground Position Line (AGPL)**, about **110 km**, still contested.

**Siachen:** highest battlefield; about **2,600 km²**; a **choke point** — whoever holds it has oversight toward **Srinagar / Leh** (class). Under Indian occupancy.

---

sections.heading: 4. Three perspectives; China 1962–63 (IS-01-04)
sections.content:
| Whose lens | Class line |
|:---|:---|
| **India** | The 1/3 is **Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK)**. **S. Jaishankar:** first item for any talk = Pakistan’s **illegal occupancy** of Indian land. Class: Finance + Home recently sent **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** notices into PoK (“you are Indian citizens”). |
| **International** | “Pakistan-administered” vs “India-administered” Kashmir. |
| **Pakistan** | Two parts: **South — Azad Kashmir**; **North — Gilgit-Baltistan**. Gilgit-Baltistan is **not** a Pakistan province: own assembly / president / prime minister / supreme court. After India’s **2019** reorganisation, Pakistan’s **National Assembly (2020)** tried to make it a **full-fledged province** — **did not fully succeed** (people revolted). |

**China, October 1962 — Battle of Namka Chu.** **People’s Liberation Army (PLA)** defeated India. **November 1962: unilateral** ceasefire (China was not forced). Relinquished **Arunachal Pradesh** (had penetrated deep); **kept Aksai Chin**. Class: then-leadership called Aksai Chin a **barren wasteland**; China kept a strategic horn-shaped tract. India still **claims** it.

**1963 Sino-Pak agreement:** Pakistan **ceded Shaksgam Valley** to China.

sections.heading: Update — 8 September 2026 (UN Geospatial map — not a new 1962 topic)
sections.content:
*The Hindu* (Kallol Bhattacherjee). A **UN Geospatial** world map (**July 2026**) draws **Arunachal Pradesh** and **Aksai Chin** as strips **between Indian and Chinese claim lines**. India voted for UNGA **“Correct the Map”** (**4 September 2026**) as an **equal-area** principle (**Togo / African Union**). **MEA (Randhir Jaiswal):** that vote is **not** an endorsement of those lines; J&K, Ladakh, Arunachal follow **India’s official map**. Full UNGA / LoC-note write-up: `Current_Affairs/September_2026/2026-09-08_Current_Affairs.md` (**CA-260908-02**). Same **IS-01** cluster — no extra Day-1 row.

**14 Sep follow-up (same cluster):** **António Guterres** — **no such thing as a UN map with borders**; website sheet = **NGO / indicative**, not official. **MEA** is **taking the anomaly up with the UN**. No extra Day-1.

sections.heading: 5. Insurgency; Naga (1952) (IS-01-05)
sections.content:
> **Insurgency** is an act of **armed rebellion** by a **group of citizens**, usually with a **political ambition** (**sovereignty or autonomy**), **with the support of a hostile element**. Example for the North-East: **China and Pakistan**.

**1950s** — next decade after the first border opening. Roots of North-East insurgency = **Naga insurgency (1952)** (first general election year). Leader **A.Z. Phizo**: declared **independence from India**; **Naga Federal Republic** + **Naga Federal Army**.

**Demand:** separate sovereign region **Nagalim** = hilly tracts of **Manipur** + parts of **Myanmar** + **Naga Hills district**.

**North-East political origin (class):** **United Assam** + princely **Tripura, Manipur, Sikkim** + **North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA)** (today’s **Arunachal Pradesh**), administered by Assam. **Majority of NE states were carved from United Assam.** Naga Hills was in United Assam.

**1963:** **Nagaland** created on the **16-point Agreement (1960)**. **Article 371** special privileges (Nagaland’s provision is **371A**). Still did not satisfy the Naga groups.

**2021 — National Socialist Council of Nagaland (Isak-Muivah) (NSCN-IM)** to the Union Home Minister: **separate Constitution** + **separate flag** (both = **sovereignty**). **Still in 2026, Nagalim demands exist.**

---

sections.heading: 6. Mizo, Assam / United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA), Bodo (IS-01-06)
sections.content:
**Mizo (Lushai Hills / Mizoram):** flowering of **bamboo** → explosion of **rats** → food stock hit → **1959 famine (Mautam)** → **Mizo Famine Front** under **Laldenga** → **Mizoram** **1972 Union Territory (UT)** → **1987 statehood**.

**Assam:** **illegal migration** → demography / **demographic re-engineering** → internal conflict (jobs + cultural transgression). **ULFA** — demand **Swadhin Assam** (sovereign Assam); sheet: **southern Assam**. Detail later.

**Bodo:** demand **Bodoland**. Detail later.

Insurgency from **1952** onward, then an unprecedented rise of related developments.

---

sections.heading: 7. Naxalism (1960s) and why “Naxal-free” is early (IS-01-07)
sections.content:
**Naxalbari, West Bengal (WB), 1967:** **violent peasant uprising against zamindars** (majority of the peasants were tribal). Inspired by **Mao**. Spread quickly to **Uttar Pradesh (UP), Bihar (BR), WB, Madhya Pradesh (MP), Odisha (OR / Odisha)**. **Chhattisgarh** as a separate state did not yet exist.

**Class trap:** Naxalbari is only an **identifier**. Naxalism is **not a one-day event**. It is the **culmination of tribal uprisings** from **pre-independence** (class listed Kol, Bhil, Santhal, etc.; **~110** tribal uprisings) that **continued after 1947** (Telangana struggle **1946–51**, Koel-Karo in Bihar, Bhoomi Sena in Maharashtra, Naxalbari 1967). **Naxalbari = episodic** in that chain.

**Still live (class):** Niyamgiri (Odisha, 2024); Ken–Betwa “fast until death” (recent); **March 2026** Palghar and Nashik (Maharashtra) tribals denied forest **title / ownership**. Until tribal discontent is resolved, the issue continues.

**Home Minister / “Mission Naxal Mukt Bharat”:** class heard India called **Naxal-free this year** on the floor. Class: **too early**. Operations alone cannot finish it — **dialogue + development** must run **parallel** to the offensive.

sections.heading: Update — 9 September 2026 (Sandhu IR — CPI split; no extra Day-1)
sections.content:
IR world-order class used Naxalism as the **violent-communism** example. **Keep the IS lock: too early.**

- **Communist Party of India (CPI)** = **peaceful** (elections). **Communist Party of India (Maoist)** = **banned**. Sheet “CPI(M) banned” is **Maoist**, not CPI(Marxist).
- Start-place still **Naxalbari** → Naxalite. **Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)** is the force Sandhu named. He said India is “on the verge of eradicating” — that is **not** the IS conclusion.

**Bihar — Bhojpur:** “red hot spot.” **Dola system** (sheet wrote “Dala”) — dominant **Kshatriyas / Bhumihars** holding majority land. Newly wed women from lower-caste / landless households were forced to spend the **first night** at the **zamindar’s** house, not the husband’s. Peasants **joined the Naxalites**. **Ranvir Sena** (same caste bloc) — **Supreme Court (SC) banned** it.

sections.heading: Update — 7 September 2026 (Dola = palanquin; not a new topic)
sections.content: Keep the class line (Bhojpur, Kshatriya/Bhumihar land, first night with the zamindar, peasants → Naxalites, Ranvir Sena SC-banned). Extra reading only fills the name. - **Dola** = the bride’s **palanquin / palki**. The custom was to **divert** that palanquin to the landlord’s **haveli** instead of the husband’s home. - **Feudal use:** dominance, humiliation, and sexual exploitation of labouring castes so they stayed subjugated. **Prelims trap:** **Dola**, not Dala. Name = palanquin, not a caste. SC banned **Ranvir Sena**, not the Dola custom as a statute. **Chhattisgarh — Salwa Judum:** “peace-keeping force” developed by the **Chhattisgarh government**. **SC banned** it. Divided villages into **support Naxals** vs **against Naxals**. **Unemployment (Mains hook):** high unemployment is dangerous for IS. Unemployed youth: **rejection of societal norms** → easier **exit into crime** + **radicalisation** by anti-social elements. In Naxal areas, **majority of the peripheral cadre** are **unemployed** (core cadre vs peripheral cadre). ---

sections.heading: 8. Khalistan (1970s–80s) and Kashmir 1987 (IS-01-08)
sections.content:
**Khalistan** = **land of the pure**. **Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale.** Demand: **separate Sikh nation**. Built first on a **Hindu–Sikh divide**. Detail of causes = later class.

**Counter (class):** **Operation Blue Star**, **Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act (AFSPA)**, **Gill doctrine**. Class takes **1997** as the close — **AFSPA withdrawn** from Punjab; no longer a disturbed area — **not** 1984–85 as the end-year.

**1987 Kashmir insurgency:** **rigging of the Assembly election** → **Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF)** separatist movement.

**Five traditional IS threats (sheet listed “4” then five):**

1. North-East insurgency  
2. Naxalism  
3. Khalistan insurgency  
4. J&K militancy  
5. Border disputes  

---

sections.heading: 9. Non-traditional threats; social media (IS-01-09)
sections.content:
**Organised crime** has **no universal definition** because of its **evolving** nature.

| Item | Class / sheet |
|:---|:---|
| **Drug / human / arms trafficking** | All organised crime. |
| **Money laundering** | Concealing the identity of **illegally obtained** money by passing it through **complex financial channels** so the output **appears legitimate**. Not the lay line “black into white.” **Black money** = no receipt. |
| **Hawala** | **Trust-based** system; **transfer money without physical movement**. Crypto = a form of **digital hawala**. |
| **Dead-drop email** | Mail is **written but not sent** (stays in drafts). Login is shared; the other party reads it. Agencies intercept **communication that has taken place** — a dead drop never “sends.” Class linked it to a **Delhi blast** example. |
| **Ransomware** | Intruder **breaches** a system, **takes control of data**, demands **ransom** (often **crypto**) to return control. **WannaCry** named as a famous ransomware. |
| **Digital arrest** | Impersonation of **law enforcement** to create urgency by intimidation. |
| **Pig butchering** | Lures via **investment fraud, Ponzi, job scams**. |
| **Honey trap** | Faking online romance. |
| **Pretexting** | Trying to extract sensitive information by a false claim. |

sections.heading: Update — 8 September 2026 (FATF digital hawala — same class topic)
sections.content: *The Hindu* (Devesh K. Pandey). **Financial Action Task Force (FATF)** report *Investigating Professional Money Laundering, Underground Banking, and the Use of Hawala and Other Similar Service Providers*. Keep the class line (trust; **no physical cash movement**). New facts only: - Informal networks now fuse **virtual assets** with old hawala; used for **money laundering** and **terror financing**. - Nearly **70%** of surveyed jurisdictions reported **new technology** inside these networks. - Six “digital hawala” forms in the clip: (1) **encrypted apps / shared ledgers** for instructions, still **traditional** settlement; (2) **mobile wallets / fintech** for the customer, operators still settle in **cash or trade**; (3) **stablecoins** to settle **between operators**; (4) **payment service providers**, fintech, **virtual International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs)**; (5) **artificial intelligence (AI)** for structuring, **mule-account** routing, fast **fiat-to-crypto**; (6) bundled **“hawala” apps** (messaging, cloud, social media, **Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs)**, lending, gaming). **Prelims trap:** Class crypto-as-digital-hawala still holds. FATF’s six forms are **configurations**, not a replacement definition. **70%** = jurisdictions seeing **tech integration**, not “70% of all hawala is now crypto.” **Social media and security** **Mob lynching** ← **fake news** → misinfo → confusion → **political agenda** / **illegitimate business gain**. Also **xenophobia**. **Social engineering** → manipulation of mindset → **radicalisation / religious indoctrination**. Platforms are **decentralised**; **cadre strength** (boxed on the sheet). **Orwellian world** — class: *Nineteen Eighty-Four* was **fiction** (1980s publication in class talk); now used as a lens on surveillance / information control. (Margin scribble on the sheet is unclear — not invented here.) Closing Q from class: 1947–48 Pathan/Scout revolt was **revenue/tax**, **not** framed as a religious war. A sharper **Hindu–Muslim** split in Kashmir is more a **1990s** story. ---
