sections.heading: Mechanism of Infection
sections.content:
```
Infected person → Coughing/Sneezing → Respiratory droplets
                                           |
                                    Inhalation by another person
                                           |
                                    Nasal cavity (nasal mucosa)
                                           |
                                    Trachea (windpipe)
                                           |
                                    Lungs → Infection → Inflammation
                                           |
                                    PNEUMONIA (infection + inflammation of lungs)
                                           |
                                    Reduced oxygenation of lungs
                                           |
                                    Shortness of breath / Breathlessness
```

sections.heading: Virus Attachment Protein (VAP) and Cell Surface Receptor
sections.content:
| Component | In SARS-CoV-2 Context |
|:---|:---|
| **Virus Attachment Protein (VAP)** | **Spike protein** of SARS-CoV-2 |
| **Cell Surface Receptor** | **ACE-2 receptor** on human lung cells |

- Spike protein contains **Receptor Binding Domain (RBD)**
- RBD interacts with ACE-2 receptor → allows virus to **attach, enter, and multiply** in lung cells
- ACE-2 receptors act as **gateway** for virus attachment and entry

sections.heading: If Virus Succeeds (No Immunity):
sections.content:
1. Virus infects host cell
2. Increased **viral replication** → new viral copies
3. Increased **viral load** (concentration of virus in blood)
4. **Severe pneumonia** → dip in oxygen saturation → breathlessness
5. Rush to hospital for **oxygen therapy**

sections.heading: Why Adults Were More Severely Affected Than Infants (COVID-19)?
sections.content:
| | Infants & Children | Adults |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Lungs | **Immature & developing** | **Fully developed & mature** |
| ACE-2 receptors | **Fewer in number** | **More in number** |
| Virus sticking | **Loose / weak** | **Strong** |
| Pneumonia severity | Mild / spared | **Severe** |

- This is **NOT about immunity** — adults have stronger immunity
- It's about **ACE-2 receptor expression** on lung cells
- Immature lungs = fewer ACE-2 receptors = virus cannot stick strongly
- This was a **blessing in disguise** for infants and children during COVID-19

---

sections.heading: How Antibodies Protect Us
sections.content:
```
Human body → WBC (White Blood Cells)
                  |
          B-cell lymphocytes
                  |
          Secrete ANTIBODIES (immunoproteins)
                  |
          Circulate in the blood
                  |
          Find & MASK the spike protein of virus
                  |
          CUT OFF virus-host cell interaction
                  |
          Virus CANNOT attach, enter, or multiply
                  |
          Viral load does NOT increase
                  |
          No severe pneumonia
                  |
          Virus forced to LEAVE the body
                  |
          Infection CLEARED
```

- **Antibodies** = Defensive/immunoproteins circulating in blood
- Secreted by **B-cell lymphocytes** (a type of WBC)
- Antibodies **block virus attachment and entry** by masking the spike protein
- This is called **Antibody-Mediated Immunity**
- If spike protein is overwhelmed by antibodies → interaction with ACE-2 receptor is cut off → virus becomes **unsuccessful**

sections.heading: Victor vs Victim
sections.content:
| Scenario | Victor | Victim |
|:---|:---|:---|
| No antibodies | Virus | Human body |
| Antibodies present | **Human body** | **Virus** |

---

sections.heading: Respiration (Metabolism)
sections.content:
> **Respiration** = Biochemical process that breaks down food into energy

| Type | Condition | Energy Produced |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Aerobic** | In presence of O2 | Significant/considerable amount |
| **Anaerobic** | In absence of O2 | Less amount |

sections.heading: Does Virus Have Respiration?
sections.content:
> **NO.** There is **absence of respiration (metabolism) in a virus** — neither aerobic NOR anaerobic

- Virus cannot produce its own energy source
- This is why virus is considered **non-living**

sections.heading: Does Bacteria Have Respiration?
sections.content:
> **YES.** Bacteria has **BOTH** aerobic AND anaerobic respiration

- Bacteria can convert food into energy → shows metabolism → is living

sections.heading: Reproduction
sections.content:
| Organism | Can Reproduce? | How? |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Virus** | Yes, BUT only inside a living host cell | Uses host cell machinery; no independent reproduction |
| **Bacteria** | Yes, independently | **Binary fission** (asexual reproduction) — cell divides into 2 equal halves |

- **Binary fission** = natural cloning (next generation cells are genetically identical to parent = clones)

sections.heading: Conclusion: Virus = Transition Phase
sections.content:
> **Virus is regarded as at the transition phase or at the border of living and non-living**

| Feature | Living? | Non-Living? |
|:---|:---|:---|
| No respiration/metabolism | | Yes |
| Reproduction (inside host cell) | Yes | |
| **Verdict** | **Transition between living & non-living** | |

---

sections.heading: Part J: Bacteria vs Virus — 7-Point Comparison
sections.content:
| # | Feature | Bacteria | Virus |
|:---:|:---|:---|:---|
| 1 | **Cellular location** | **Extracellular** microbe (outside host cell) | **Intracellular** microbe (inside host cell) |
| 2 | **Reproduction** | Self-reproduction using **binary fission** (asexual) — no host cell needed | Always replicates/reproduces **inside a living host cell** |
| 3 | **Genome** | Always **DNA only** | Either **DNA or RNA** (but NOT both) |
| 4 | **Respiration (Metabolism)** | Present — both **aerobic & anaerobic** | **Absent** — neither aerobic nor anaerobic |
| 5 | **Ribosomes** | **Present** — for protein synthesis | **Absent** (acellular) — uses host cell ribosomes for viral protein synthesis |
| 6 | **Culture medium** | Can use **both living & non-living** (synthetic/artificial) medium | Culture medium is **always living** medium — cannot use synthetic medium |
| 7 | **Drug sensitivity** | Sensitive to **antibiotics** | **Not sensitive to antibiotics** — requires **antiviral drugs** |

sections.heading: Key Differences to Remember:
sections.content:
- **Bacteria** = has cellular structure, independent metabolism, self-reproducing, DNA-only genome
- **Virus** = acellular, no metabolism, dependent on host cell, can have DNA or RNA
- **Ribosomes** = protein factories of the cell → present in bacteria, absent in virus
- Virus uses **host cell's ribosomes** to make its own proteins

sections.heading: Lecture 2 — 8 September 2026 (Public Health / Virology continued)
sections.content:
> **Date of Lecture:** 8 September 2026. Notebook pages dated **8/9/26**.  
> **Cluster:** **ST-05**. First Ghost Recall **9 September 2026**.  
> **Source:** 8 notebook pages + `S_and_TLecture080926` transcript.  
> **Already in Lecture 1 (`ST-01`):** virus = obligate intracellular parasite; nucleocapsid; DNA **or** RNA never both; tropism; spike / ACE-2; antibody-mediated immunity; culture medium is **always living**. Today **uses** those, then zoonosis, antigenic variation, three culture methods, and innate vs adaptive (Treg + 2025 Nobel).  
> **Parked for next sitting:** communication link between innate and adaptive immunity.

Class recap (do not re-learn as new): **Virus Attachment Protein (VAP)** of SARS-CoV-2 is the **spike protein**. It docks on **Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 (ACE-2)** receptors on **human lung cells** → attachment → **entry / penetration** → virus-infected host cell → pneumonia.

---

sections.heading: 1. Host specificity, zoonosis, spillover (ST-05-01)
sections.content:
**Host specificity** = **virus tropism** (Lecture 1). Some viruses stay narrow (human lung). Others circulate in a **wide range of hosts** — humans, birds, animals. **Zoonotic virus** (class): a virus that **travels from animal to human** — earlier confined to the animal, now infects a **new host**. Examples used today: **influenza** (swine flu, bird flu), **Ebola**, **Nipah**, **coronavirus**. **Spillover** = the pathogen **jumps** from an animal reservoir into a new host (humans). Constant virus–host contact → **mutation / genetic variability** → preference for the new host. Risk: **zoonotic outbreak** (COVID-19 pandemic, Nipah, Ebola). **Primary push** (class linked it to the same engine as climate change): **deforestation** → more **human–animal** contact → mutation + spillover. Five anthropogenic (man-made) factors on the sheet: 1. Intensive **livestock farming** and agriculture 2. Using **wildlife as a food source** 3. Clearing land for **farming and grazing** 4. Human **encroachment** on wildlife habitats 5. International trading of **exotic** (non-native) animals **and urbanisation** Surveillance is needed before **import / trade** of animal products.

Figure: Left = spike (VAP) on ACE-2. Right = class chain from deforestation to spillover.

---

sections.heading: 2. Genetic factor: RNA viruses and antigenic variation (ST-05-02)
sections.content:
Two engines of zoonotic outbreak (sheet fork): | Engine | Class line | |:---|:---| | **Anthropogenic** | Deforestation and the five factors above | | **Genetic (virus)** | Many outbreak viruses are **RNA** viruses — **unstable**; **short generation time** → faster mutation | RNA examples today: **influenza, SARS, Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS), Ebola, SARS-CoV-2, Nipah (NiV)**. | | **DNA virus** | **RNA virus** | |:---|:---|:---| | Genome | More **stable** | More **unstable** | | Mutation | Lower | **↑ mutation** → **antigenic variation** | Class sentence (write as class, do not invent a second number): RNA viruses are the primary **etiologic** (causative) agent of **94%** of **emerging infectious diseases**. **Antigenic variation** (board flow): virus replicates in a **wide pool** of hosts → ↑ mutation / genetic change in the **viral genome** → change in **antigen (protein)** of the virus → change in **behaviour** → **↑ spread / transmissibility**. If the host already has matching antibodies, multiplication (and therefore mutation) is slowed. Pandemics (global spread) are mainly **RNA**, not DNA. Sheet: **Spanish flu 1918–19–20** = **influenza**; also swine flu. **Nipah:** class illustration — out of **1,000** infected, risk of **900** deaths → **case fatality rate (CFR) ~90%**. COVID-19 class: **1–2%** CFR. You cannot change the virus’s nature; you **can** cut anthropogenic contact. You cannot predict *when* the next RNA spillover hits (class: next 5 years or later).
---

sections.heading: 3. Novel virus and three coronavirus waves (ST-05-03)
sections.content: **Novel virus** = the host has **never been exposed** to it before (appears “all of a sudden”). | Name | Class facts | |:---|:---| | **n-CoV-19** | **Novel coronavirus 2019** — cases from **December 2019**; later **WHO** renamed **SARS-CoV-2** (COVID-19 pandemic) | | **SARS-CoV-1** | **2002–03**; started **China**, including **Hong Kong** and **South Korea**; same **family**, not the same virus | | **MERS-CoV** | **2012–13**; **Middle East Respiratory Syndrome**; started **Saudi Arabia** | **Prelims trap:** SARS and MERS are **coronaviruses**, not influenza. **Prelims trap (`MST-060`):** **n-CoV-19** was renamed **SARS-CoV-2**, not SARS-CoV-1. **SARS-CoV-1 = 2002–03**. **MERS = 2012–13**, not 2019. Evening 8 Sep: he marked statement III with I and II. ---

sections.heading: 4. Culture media for virus — always living (ST-05-04)
sections.content:
**Culture medium** = what you need for **growth and multiplication in the lab** (study genome / protein, tropism, drugs, damage). Lecture 1 already: virus medium is **always living** — no synthetic / non-living medium. Three living methods (sheet): | Method | What you do | Ethical | |:---|:---|:---| | **Animal inoculation** | Inject virus into lab animals (class: **monkeys**) | **Kills life** | | **Embryonated egg** | Living **embryo** inside a **hen’s egg** (class: swine-flu work often uses this) | **Kills life** | | **Cell culture** | Take **animal tissue**, infect with virus; tissue undergoes **continuous cell division** → many copies **without killing the animal** | Preferred today | **Aims of cell culture (sheet, 4):** 1. Study **viral genome** and **virus protein / antigen** and its properties 2. Study **host specificity / tropism** 3. **Test antiviral drugs** (before human trials) 4. Nature of damage during replication = **cytopathic effect (CPE)** — e.g. HBV damages **liver** cells, not lung cells
---

sections.heading: 5. Immunity map — innate (ST-05-05)
sections.content:
**Immunity** = ability of the body to fight infection / disease. **Pathogen** = disease-causing organism (bacteria, virus, fungus, other microbes). Two types (working different, both present as systems): | | **Innate / inborn** | **Adaptive / acquired** | |:---|:---|:---| | When | **Since birth** (day zero) | **Takes time** during life | | Memory | **No** specific memory of the pathogen’s protein | **Yes** — antigen / protein memory | | Response | **Non-specific**, immediate | **Strong, specific** | | Role | **First line of defence** — can **engage** the enemy, may not **defeat** it | Precise attack (lymphocytes) | **Innate — four class examples** 1. **Skin** — **epithelial barrier**. Intact skin blocks entry; **broken** skin (injury / infection) lets microbes in. 2. **Lysozyme** — in **tears and saliva**; **antibacterial**. Tears also **24×7** lubricate the eyeball. Tear production needs **Vitamin A**. **Beta-carotene** (papaya, carrot, coloured fruit/veg) → **Vitamin A in the liver**. Deficiency → dryness of eyeball = **xerophthalmia**. Vitamin A also supports **White Blood Cell (WBC)** production. 3. **Phagocytosis** (“cell eating”) — **engulf and kill bacteria**; done by **neutrophils** (a WBC; class: ~**two-thirds** of WBCs). 4. **Interferons** — **antiviral proteins**. A virus-infected cell signals healthy neighbours. **Breastfeeding = bridge** until adaptive immunity matures. Transfers **readymade antibodies** mother → infant = **passive immunity**. First **24–48 hours** = **colostrum** (highest). Class: breastfeeding about **6 months** is essential.
---

sections.heading: 6. Adaptive immunity — humoral / B-cell (ST-05-06)
sections.content:
**Adaptive** uses specialised WBCs = **lymphocytes**: **B-cell** and **T-cell**. T-cells split into **Helper T (TH)**, **Cytotoxic / killer T (TC)**, **Regulatory T (Treg)**. **Humoral** (from *humor* = **fluid**): antibodies circulating in **blood** = **antibody-mediated immunity**. **B-cells secrete antibodies**. Y-shaped antibodies **mask the spike** → block attachment and entry (Lecture 1 picture, reused today). Lymphocytes become **memory cells** = **antigen-specific lymphocytes**. Memory of **this** virus’s protein. Antibody that blocks **SARS-CoV-2** will **not** block **HIV** (sheet crossed HIV) or dengue — different protein, different memory B-cell. How memory enters the body: **exposure**. | Route | Class | |:---|:---| | **Natural infection** | Live virus — dangerous (class: unvaccinated polio → paralysis of limbs) | | **Vaccine virus** | Safer route to the **same memory** (class: **oral polio vaccine**) |
---

sections.heading: 7. Cell-mediated immunity — T<sub>C</sub> and T<sub>H</sub> (ST-05-07)
sections.content:
If antibody **fails**, virus **enters** the host cell → **virus-infected host cell** (hijacked **biological factory**: virus has **no ribosome**, so it uses the host’s for **viral protein synthesis** and copies).

Two directions:

- **↑ replication → ↑ viral load → virulence / severity** (hospitalisation, death)  
- **↓ replication → ↓ viral load → prevent virulence** — this is **cell-mediated immunity (CMI)**

**Infection ≠ disease.** Antibody failure can mean you are **infected**; CMI can still stop **virulent disease**.

**Cytotoxic T-cell (T<sub>C</sub>)** releases **perforins** and **granzymes**:

- **Perforins** punch **holes** in the infected-cell membrane  
- **Granzymes** enter those holes → fragment **virus and its genome** and **kill the infected cell**  
- Also kill **cancer cells**  
- This is **apoptosis** (programmed cell death)  
- After recovery, leftover **fragments** can give a **false-positive** test

**Helper T-cell (T<sub>H</sub>)** secretes **cytokines** into blood — “radar” / inflammatory molecules — **alert and activate**:

- **B-cells** → antibodies  
- **Cytotoxic T-cells** → kill infected cells  

**Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)** **infects and reduces Helper T-cells** → command-and-control gone → **immunodeficiency** → **secondary opportunistic infections** (take the chance of weak immunity). Neither humoral nor CMI work well. HIV is a **retrovirus** — packaged genome is **RNA**, not dsDNA.

Full lock sits on the Lecture 1 **DNA vs RNA** table. Same PYQ, next to HIV because statement 2 is the AIDS line: - **Adenovirus = dsDNA**; can cause **common cold**. - **Retrovirus = RNA** (HIV). AIDS. Class: kills **TH**. - UPSC inverted statement 1 (ssDNA / dsDNA swap). Only statement 2 is correct.
H → immunodeficiency → opportunistic infection

sections.heading: 8. Regulatory T-cell, autoimmunity, Nobel 2025 (ST-05-08)
sections.content:
**Immunity** = WBCs + antibodies **protect**. When they **harm healthy cells** = **autoimmunity**. Class: can follow **mutation** in the human **genome / DNA** (confused “self” vs foreign). **Regulatory T-cell (Treg)** — “security guards”: - Promote **peripheral immune tolerance** - **Control cytotoxic T-cells** so they kill **infected / cancer** cells, **not** healthy cells - Prevent **excessive** immune response (calm down after the invader is gone) - **Prelims line (class):** “Regulatory T-cells prevent autoimmunity” — **correct** **FOXP3 (Forkhead box P3)** gene (in DNA) **controls development of Treg**. Mutation / fewer Treg → TC not stopped → autoimmune disease. **Thymus gland** = **training** of immunity (self protein vs foreign). **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2025** — discoveries concerning **peripheral immune tolerance**. Names (class sheet + Nobel list): **Mary E. Brunkow**, **Fred Ramsdell** (sheet: Fredrick J. Ramsdell), **Shimon Sakaguchi**. Next class: **communication link between innate and adaptive** (not taught today).
C don’t kill healthy No auto- immunity Nobel 2025: peripheral immune tolerance Brunkow · Ramsdell · Sakaguchi · Treg as security guards
---

sections.heading: 9. Lecture 2 — UPSC Quick Recall
sections.content:
1. **Zoonosis** = animal → human; **spillover** = jump to a new host. Push: **deforestation** + five anthro factors.  
2. **RNA** viruses mutate fast (**antigenic variation**); class **94%** of emerging infectious diseases; **Spanish flu** = influenza **1918–19–20**.  
3. **n-CoV-19** → **SARS-CoV-2**; **SARS-CoV-1 2002–03**; **MERS 2012–13**. **NiV CFR** class ~**90%**.  
4. Virus culture = **always living**; **cell culture** preferred (ethics). Damage in culture = **cytopathic effect**.  
5. **Innate** = skin, lysozyme, neutrophil phagocytosis, interferon; **colostrum 24–48 h** = passive. **Xerophthalmia** = Vit A.  
6. **Humoral** = B-cell antibodies in blood; memory is **antigen-specific** (COVID Ab ≠ HIV).  
7. **T<sub>C</sub>**: perforin + granzyme; **T<sub>H</sub>**: cytokines; **HIV** kills **T<sub>H</sub>**. **Adenovirus = dsDNA** (cold can be adenovirus); **retrovirus = RNA** (`CSE-2021-Q70`).  
8. **T<sub>reg</sub>** prevent autoimmunity (**peripheral immune tolerance**); **FOXP3**; **Nobel 2025**.

sections.heading: Nature and Demand of S&T in UPSC
sections.content:
- **Generalist vs Specialist:** UPSC tests the awareness of an educated, well-informed citizen, not a specialist scientist. Focus on **concepts, broad implications, and practical applications** rather than complex formulas, reaction mechanisms, or laboratory diagrams.
- **Current Affairs Dominance:** **90–95%** of S&T questions in Prelims and Mains are derived from recent scientific developments (past 1–1.5 years) in India and globally.
- **Static Foundation Role:** Core concepts (optics, micro-organisms, nuclear physics, genetics) serve as the foundation needed to understand and appreciate dynamic current affairs.

sections.heading: Core Source Architecture
sections.content:
1. **Class Notes & Handouts:** Primary foundation for conceptual clarity.
2. **Newspapers (The Hindu / Indian Express):**
   - **Strict 1-Hour Cap:** Avoid getting bogged down in minute chronological crime/accident details; focus on systemic issues, technology solutions, policy implications, and geographical markers.
3. **Monthly Current Affairs Magazine (Recitals):** Systematic monthly consolidation.
4. **NCERTs (Class 6 to 10):**

sections.heading: 2. Nuclear Technology — Dual-Use Spectrum
sections.content: ---

sections.heading: A. Nuclear Fission
sections.content:
- **Definition:** A heavy atomic nucleus (e.g., Uranium-235, Plutonium-239; atomic number 92) is bombarded with a thermal neutron $\rightarrow$ splits into two lighter nuclei $\rightarrow$ releases massive kinetic energy and additional neutrons $\rightarrow$ triggers a self-sustaining **chain reaction**.
- **Applications:**
  - *Controlled:* Nuclear Power Plants (electricity generation), Nuclear Submarine Reactors.
  - *Uncontrolled:* Atomic Bomb / Nuclear Fission Bomb.

sections.heading: B. Nuclear Fusion (Thermonuclear Reaction)
sections.content:
- **Definition:** Two light atomic nuclei (e.g., Hydrogen isotopes: Deuterium + Tritium) combine under extreme conditions to form a heavier nucleus (Helium) + release colossal energy.
- **Condition:** Requires astronomical temperatures (millions of °C) to overcome electrostatic repulsive forces between positive nuclei.
- **Weapon System — Hydrogen Bomb:**
  - Cannot trigger fusion directly under ambient conditions.
  - Utilizes a **fission trigger** (primary stage) to generate extreme heat and pressure $\rightarrow$ ignites the **fusion fuel** (secondary stage).
  - Hence, Hydrogen Bombs are **Fission-Fusion weapons** (significantly more destructive than pure fission bombs).

sections.heading: C. Radioactivity
sections.content:
- **Definition:** Spontaneous emission of energetic particles ($\alpha, \beta$) or electromagnetic radiation ($\gamma$) by unstable atomic nuclei attempting to achieve stability.
- Gamma rays ($\gamma$) are the highest energy, shortest wavelength segment of the electromagnetic spectrum, possessing extreme penetrating power.

Pointers only: **21 / 26** reactors are PHWR; **Tarapur** BWR; **Kudankulam** PWR **1000 MW** (Russia); FBR = **more fissile after**, **no moderator**, **liquid sodium**; Stage III **AHWR** at **BARC**. Cluster **ST-07**, due **13 Sep Q2**.

sections.heading: A. Nuclear Medicine & Radiotherapy
sections.content:
- **Radioisotope Used:** **Cobalt-60 ($^{60}\text{Co}$)** — an unstable isotope of Cobalt.
- **Mechanism:** Cobalt-60 spontaneously emits highly penetrating **Gamma ($\gamma$) rays**.
- **Therapeutic Action:**
  - Cancer/malignant cells multiply at an uncontrolled, abnormal rate.
  - Focused, precision beams of gamma radiation damage the DNA of rapidly dividing cancer cells $\rightarrow$ destroys tumor mass and halts metastasis.
  - Termed **Radiotherapy** (distinguished from *Chemotherapy*, which uses chemical drugs).
- **Penetration Power:** Unlike X-rays (which pass through soft flesh but are stopped by bone), Gamma rays can penetrate both flesh and dense bone.

---

sections.heading: 1. The Core Problem with Chemical Treatment
sections.content:
- In tropical climates, post-harvest losses of fruits, vegetables, pulses, and spices are high due to insect infestation, bacterial decomposition, and fungal rotting.
- Traditional chemical spraying leaves toxic **pesticide residues**, leading to:
  - Long-term human health risks.
  - Environmental soil/water toxicity.
  - **Export Rejection:** Stringent sanitary standards in developed markets (Japan, USA, EU) frequently lead to rejection of Indian agricultural exports with excessive chemical residue.

sections.heading: 2. Food Irradiation Mechanism
sections.content:
- **Cold Process:** Pre-packaged food items (in airtight, hermetically sealed packages) are passed through a specialized chamber exposed to controlled gamma radiation from a radioactive source (Cobalt-60).
- **Sanitization:** Gamma rays penetrate through the packaging material $\rightarrow$ kill all surface and internal pathogens, bacteria, molds, insect eggs, and pests $\rightarrow$ sanitize food completely without thermal heating.
- **No Residual Radiation:** The radioactive source remains strictly inside the irradiator chamber. Once food leaves the chamber, **zero radiation remains** (analogous to luggage passing through an airport X-ray scanner).

sections.heading: 3. Distinct Advantages
sections.content:
1. **Safety & Nutrition:** Certified by **US FDA, WHO, IAEA, and FSSAI**. No loss of baseline macronutrient/vitamin quality; no induced radioactivity.
2. **Shelf-Life Extension:** Significantly delays sprouting (potatoes/onions) and ripening (fruits).
3. **Versatility:** Can treat items unsuitable for chemical/thermal treatment (spices, meat, poultry, seafood, frozen foods).
4. **Trade Facilitation:** Eliminates chemical residue barriers, boosting agricultural export competitiveness.

sections.heading: C. Agriculture — Mutagenic Crops vs GM Crops
sections.content:
| Parameter | Mutagenic Crops | GM Crops (Biotech) |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Parent Technology** | **Nuclear Technology** (gamma radiation exposure) | **Biotechnology** (recombinant DNA technology) |
| **Genetic Change** | Induces ***random*** mutations in the plant's own genome | Inserts ***targeted*** genes at a chosen location |
| **Method** | **Trial-and-error screening** for beneficial agronomic traits (yield, pest/drought resistance) | **Precise, deliberate** gene alteration designed in advance |
| **Foreign Genes** | **None** — free from foreign transgenes | **Contains a specific foreign transgene** / alien genetic code |
| **Example** | Improved high-yield and disease-resistant varieties | **Bt Cotton** (*Cry1Ac* gene from *Bacillus thuringiensis*) |

---

sections.heading: A. Nuclear-Powered Submarines (SSBN / SSN)
sections.content: - **Nuclear Submarine Definition:** A submarine powered by an on-board, miniaturized **nuclear fission reactor** that drives steam turbines for propulsion and electrical power.

sections.heading: B. Nuclear vs Conventional Diesel-Electric Submarines
sections.content:
| Feature | Diesel-Electric Submarines (Conventional) | Nuclear-Powered Submarines (SSBN/SSN) |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Power Source** | Diesel Engine (Surface) + Battery Banks (Submerged) | On-board Miniaturized Nuclear Fission Reactor |
| **Air Dependence** | **Requires Oxygen** for diesel combustion; cannot run diesel engines underwater | **Zero Oxygen Required** for nuclear fission; reactor operates fully underwater |
| **Submerged Endurance** | **Limited (Few days):** Must snorkel / surface frequently to run diesel engines and recharge batteries | **Virtually Unlimited (Months):** Limited only by crew food supply and human psychological endurance |
| **Refueling Cycle** | Frequent fuel replenishment (diesel logistics) | Single nuclear fuel core lasts **years to decades** |
| **Stealth & Detection** | Diesel engines create acoustic noise; surfacing exposes radar/visual profile | **Extremely Quiet:** Silent fission process; zero requirement to surface $\rightarrow$ invisible in vast oceans |
| **Strategic Utility** | Tactical coastal defense / littoral warfare | **Deep-sea strategic deterrence & Second Strike** |

---

sections.heading: C. India's Indigenous Nuclear Submarine Fleet (P5 + 1 Club)
sections.content:
- **Indigenous Construction:** Project Advanced Technology Vessel (ATV).
  - **INS Arihant (SSBN-80):** India's first indigenously designed and built nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (commissioned 2016).
  - **INS Arighat:** Second indigenous nuclear submarine (commissioned 2024).
  - **INS Aridhaman:** Third ballistic missile nuclear submarine (under advanced development/induction).
- **Global Standing — P5+1 Elite Club:**
  - With INS Arihant, India became only the **6th nation** in the world to indigenously design, build, and operate nuclear-powered submarines.
  - Members: **USA, Russia, China, UK, France + INDIA**.

---

sections.heading: D. Submarine-Launched Ballistic Missiles (SLBMs) — K-Series
sections.content:
- Named in honor of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul **K**alam.
- **Role:** Submarine-launched, solid-fueled, **nuclear-capable ballistic missiles** launched from underwater tubes of SSBNs.
- **Key Missiles:**
  - **K-15 (Sagarika):** Range ~750 km (operational on INS Arihant).
  - **K-4:** Range ~3,500 km (enables deep standoff range from the Indian Ocean).

---

sections.heading: 6. Missiles Comparison — Ballistic vs Cruise
sections.content:
Figure: Ballistic missiles arc out of the atmosphere and re-enter under gravity at hypersonic speed; cruise missiles stay inside the atmosphere, flying low and flat on a jet engine. (On a phone, swipe the chart sideways.)

| Parameter | Ballistic Missiles | Cruise Missiles | |:---|:---|:---| | **Trajectory** | **Projectile / Parabolic:** High arc, launched into upper atmosphere/space, re-enters under gravity | **Horizontal / Flat:** Flies parallel to earth's surface, terrain-hugging, sea-skimming | | **Propulsion Engine** | **Rocket Engine** (solid/liquid propellant carries own oxidizer) | **Jet Engine** (turbojet / ramjet / scramjet — breathes atmospheric air) | | **Atmospheric Boundary** | **Leaves and re-enters** Earth's atmosphere (exosphere transit) | **Cannot leave atmosphere** (dependent on atmospheric oxygen for combustion) | | **Speed Profile** | High initial thrust $\rightarrow$ free fall $\rightarrow$ **Hypersonic terminal speed (>20 Mach)** | Generally Subsonic (Mach 0.8) or **Supersonic (Mach 2.5–3.0)** | | **Maneuverability** | **Low:** Fixed ballistic trajectory; difficult to redirect post-launch | **Extremely High:** Dynamic waypoint navigation, remotely guided, evasive zig-zag | | **Radar Detection vs Interception** | **Easier to detect** (high arc), but **extremely difficult to intercept** in terminal phase (>20 Mach) | **Difficult to detect** (flies low below radar horizons), but **easier to intercept** if detected | | **Payload & Range** | Heavy warheads; versatile ranges (**up to 5,000+ km ICBM**) | Precision warheads; tactical ranges (**typically <1,000 km**) | | **Indian Examples** | **Prithvi Series, Agni Series (Agni 1–5), K-Series SLBMs** | **BrahMos, Nirbhay** | ---

sections.heading: A. Agni-5 ICBM & MIRV Technology
sections.content:
- **Classification:** **Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM)** with range $> 5,000\text{ km}$.
- **Geographic Coverage:** Complete coverage of Asia and significant parts of Europe.
- **MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle):**
  - Advanced payload delivery technology successfully flight-tested on Agni-5 (Mission Divyastra).
  - **Mechanism:** A single ballistic missile carries multiple nuclear warheads, each programmed to strike a **separate, distinct target** hundreds of kilometers apart.
  - **Strategic Advantage:** Overwhelms and saturates enemy Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) defense systems.

---

sections.heading: B. BrahMos Supersonic Cruise Missile
sections.content:
- **Name Origin:** Joint venture between **India (DRDO)** and **Russia (NPOM)** $\rightarrow$ **BRAH**maputra + **MOS**kva rivers.
- **Propulsion:** Two-stage propulsion (Solid propellant booster + Liquid Ramjet engine).
- **Speed:** **Supersonic (Mach 2.8 – 3.0)** — among the fastest operational cruise missiles in the world.
- **Range Evolution:**
  - *Initial Range:* $290\text{ km}$ (capped due to MTCR guidelines before India joined MTCR).
  - *Post-MTCR Extended Range:* $450\text{ km} \rightarrow 800\text{ km}+$.
- **Universal Launch Platforms:** Multi-platform capability — Land, Sea (ships), Sub-sea (submarines), and Air (**Sukhoi-30 MKI**).
- **Export Dimension:** Major driver of India's defense export push (landmark export deal signed with **Philippines**; interest from Indonesia, UAE).

---

sections.heading: A. The Nuclear Triad Architecture
sections.content:
A comprehensive, three-pronged capability to deliver nuclear warheads from **Land, Air, and Sea**:
---

sections.heading: B. Purpose: Deterrence & Credible Second-Strike Capability
sections.content:
- **Non-Aggressive Posture:** India's nuclear arsenal is built strictly for **Deterrence**, not territorial aggression.
- **No First Use (NFU) Doctrine:** India maintains a declared policy that it will never initiate a nuclear first strike against any state.
- **Credible Second-Strike Capability:**
  - If an adversary launches a devastating nuclear first strike that incapacitates land-based missile silos and airbases, the **Sea Leg (submerged SSBNs in deep oceans)** will remain undetected and intact.
  - India retains the guaranteed ability to retaliate with **massive, punitive counter-strikes** from the sea.
  - This certainty of assured destruction deters potential adversaries from contemplating a nuclear first strike against India.

---

sections.heading: 1. Atom → Nucleus → What Is “Elementary”? (ST-03-01, ST-03-02)
sections.content:
High-school story: the atom was the smallest indivisible bit. It is not. An atom has a **nucleus** (protons + neutrons) and **electrons** in a cloud / **orbitals** around it.

**Elementary particle** = not made of anything smaller; indivisible building block. **Protons and neutrons are not elementary** — each is three **quarks**. **Electrons are elementary** (lepton family, not the quark family).

**~118 elements** discovered. **Identity of an element = number of protons = atomic number (Z).** Electrons do not: strip an electron from hydrogen and it is still hydrogen (now charged). **Sodium chloride (NaCl):** sodium donates an electron to chlorine — both stay Na and Cl.

Periodic table is ordered by **increasing Z**.

| Particle | Charge / mass (class) | Where | Elementary? | Discovery (class / sheet) |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Proton** | Positive; in nucleus | Nucleus | **No** — 3 quarks (**2 up + 1 down**), held by **gluons** | **Ernest Rutherford** |
| **Neutron** | Uncharged; mass **slightly larger** than a proton | Nucleus | **No** — 3 quarks (**2 down + 1 up**) | **James Chadwick** |
| **Electron** | Negative; **negligible mass** | Orbitals around nucleus | **Yes** — **lepton** | **J.J. Thomson** |

Almost **all mass** sits in the nucleus. Nucleus held by the **strong nuclear force** — **strongest of the four fundamental forces** — which overcomes **electrostatic repulsion** between protons.

**Gluons** = force-carrying “tiny bundles of energy” (same family as **photons** → later: **bosons**). They keep quarks together and give the strong force that holds the nucleus.

---

sections.heading: 2. Notation, Isotopes, Hydrogen and Carbon (ST-03-01)
sections.content:
**Z** = protons. **Mass number A** = protons + neutrons.

Standard symbol: **A/Z X** — mass number **A** top-left, atomic number **Z** bottom-left (example **¹²₆C**).

**Isotopes** = same element (same **Z**) , different neutron number → different **A**. **Similar chemical properties** (same electrons); **nuclear properties can differ**.

**Hydrogen**

| Isotope | Notation (sheet) | Notes (class) |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Protium** | **¹₁H** | Ordinary; non-radioactive; makes **H₂O** |
| **Deuterium** | **²₁H** | Extra neutron; **D₂O** = **heavy water** (needed in **nuclear reactors**, not as drinking water) |
| **Tritium** | **³₁H** | **Scarce** on Earth; **T₂O**; **radioactive** |

**Carbon:** **C-12** non-radioactive / stable; **C-14** radioactive — used for **carbon dating**.

---

sections.heading: 3. Radioactivity, α / β / γ, Half-Life (ST-03-03, ST-03-04)
sections.content: **Radioactivity:** spontaneous emission of energetic **radiation** (gamma) or energetic **particles** (alpha, beta) from the nucleus of an **unstable** atom, to become more stable. Spontaneous = the species that emits α cannot be made to emit β instead. If the daughter is still unstable, the chain continues.

sections.heading: 3.1 What is emitted
sections.content:
| | What it is | Charge | Nucleus change (class) |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Alpha (α)** | **2 protons + 2 neutrons** = **helium nucleus** = **He²⁺** (“doubly charged helium”) | Positive | **A/Z X --α--> (A−4)/(Z−2) Y** — **new element** |
| **Beta (β⁻)** | **Fast-moving electron.** Inside: **n → p + e⁻**; proton **stays** in the nucleus | Negative | **A/Z X --β⁻--> A/(Z+1) Y** — **A unchanged, Z + 1** |
| **Gamma (γ)** | **Energy only** (not a particle in this scheme) | — | No change of Z or A in the class picture |

**Penetrating power:** **γ > β > α**. Class: α exposure is the *least* dangerous of the three in this ranking; **gamma is highly dangerous** (largest penetrating capacity).

Beta electron is **not** an orbital electron — it is born in the nucleus from neutron decay.

sections.heading: 3.2 Half-life
sections.content:
Time in which the radioactive substance falls to **half** its quantity. Measures **rate of decay**. **Every radioactive isotope has its own half-life.** You **cannot alter** it.

**Prelims trap:** **twice the half-life is not the “full life.”** After one half-life you have ½; after two you have ¼ — not zero.

**Uses class drilled**

1. **Chernobyl (1986), USSR — now Ukraine.** Biggest nuclear-reactor disaster in class’s telling. City evacuated; **~40 years on, still abandoned**; unfit for **thousands of years** because isotopes there have **long half-lives**. Half-life is how you **predict** that.
2. **Technetium-99m (Tc-99m)** — medical diagnosis. Half-life **~6 hours**: long enough to inject / ingest a **tiny** dose, map organs / tumours in 2-D or 3-D, then decay to insignificant activity so it does not sit in tissue.
3. **Carbon dating** — age of **dead organic** matter. Living things keep the environmental **C-12 : C-14** ratio (plants fix carbon; animals get it from the food chain). After death, **intake stops**, **C-14 keeps decaying**. Half-life of C-14 **~5,000 years** (class: “around 5,000 something”; sheet **5k yrs**). Ratio mismatch → age. **Bodies are slightly radioactive** while alive because of C-14.

---

sections.heading: 4. Elementary-Particle Map (ST-03-05, ST-03-06)
sections.content:
Elementary particles = building blocks; everything else is combinations of them.

Two big families:

**Fermions** = **matter** particles (all ordinary matter). Two types:

| Quarks (6) | Leptons (6) |
|:---|:---|
| Up, Down, Top, Bottom, **Strange**, **Charm** | **Charged (−1):** electron, muon, tau |
| | **Neutral:** electron neutrino, muon neutrino, tau neutrino |

**Bosons** = **force-carrying** particles (“tiny bundles of energy”). Four, matching the **four fundamental forces**:

| Boson | Force |
|:---|:---|
| **Gluon** | Strong nuclear |
| **Photon** | Electromagnetic |
| **W and Z bosons** | Weak nuclear |
| **Graviton** | Gravitational |

A fundamental force exists only if energy / a force-carrier is **exchanged**.

**Quarks**

- Building blocks of protons, neutrons, etc.
- **Only** particles in nature with **fractional charge** (class: ±⅓, ±⅔).
- Can feel **all four** fundamental forces.

**Leptons** feel **weak**, **gravity**, and **electromagnetic if charged**. They **do not** feel the **strong** nuclear force.

**Hadrons** = quark combinations (proton, neutron, …). **Not elementary.**

Class also named **pion** as another quark combination — do not drill unless asked.

**Higgs boson** sits **outside** this four-force table until later: **CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC), 2012** — **“God particle”** because it (via the **Higgs field**) **gives particles mass**.

---

sections.heading: 5. Neutrinos — “Ghost Particles” (ST-03-07)
sections.content:
Lepton family. **Tiny (not massless)** mass, **not yet quantified** in class; **electrically neutral**; **rarely interact** with matter. **Second most abundant** particles in the universe after **photons**.

Because they barely interact, they keep information from **origin of the universe**, neutron stars, nuclear events. They **cannot be contained** — class: in principle useful even for spotting **hidden underground nuclear activity**. Hard to detect.

**India-based Neutrino Observatory (INO):** **Theni district, Tamil Nadu** — **Bodi West Hills**. Tunnel **~1.2 km** deep so only neutrinos arrive; other radiation is absorbed. **IceCube** neutrino observatory = **Antarctica**, **not** India’s.

---

sections.heading: 6. Bosons, S.N. Bose, States of Matter (ST-03-08)
sections.content:
**Boson** is named for **Satyendra Nath Bose (S.N. Bose)** — **not J.C. Bose**. Contemporary of **Einstein**; they built **Bose–Einstein statistics**. His work helped later discovery of bosons; he did not “find” the particles himself.

**States of matter (class upgrade from Class 10’s three):**

| State | When |
|:---|:---|
| Solid, liquid, gas | Everyday |
| **Plasma** | Extremely high T — electrons knocked off → **ionised gas** (core of the **Sun** / stars). **Not** Bose’s discovery |
| **Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC)** | Another state associated with Bose–Einstein work |

**Homework (Mains):** keep a running list of **contribution of Indians in science and technology** (class names: S.N. Bose, M.S. Swaminathan, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, Homi J. Bhabha, Vikram Sarabhai). Professional contribution only.

sections.heading: Particle and anti-particle (class closed here)
sections.content:
Every particle has a counterpart: proton ↔ antiproton, neutron ↔ antineutron, electron ↔ **positron**, neutrino ↔ antineutrino. Same mass, opposite charge.

When a particle meets its antiparticle they convert to **energy as photons**. A high-energy photon can make a **particle–antiparticle pair**. Class: if antimatter could be made commercially it would be an extreme energy source; **CERN LHC** has made only tiny amounts.

sections.heading: Update — 10 September 2026 (Shobhit Sir, next nuclear class)
sections.content:
Completed the close + four-force **range / strength** table. Full write-up: `05_Nuclear_Fission_Fusion_and_Reactors.md` (cluster **ST-06**). New locks only: **annihilation = mass → energy**; **pair production = energy → mass**. Neutron’s antiparticle is also **neutral**. **Graviton not yet discovered**. Range: strong and weak = **short**; electromagnetic and gravity = **infinite**. Strength order: **strong > EM > weak > gravity**. Antimatter scale: **<1 g** Earth→Moon; **>$60 trillion / 1 g**; CERN **~1 nanogram**.

---

sections.heading: UPSC Cues
sections.content:
- **Z = protons = identity.** Electrons can change without changing the element.
- **p = uud, n = udd**; gluons; **e⁻ = lepton / elementary**. Discoverers: Rutherford / Chadwick / Thomson.
- Isotopes: same Z, different A; **D₂O = heavy water (reactors)**; tritium scarce + radioactive; **C-14 dating**.
- α = He nucleus, **A−4, Z−2**; β⁻ = nuclear electron, **Z+1, A same**; γ = energy; penetration **γ > β > α**.
- Half-life: **2 × half-life ≠ gone**. **Tc-99m ~6 h**; **C-14 ~5,000 y**; Chernobyl **1986 / Ukraine** still empty because of long half-lives.
- Fermions vs bosons; quarks feel **all four** forces; leptons **no strong** force; hadrons **not** elementary.
- **INO = Theni / Bodi West Hills / 1.2 km**; IceCube = Antarctica. Higgs **2012 / God particle / mass**. **Boson ≠ J.C. Bose**. Particle + antiparticle → photons; electron’s antiparticle = **positron**.

---

| **BEC** | Bose–Einstein Condensate |
| **S.N. Bose** | Satyendra Nath Bose (not J.C. Bose) |
| **u / d** | Up / Down quark |

sections.heading: 1. Why space (and later biotech) stay predictable (ST-04-01)

You name the field. 3. **India** is doing well, and the programme is in a **metamorphosis** (private opening). Same three-point test will apply when biotechnology starts.

sections.heading: 2. Biotechnology preview (later block) (ST-04-02)
sections.content:
After outer space, class will jump to the opposite extreme — **molecular** sizes.

**Biotechnology** is not a literal “biology + technology.” Functionally: **all the tools and techniques** through which humans change the **rate and direction of evolution** of a living organism — and can even cause **extinction**. Class: that is “playing God / nature.”

**Evolution** (class): gradual and **accumulative** changes towards **better adaptability** to the environment. Everything evolves — living, non-living, culture, language, even the Civil Services Examination.

**Cotton → bollworms → BT cotton**

- Cotton’s damaging pests = **bollworms** (larvae of a moth). They feed on cotton **bolls** and cut productivity. (Audio: “ball bombs” / “bonbons” = bollworms.)
- Given centuries, cotton *might* evolve resistance. We do not wait.
- **BT cotton** is the biotech shortcut: **gradual → quick**. Class: **BT here is not the word “biotechnology.”** (Sheet did not expand the letters; do not invent a full form until next class.)
- Knock-on: cotton becomes non-edible to the pest → bollworm numbers fall → birds that eat them are hit. One gene edit moves a **food web**.

**CA hooks for later:** India–United States trade deal and **genetically modified (GM)** crops; **GM mustard**; **messenger Ribonucleic Acid (mRNA)** cancer therapy; **ethanol** from molasses / maize / rice (productivity of feedstock).

---

sections.heading: 3. Orientation only — exam evolution and the brain (not a recall cluster)
sections.content:
Sir spent the first half on **co-evolution**: UPSC adapts against *you*. No rational ground to complain that the paper got harder.

**Prelims count (class):** **270** questions → **2011** overhaul → **180** (**100** General Studies + **80** Civil Services Aptitude Test (CSAT)) → after **2014** protests / election, CSAT became **qualifying** and GS sits around **100**. Each cut raises the **weight of one mistake** (T20 vs Test: fewer balls, more upsets). Aspirants **~3 lakh (2006) → ~13 lakh**. Vacancies have **no trend** (class example: **1000+** one year, **~700** the next). Cut-offs as a **percentage** have **not** risen with “smarter” candidates — class showed a **20-year decline**; **2023** cited around **37%** of those who appeared (audio garbled on the exact medal line).

**Memory science:** content sticks when packaged in **emotion**. Solve questions as a **method of preparation**, not only as a test. Three revisions + repeated questioning > ten passive revisions.

**Brain = neurons; preferred / only fuel = glucose.** Extra glucose → **liver** as **glycogen** (~**12 hours**). Skipping **breakfast** = brain starving (attention, analysis, memory). Also: **hydration** (thirst = already dehydrated; alcohol headache = brain first); **sleep** = quantity **≥ 7 hours**, quality = **dark** room → **melatonin** (pineal / “third eye”), pattern = **biological clock / circadian rhythm** (sunrise–sunset cue); **10–15 min** aggressive cardio → **pituitary** (memory, attention, analysis, natural painkillers, “feel-good”); **recreation** only after you **pay the price** (reward, not a random break). Margin: **peak at the right time** — do not burn both ends of the candle in Foundation.

Sheet path: Khan / memory → science → emotion. Keep this as hygiene, not as S&T syllabus.

---

sections.heading: 4. What “space” means — Karman Line and the Outer Space Treaty (ST-04-03, ST-04-04)
sections.content:
**Space** (generic) = any **three-dimensional unoccupied** area. **Space technology** always means **outer space**. Walk up from Earth’s curvature. Imaginary boundary at **100 km** = **Kármán / Karman Line**, proposed by **Theodor Karman** (class: Hungarian physicist — no biography needed). | Domain | Where | Activities | Sovereignty | |:---|:---|:---|:---| | **Aeronautical space** | **Below** the line | Needs **air** — aircraft | **Yes.** Airspace belongs to the state underneath. Class joke: BrahMos “evening walk” over Pakistan. | | **Outer / astronautical / astronomical space** | **Beyond** the line | Spacecraft, satellites | **No** sovereign claim. Common property of humankind. **No military base** on Moon / Mars / an asteroid. | **100 km is not rigid.** **National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)** / United States treats it as **80 km**. Lies “largely in that zone.” **United Nations Outer Space Treaty (OST), 1967** — Cold War, fear of space militarisation. Class: **non-binding / non-enforceable** — moral pressure. That is why militarisation is creeping back.
---

sections.heading: 5. What a satellite is — and the three application families (ST-04-05)
sections.content:
**Generic satellite** = any entity whose **identity is derived around another body**. NCR cities are satellites of Delhi. Moon is Earth’s satellite; Earth is the Sun’s. **Microsatellite Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA)** in biology uses the same word with no orbit.

**Here:** **artificial / application satellites**, **majorly** around Earth — not absolutely. **Chandrayaan** orbits the Moon; **Mangalyaan** orbited Mars; **Shukrayaan** would orbit Venus.

Value is not “a new application terrestrial tech cannot do.” Value is **coverage** → **cheaper** service. Higher altitude → bigger footprint.

| Family | What it does | Class applications |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Communication** | Links | **70–75%** of use = **TV broadcast**. Also **tele-education**, **tele-medicine** (Siachen soldier guided from a city), **satellite-based internet services (SBIS)** — **Starlink** most numerous / successful. |
| **Remote sensing (RS)** / **Earth Observation Satellite (EOS)** | Sense from a distance | Forestry, agriculture (this year’s GS-I), geology / minerals, disaster management, weather, **military surveillance** + **surgical-strike precision**. |
| **Navigation** | **Position and timing** in real time | The blue dot + “you will be there by…”. Essay hook: tech making humans loners. Class: siblings in **Uttar Pradesh (UP)** guided onto a half-built bridge. |

**Trap:** an **EOS is necessarily** a remote-sensing satellite. A remote-sensing satellite is **not necessarily** Earth-sensing — **Chandrayaan** remote-senses the **Moon**.

---

sections.heading: 6. Why 100 km — orbital velocity, fuel, collision avoidance (ST-04-06)
sections.content:
**Orbit** = the path. Each orbit needs a **unique orbital velocity**. More or less → you leave that orbit. Sheet: **~30 km** holds **99.99%** of Earth’s atmosphere. Audio: **under the Karman Line** sits **nearly 100%** of the atmosphere (gravity glues it). **International Space Station (ISS)** class altitude: **~400 km**. **Thought experiment:** plant a satellite at **30 km** vs **400 km**, both given the “right” speed. - **30 km:** air **resists** → speed drops → only fix is **burn fuel continuously** → tank empty in **minutes**. You do not spend billions for minutes. **No satellite stays in orbit powered by fuel.** - **Beyond atmosphere:** give the velocity **once**. **Inertia** keeps it going unless an external force acts. That is **why** outer space is defined where it is: **beyond Karman, motion is not fuel-powered.** **Satellites still carry fuel** — for three jobs only: 1. **Acquire initial velocity** 2. **Change orbit** — **orbit raising** (higher) / **orbit lowering** (lower). Today’s GISAT: **transfer orbit** = temporary; must be raised. 3. **Collision Avoidance Manoeuvre (CAM)** — dead objects at **25–30,000 km/h**, millions of them. Satellite must “dodge.” Fuel for CAMs. Fuel quantity is a **strong determinant of lifespan**. First mistake after dry tanks is the last. World (including India) is working on **on-orbit refuelling** — not operational in class’s “at the moment.”
**Coverage assignment (remember):** **three** satellites on the vertices of an **equilateral triangle**, same orbit, **35,786 km** from Earth’s **surface** → **global coverage**. Same orbit ⇒ **same** orbital velocity. Towers cannot wrap the planet this cheaply.
---

sections.heading: 7. History — balloons, sounding rockets, Space Race 1.0 (ST-04-07)
sections.content:
Astronomy is as old as humankind. **Space technology** is ~a century old. **1930 (sheet and class):** United States sent **hot-air balloons** — first military surveillance (height = coverage), then **scientific instruments** for **vertical profiling** (layer-by-layer: thermometer, pH, carbon dioxide (CO₂), magnetic field, particles). **Two limits:** very **slow**; ceiling ~**25 km** (outer pressure falls, balloon bursts / drops). Not outer space — but it posed the problem. **Sounding rockets** — faster + higher; still carry instruments for **atmospheric investigation**. **“Sounding”** is figurative: a **naval** term (sound waves for **underwater** vertical profiling). Not because the rocket uses sound. **India / ISRO** example is **later than Sputnik**, not before it. Class named the **Rohini** series (regular; **do not confuse** with **Rohini satellites**). First Indian sounding-rocket launch: **21 November 1963** (Nike-Apache from **Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS)**, Thiruvananthapuram). First fully Indian **Rohini RH-75: 20 November 1967**. **Space Race 1.0** = **military hostility + geopolitical antagonism + high optics** (whatever goes up is visible). Tool of **upmanship**, not humanity. Expect a Mains “**then vs now**” question. | Who / when | What (class) | |:---|:---| | **Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR), 1957** | **Sputnik** — first artificial satellite. US President: “just one small ball in the air.” Optics = nationalism. | | USSR | First **man** in space — **Yuri Gagarin** (audio: “Gaginam”) | | USSR | First **woman** — **Valentina Tereshkova** | | USSR | **Laika** — street dog, not a trained space dog; **not brought back** (planned sacrifice). Books / films later. | | **John F. Kennedy (JFK)** | Moon not because it is easy — because it is **hard**. Finish line shifted after USSR’s early wins. | | **16 July 1969** | **Apollo 11** lifts off | | **20 July 1969** | **Man on Moon** (“one small step…”) | | **1972 · Apollo 17** | **Abrupt end.** USSR did not contest the lunar finish line. NASA later: **>60%** of budget on a mission not justified by human value. Then **five decades** with **no** human lunar landing. | **Apollo** = Greek sun god. Isolated / **separate** missions — each crew had its own objectives. **Sputnik** as a symbol: Russia named its Covid vaccine **Sputnik**.
---

sections.heading: 8. Space Race 2.0 / Lunar Race — Artemis, ILRS, India (ST-04-08)
sections.content:
**2015:** China announces a **human-to-Moon** goal. Next year, Trump government: we go **first**. **Space Race 2.0** = **Lunar Race**. **Artemis** = **twin sister of Apollo** (Greek). Female name = **gender-inclusive** symbolism. | Mission | Class facts | |:---|:---| | **Artemis 1 (2022)** | **Unmanned.** **Orion** spacecraft: to the Moon, orbit, return. | | **Artemis 2 (1 April 2026)** | **Manned.** **No landing.** Orbit + return. **Farthest** humans have travelled (wider lunar loop than Apollo). Crew named in class: **Christina Koch** — first **woman** to the Moon (fly-by); **Victor Glover** — first **Black** man (US briefings repeated it until it felt token; Glover’s Earth-from-Moon clip: we see **Homo sapiens**, not races). | | **Artemis 3 / 4…** | **Humans on Moon by 2028** (US target — China said it would land **after** that year, so US is hurrying). | | **Base camp ~2032** | **Sustained human presence.** NASA Administrator (class: **Jared Eisenman**): not **“flags and footprints”** — **stay**. Crew landings every **six months** after Artemis 5; “America will never again give up the Moon.” | **Apollo vs Artemis (Mains hinge):** Apollo missions were **isolated**. Artemis is **additive** — each flight builds the next. **Why a lunar base (class order):** 1. **Research** — lunar atmosphere, soil, geology, helium, water (open-ended). 2. **Space tourism** (not yet for the Moon). 3. **Springboard to Mars** — the **main** reason. Lower gravity; use lunar **water → fuel**; then hop. **United States “Gateway”:** an orbital platform around the Moon was the original stepping stone (Earth → Gateway → surface). **Week before Artemis 2** they dropped the mediator — **direct landing**. Class: that is why Gateway was not taught as current US plan. **China (2031) + Russia → International Lunar Research Station (ILRS)** — could be an **orbital platform** *or* a **surface base camp**. Still waiting. Goal: same — **sustained human presence**. **India is not a participant in the race.** Write that **categorically** in answers. **Vikram Sarabhai** (father of the Indian space programme): invest in space only for **national development**, not power or prestige = **Sarabhai Doctrine**. India has still **walked ahead** of a pure-development reading — **humans to the Moon** is a goal (sheet: **2040**). Practical brake: **Gaganyaan** not done; senior-scientist resignation / delays. Not racing is, for now, also a **compulsion** (we do not run that fast).
---

sections.heading: 9. “House in space” — space station (started; unfinished) (ST-04-09)
sections.content:
After the Moon, the next prestige target was **who builds a house in space first**. No land to buy — make it **orbit**.

**Space station / orbital platform** = platform for **sustained human presence** in space. Also a **research** platform. Tourism was not the 1970s reason.

**Prelims trap (class wrote a four-option question):** valuable because of (1) **zero gravity** (2) **weightlessness** (3) **high-frequency radiation**.

| Claim | Verdict |
|:---|:---|
| **Zero gravity** | **Wrong.** If gravity were zero the station would **escape** Earth. Gravity is what **binds** it. You get **microgravity** — very small, **not zero**. Gravity falls with distance. |
| **Weightlessness** | **Correct.** Station is in **continuous free fall**. Weight is felt as the **recoil** of a surface. No platform “pushing back” → no weight. ISS has been “falling” for **over two decades** without hitting Earth because **orbital velocity** makes the **curve of fall parallel to Earth’s curve**. |
| **High-frequency radiation** (ultraviolet (UV), X-rays, …) | **Correct.** Outside the atmosphere those frequencies are **accessible**. |

**Orbital-velocity recap (Newton’s tower):** throw harder → land farther; give the **specific** velocity → you keep “falling around” the planet. Velocity is a **vector**; gravity still pulls; the path is curved **because** of gravity.

**National stations (class paused here):**

- **United States — Skylab**
- **USSR — Mir** (audio: “Neel”)

Leave page-space. Next lecture: why they later **shared** a station (International Space Station), and why this is Mains-relevant for the next two years.

sections.heading: Prelims traps (class)
sections.content:
- **Karman = 100 km**; **NASA / US ≈ 80 km** — not a brick wall.
- **OST 1967 is non-binding.** No sovereign claim; no mili-base on celestial bodies — **moral**, not a police force.
- **EOS ⊂ remote sensing**; Chandrayaan is RS, **not** an Earth-observation sat.
- Satellites do **not** stay up by burning fuel. Fuel = start + raise/lower + **CAM**.
- **Three** sats at **35,786 km** (equilateral, same orbit) → global cover.
- Space station ≠ **zero gravity**. **Microgravity + weightlessness + radiation.**
- **Rohini sounding rockets ≠ Rohini satellites.**
- **BT** in BT cotton **≠** the word biotechnology.

Nuclear technology still sits on **three** processes: **radioactivity** (last class), **nuclear fission**, **nuclear fusion**. Today finishes **particle / anti-particle**, then fission–fusion, fuels, enrichment, and the reactor (minus moderator).

---

sections.heading: 1. Particle and anti-particle (ST-06-01)
sections.content:
Every type of particle has a corresponding **anti-particle**.

| Particle | Anti-particle |
|:---|:---|
| Proton | Antiproton |
| Neutron | Antineutron |
| Electron | **Positron** |

**Similar masses, opposite charges** (if the particle has a charge). Proton +, antiproton −. Electron −, positron +. **Neutron is electrically neutral → antineutron is also electrically neutral.**

**Annihilation:** particle + its anti-particle meet → they **destroy each other**. Mass converts to **energy as photons**. Class: this is **mass → energy**.

**Pair production:** **high-energy photons** can produce a particle **and** its anti-particle. Class: this is **energy → mass**. Needs a system / infrastructure — commercially costly.

**Anti-hydrogen (class picture):** ordinary hydrogen = **one proton** in the nucleus + **one electron**. Anti-hydrogen = **antiproton** (negative nucleus) surrounded by a **positron**. Hydrogen + anti-hydrogen → energy.

**Matter–antimatter puzzle:** if all matter came from energy, energy should make a **pair** (matter + antimatter) → roughly **equal** antimatter. Scientists have **not** found that equal amount. Class: a paradox / puzzle in the theory.

**Utility — far future, not near.** Antimatter would be an **unparalleled** energy source because **all** the mass converts (fission / fusion convert only a **tiny** mass). Class scale: **less than a gram** could send a spaceship **Earth → Moon**; a **few grams** toward distant planets. **Not commercially viable now:** infrastructure huge; **more than 60 trillion dollars** to generate **1 gram**. **CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC)** has made a **tiny** amount — class: **1 nanogram** (**10⁻⁹ g**). Scaling that infrastructure to **1 gram** would take **billions of years**.

---

sections.heading: 2. Four fundamental forces — match table (ST-06-02)
sections.content:
Last class named the bosons. Today: **what each force does**, **range**, **relative strength** (descending). Prelims have asked **which is the weakest**.

| Force | What it does (class) | Force-carrying particle | Range | Relative strength |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Strong nuclear** | Binds the **nucleus** (quarks) together | **Gluon** | **Short** | **Strongest** |
| **Electromagnetic** | Acts between **charged** particles | **Photon** | **Infinite** | 2nd |
| **Weak nuclear** | Governs **particle decay** (radioactive decay) | **W and Z bosons** | **Short** | 3rd |
| **Gravitational** | Acts between objects with **mass** | **Graviton** (**not yet discovered**) | **Infinite** | **Weakest** |

**Order of strength:** strong > electromagnetic > weak > gravity.

---

sections.heading: Fission
sections.content:
**Nuclear fission** is the **energetic splitting** of **large** atoms such as **uranium** or **plutonium** into **two smaller atoms**, called **fission products**.

- **Uranium** atomic number **92** (92 protons). **Plutonium** **94**.  
- Hit the large atom with a **neutron** → splits + **energy** + **more neutrons**. Those neutrons split nearby atoms → **self-sustaining chain reaction**. Initiate once; then it runs.  
- Neutrons rise **exponentially**. If **uncontrolled**, all fuel is consumed in a **short** time → **accumulated** energy = **explosion** = **atom bomb**.  
- **Nuclear reactor** uses the **same reaction** but **controlled**: **extended** release, fuel consumed slowly. Control the **neutron population**. Extra neutrons absorbed by **control rods** (**boron** / **cadmium** — §7).  
- Smaller atoms = **radioactive nuclear waste** (must be discarded). Class named barium / krypton then said **do not write them** — not a physics paper.  
- **All commercial nuclear power plants presently in operation** (India and the world) are based on **fission**. Fusion is **not** commercialised **anywhere**.

**Bomb vs reactor** = **uncontrolled vs controlled** fission. Same reaction.

sections.heading: Fusion
sections.content:
**Nuclear fusion** is the **combining** of **two small** atoms (e.g. **hydrogen**) to produce a **heavier** atom (e.g. **helium**) **along with** energy.

- Only under **extremely high temperature and pressure**. Class: **millions** of °C — **not** 100,000 °C. **Not** naturally on Earth (surface or interior).  
- Natural home: **core of the Sun and other stars**. Sun **surface ~6,000 °C**; **core ~15 million °C** + huge pressure from mass. Core: **hydrogen → helium**. **Source of energy of the Sun and stars = fusion.**  
- **Fusion releases more energy than fission for the same amount of mass**, **without producing radioactive by-products**. Major by-product **helium** = inert, non-toxic, **not** a greenhouse gas. Fuel story: **hydrogen** from **water** → nearly **limitless**, **low-pollution**.  
- **Not commercially developed**, but **serious research worldwide** for that reason.

**Status on Earth:** fusion **can** be conducted in experimental reactors (must **supply electricity** from outside to make the conditions). **Not commercial** because **efficiency = output power / input power is less than 1** — the machine **eats more power than it gives**. Viable only when efficiency **> 1**. Class: reactors have reached temperatures **5–7×** the Sun’s core (**~75 million °C** and more).

**Named experiments (class):** China’s **EAST** reactor, nicknamed **artificial sun**; South Korea **K-STAR**. **ITER** = **International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor** — **33 nations including India**, experimental fusion reactor being built in **France**. Class: among the most expensive science experiments; **technological goal = efficiency 10** (**50 MW** in → **500 MW** out). Tokamak / 7 members / tritium-breeding **detail 14 Sep** → `06_Moderator_Reactors_and_Three_Stage_Programme.md` (**ST-08**).

sections.heading: 4. Source of the energy — Einstein (ST-06-04)
sections.content:
In fission **and** fusion a **certain amount of mass (m)** converts to **energy (E)** by **Einstein’s formula E = mc²**.

- **c** = speed of light = a **very large** number = **3 × 10⁸ m/s**.  
- **c² = 9 × 10¹⁶** → even a **tiny** mass gives **huge** energy.  
- Class contrast: particle / anti-particle convert **all** mass → even larger potential than fission / fusion.

---

sections.heading: 5. Fuels for nuclear fission (ST-06-05)
sections.content:
**Naturally occurring uranium** (mined) is **always a mix of two isotopes:** **Uranium-235 (U-235)** and **Uranium-238 (U-238)**.

| | **Thorium-232** | **U-233** | **U-235** | **U-238** | **Plutonium-239** |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Notation (sheet) | **²³²₉₀Th** | **²³³₉₂U** | **²³⁵₉₂U** | **²³⁸₉₂U** | **²³⁹₉₄Pu** |
| Found | Naturally | **Artificial** | Naturally (**0.7%** of natural U) | Naturally (**99.3%** — abundant) | **Artificial** — **not found naturally** |
| Fissile? | **No** — **fertile** | **Yes — fissile** | **Yes — fissile** | **No** — **fertile** | **Yes — fissile** |

**Fissile** = can undergo nuclear fission = **fuel**. Class fuels: **U-235, U-233, Pu-239**.  
**Fertile** = **cannot** start fission, but inside a reactor it **absorbs neutrons** and **transmutes** into a fissile isotope. Analogy: **wet wood** — you cannot start a fire with it; put it on a fire already going and it dries and burns.

**U-238:** non-fissile, **not** a fuel by itself. Beside **U-235** fission it absorbs neutrons → eventually **Pu-239** (fissile). Curiosity (class: **not required for the exam**): U-238 + n → **U-239** (unstable) → **β** → **Neptunium-239** (Z **93**) → **β** → **Pu-239** (Z **94**). Intermediates have their own half-lives.

**Plutonium:** **not found naturally anywhere**. No country has “plutonium mines.” Whatever Pu a country has, it **derived** from **U-238**. **Uranium is the last naturally occurring element (Z = 92).** Beyond 92, discovered elements (**118** in the L09 count) are **artificial**. Pu **Z = 94** → must be artificial.

**India and uranium:** **not enough** reserves; **largely import-dependent**. Class: **Kazakhstan** = **top exporter**; **Canada** = **largest reserves**; **Australia** also rich.

**Thorium-232 — special for India.** India has **one of the largest** (class: some estimates **the largest**) **thorium** reserves. Found on the **eastern and southern coasts** in **monazite sand**, which also holds **other rare-earth minerals**. **Non-fissile, fertile** → absorbs neutrons → **U-233** (fissile, artificial). **Cannot start** the programme on thorium alone: need a running fission (imported **uranium**) beside the thorium; later, enough **U-233** can fuel reactors. That is why India **still imports uranium** despite rich thorium.

---

sections.heading: 6. Enrichment of uranium and downblending (ST-06-06)
sections.content:
**Enrichment** = increasing the **concentration of U-235** (the fissile isotope) in natural uranium fuel, by **removing U-238**. Makes the fuel **more efficient**. Done in a **centrifuge**.

| Use | Class lock |
|:---|:---|
| **Peaceful** (electricity) | **3–5%** U-235 is **usually enough** |
| **Nuclear weapons** | Enrichment **more than 90%** |
| **Highly Enriched Uranium (HEU)** | Beyond **20%**. Around **80–90%+** class called **bomb-grade** |
| **Iran (class current-affairs hook)** | Found enriching **beyond 60%** — signal that the path is **weapons**, not power. **Centrifuge** is the threat; a power **reactor** using low enrichment is not. |

**Centrifuge:** uranium first **gasified**. Machine rotates very fast; **heavier U-238** (~**1% heavier** than U-235) goes to the **edge** and is removed. Class: **50,000–80,000 rotations per minute (RPM)**; needs alloys / technical expertise.

**Downblending** = **reverse of enrichment**. Mix **HEU** with **natural uranium** to **bring U-235 down** (class: to **less than 5%**) so it is **not** bomb-usable, only reactor fuel. Class: US proposed Iran **downblend under International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)** oversight; talks did not land. **Low Enriched Uranium (LEU)** = the product of that bring-down.

---

sections.heading: 7. Nuclear reactor — what it is; how it makes electricity (ST-06-07)
sections.content:
A **nuclear reactor** is a system that **contains and controls sustained nuclear chain reactions**.

**Uses (class):** generating **electricity**; moving **aircraft carriers** and **submarines**; producing **radioactive isotopes**; **research**.

**Electricity path (same idea as a thermal plant):** nuclear fission → **heat** → converts **water** to **steam** → steam **rotates a turbine** coupled to a **generator** → electricity.

sections.heading: Main components
sections.content:
**1. Core**  
Main area. Contains **all the fuel**, placed inside **fuel rods** (generally **zirconium** — high melting point, low reactivity). Pellets in cylindrical rods; **hundreds / thousands** of rods; **not** refuelled daily — months. **Fission happens here; all the heat is generated here.** **Control systems** also sit in the core.

**2. Coolant**  
A **fluid** that **captures heat** in the core and **transfers** it so water can become steam. Also **cools** the core — without it the core **overheats / melts**. Common coolants: **plain water (H₂O)**, **heavy water (D₂O)**, **liquid sodium**. Liquid sodium flows **in pipes** and does **not** contact the steam.

**3. Control rods**  
Rate of fission **depends on neutron population**. Rods **absorb neutrons** to control that rate. Materials with a **very good ability to absorb neutrons**: **boron** and **cadmium**.

| Want | Do |
|:---|:---|
| **Shut down** | Drop **all** rods in → absorb neutrons → reaction **halts** |
| **Steady power** | Hold a **steady** neutron population |
| **More power** | **Pull rods out** → neutron population rises |

**4. Moderator** — taught 12 Sep. Graphite / D₂O / beryllium; good moderator **must not absorb**; **Pu-239 reactors need none**. Full write-up: `06_Moderator_Reactors_and_Three_Stage_Programme.md` (**ST-07**). Do not treat this 10 Sep file as the PHWR / three-stage class.

---
